title: Discounting
detail: F03 · Lesson 3 · Financial Mathematics and the Time Value of Money
terms: Reverse the growth calculation to express a future payment in today’s terms. A higher positive discount rate reduces the present value of a fixed receipt. Choose a single valuation date A promised €1,000 in three years and €1,000 today carry the same printed amount but different spending dates. Present value finds the amount at the valuation date that, invested at a suitable rate, produces the promised future payment. This allows a choice between genuinely comparable alternatives. The valuation date need not be today. If asked for value one year from now, bring earlier cash forward and later cash backward to that particular date. Under consistent rates and assumptions, ranking at a common future date and ranking at today’s date will agree. Mixing amounts from different dates in one sum breaks that consistency. Rates, risk and promised amounts A one-period discount factor is the current price of one unit at the future date under the applicable assumptions. Discounting a certain cash amount at a rate reflecting its currency and horizon is straightforward. A risky promise requires a coherent treatment of default or uncertainty. A risky promised bond payoff is different from its expected payoff after default. For a deliberately simple exercise, if a risk-neutral valuation with a stated risk-free rate is appropriate, average state payments under the given pricing probabilities and discount that expectation. In other problems a risk-adjusted rate is explicitly supplied for expected cash. Avoid deducting the same risk from the cash flow and then applying an arbitrary extra penalty without a consistent model. What a change in rates does A distant fixed receipt is divided by the growth factor more times than a near receipt. Raising a positive discount rate lowers both present values, with a larger proportional impact on the later payment under a common proportional change in the discount factor. This relationship underlies the sensitivity of long-dated promises. The discount rate can in principle be negative. When r is between −1 and zero, the denominator 1+r is below one and a certain future receipt discounted using that rate has a higher present value than its face amount. Familiar inequalities about positive rates must therefore be stated with their assumptions. Move all cash to the same date A choice of sale terms

title: Quoted and effective rates
detail: F03 · Lesson 4 · Financial Mathematics and the Time Value of Money
terms: A nominal annual quote compounded monthly produces a different effective annual rate. Convert the cash-flow frequency and rate to matching periods. A stated annual number is not always annual growth A deposit quotes a nominal annual rate j convertible m times per year. The prescribed periodic rate is j/m, and the account earns it m times. Its effective annual factor is therefore (1+j/m)ᵐ. Write the label alongside the number to differentiate it from an effective annual rate, which directly states the actual one-year growth. For a given positive nominal rate, more frequent compounding produces higher annual growth if interest is reinvested. Comparing two contracts using their nominal numbers alone can rank them incorrectly. Accounts charging mandatory fees or making different payment schedules warrant a cash-flow comparison, since equal interest conventions do not guarantee equal consumer costs. Convert without counting interest twice An effective annual rate i contains its compounding already. The equivalent monthly rate is (1+i)^(1/12) − 1, not i/12. The growth factors should satisfy (1+r_month)¹² = 1+i. When changing from annual to quarterly effective rates, take a fourth root for exactly the same reason. For a nominal monthly-compounding quote, a quarter spans three successive monthly periods. Its effective growth is (1+j/12)³ − 1. Taking a quarterly rate four times reproduces the effective annual factor. Pick one representation and remain consistent with the payment dates when discounting or calculating instalments. Continuous compounding as a limiting quote Some financial models quote a continuously compounded annual rate c. Its one-year growth factor is exp(c), and its equivalent effective rate is exp(c) − 1. Conversely c = ln(1+i), where ln is the natural logarithm. This convention is useful because continuously compounded returns add across consecutive periods when defined on positive wealth ratios. All these expressions can describe exactly the same cash flows. The change of convention itself creates no extra income. A rise in an effective rate under a fixed nominal quote occurs because the contract actually credits interest more frequently. title: Annuities and perpetuities
detail: F03 · Lesson 5 · Financial Mathematics and the Time Value of Money
terms: Derive the value of repeated payments by adding a geometric series. Distinguish payments at the period start from payments at the end. Why the annuity formula works A sequence of n equal payments C at each period end is worth the sum C/(1+r) + C/(1+r)² + … + C/(1+r)ⁿ. Multiplying that sum by 1+r shifts every term one place forward. Subtracting the original sum cancels the internal terms and leaves C − C/(1+r)ⁿ. Rearranging gives present value = C × [1 − (1+r)^−n]/r for nonzero r. When r is zero the value is n × C. This derivation assumes a common effective rate per payment period. A staircase of different payments can be handled as separate ordinary cash flows or as blocks with matching dates. Timing, deferral and a final balance An annuity due pays at the beginning of each period. Moving every payment one period earlier multiplies its present value by 1+r. For a deferred annuity, first value the ordinary sequence one period before its first payment and then discount that intermediate value back to the chosen valuation date. A final balloon is a separate payment added to the final instalment on its stated date. Mixing the balloon into every instalment would overstate the liability. A common exam technique is to label the valuation date, the date of the first regular instalment, and the date of the final extra balance. A growing stream and its limit A perpetuity promises payments forever. With a constant first payment C₁ one period from now and no growth, its value C₁/r follows as the limit of the annuity formula for positive r. The value is finite because later cash flows are progressively discounted to very small present amounts. If payments grow at a constant rate g from the first future payment, the ratio of consecutive discounted terms is (1+g)/(1+r). When r exceeds g under the usual positive-factor assumptions, the sum converges to C₁/(r−g). Very small differences between r and g make the value highly sensitive. Replacing C₁ with an earlier historical payment misses one period of growth. Choose an annuity date Deferred maintenance receipts

title: Loan amortization
detail: F03 · Lesson 6 · Financial Mathematics and the Time Value of Money
terms: Each instalment combines interest on outstanding principal with repayment. Only the principal portion reduces the borrower’s balance. Derive the level instalment A fully amortizing loan ends with zero outstanding principal after the last scheduled payment. At origination, the amount borrowed equals the discounted value of its promised payments when the contractual rate is used and fees are absent. The relation makes a fixed instalment a direct application of the ordinary annuity formula. If principal is P, rate per period is r, and n equal payments A fall at period-end, then P = A × [1 − (1+r)^−n]/r. Rearrange to get A = P × r/[1 − (1+r)^−n]. A zero-interest loan simply divides principal evenly across the scheduled payments. Two ways to find the balance The retrospective approach starts at origination, accumulates interest, subtracts payments and carries the outstanding balance forward. Immediately after payment k, the prospective approach values the remaining n−k promised payments at the contractual rate. With correct timing, both procedures give identical balances. This equivalence helps detect errors in loan models. A balance immediately before a payment includes accrued interest and that payment is still due. A balance immediately afterward excludes it. An early settlement amount can differ from either scheduled balance if fees, contractual penalties or interest through a later settlement date apply. Unequal principal paths Level instalments differ from equal-principal repayment. With equal principal, each period retires P/n and pays interest on what remains, so total instalments usually decline at a positive rate. An interest-only period retires no principal, and a final balloon can remain even after many interest payments. Compare affordability as well as lifetime interest. A long maturity can reduce near-term instalments yet keep the balance outstanding longer. Calculate the period’s total charge and do not assume a low first payment implies a low overall cost. title: Inflation and real values
detail: F03 · Lesson 7 · Financial Mathematics and the Time Value of Money
terms: Separate growth in purchasing power from growth in money amounts. A nominal cash forecast needs a compatible nominal discount rate. Use a consistent purchasing-power unit Imagine a university scholarship rising 4% while rent and food rise 6%. The nominal scholarship is larger, yet a fixed basket of goods is harder to afford. To express an amount from date t in base-date purchasing power, divide it by the price index at t relative to the base index. A single consumer price index represents a specified basket, and different households may face different inflation. If a model assumes one general inflation rate, use it consistently for the relevant cash flows. A contract linked to a particular commodity or wage index can behave differently from a claim to general purchasing power. Connect nominal and real rates Let i be the effective nominal return, π inflation and r the realized real return over the same period. One unit of money grows to 1+i in currency and each basket costs 1+π times the previous price. The real growth factor is (1+i)/(1+π), so 1+i = (1+r)(1+π). The approximation r ≈ i−π omits the cross-product in the exact relation. The discrepancy is small for modest rates but can matter materially at high inflation. If inflation is unknown in advance, distinguish the real rate calculated using forecast inflation from the real return actually delivered after realized inflation is observed. Two ways to value an inflation-linked flow Suppose a future payment preserves fixed present purchasing power. Inflate it to its future cash amount and discount with a nominal rate, or leave it in base-date purchasing power and discount using the corresponding real rate. The two present values coincide if inflation and rates are deterministic, internally consistent and use the same timing. A fixed nominal payment does not promise fixed real value. When inflation changes after a fixed-rate contract is signed, the borrower’s and lender’s purchasing-power outcomes change. To evaluate an indexed contract, read the base date, lag, cap and index. title: Investment criteria
detail: F03 · Lesson 8 · Financial Mathematics and the Time Value of Money
terms: Net present value subtracts investment cost from discounted benefits. Internal rate of return is the rate that makes that difference zero and can have multiple solutions. Translate the investment decision into cash A project that reports high accounting earnings may require substantial working capital before customers pay. Net present value uses the incremental cash flows caused by accepting rather than rejecting the project. Include replacement or salvage proceeds and the opportunity cost of resources already owned when they would be sacrificed. Write the counterfactual explicitly. Prior feasibility spending may be sunk and should not be counted again. A recovery of working capital at the end is a receipt only if that cash is genuinely released. Discount each cash flow at a rate consistent with its risk, dates and currency. A positive NPV means this cash-flow plan exceeds its opportunity cost under those assumptions. What the internal rate can and cannot do The internal rate of return is any rate making the NPV equal to zero. For one initial negative cash flow followed only by positive receipts, NPV usually falls as the positive discount rate rises and there is a unique economically relevant root when the sign changes across rates. This makes the IRR a useful threshold for a conventional project. Unconventional projects can change sign again when cleanup or decommissioning costs arrive. Their NPV can cross zero more than once. For example the cash pattern −100, +230, −132 has roots at 10% and 20% because substituting either rate gives zero. Between those values NPV has a different sign from some rates outside them. Use the NPV at the actual opportunity cost. Ranking projects that compete Two independent projects with positive NPVs can both add value if sufficient resources exist. Two mutually exclusive plans require choosing one. A high percentage return on a tiny outlay can produce less total value than a lower percentage return on a large investment. Compare NPVs or analyze the incremental cash flows of choosing the larger plan over the smaller. Payback period measures when cumulative cash recovers the initial outlay. It can reveal exposure to illiquidity, but ordinary undiscounted payback ignores the time value of money and all later receipts after the cutoff. When capital or capacity is limited, establish the actual feasible combinations rather than mechanically selecting the single highest IRR. title: Term-specific rates
detail: F03 · Lesson 9 · Financial Mathematics and the Time Value of Money
terms: Cash at different maturities may command different rates. Discount each dated payment using a compatible spot rate or discount factor. Prices by maturity Think of a discount factor Dₜ as the current price of receiving one unit at date t under a specified risk and currency basis. A strip of these factors values a known cash schedule without requiring all maturities to share one rate. For annual effective spot rate sₜ, Dₜ = 1/(1+sₜ)ᵗ. A two-year annual spot rate describes a two-year investment starting now at a single compound rate. It is different from the one-year interest rate that will actually be available next year. A coupon bond’s single yield to maturity is a summary rate reproducing its price and need not equal any particular rate on the spot curve. Recover an unknown discount factor Start with a short instrument paying only one known amount. Its price divided by payoff gives the factor to that date. A longer instrument has early coupons that can already be priced with previously inferred factors. Subtract their present values from its price and divide the remainder by the final cash payment. This stepwise recovery is called bootstrapping. It depends on comparable credit quality, currency, settlement and treatment of coupons. If one bond is riskier or materially less liquid, its price difference may include that effect. Then treating its price as pure evidence about time can produce a misleading curve. What an implied forward rate means A one-year forward rate from year one to year two can be inferred by comparing investing to year two directly with investing to year one and entering a contract today that fixes the reinvestment rate. With D₁ and D₂ on the same basis, the implied forward growth factor is D₁/D₂. That rate follows from current prices and the availability of equivalent trades. It is not a guaranteed prediction of the future spot rate available in a year. Risk compensation and market expectations can contribute to the current term structure. title: Replication and arbitrage
detail: F03 · Lesson 10 · Financial Mathematics and the Time Value of Money
terms: If two portfolios promise identical payments in every state, compare their prices. The argument requires that the replicating trades and financing are actually available. Match state by state Two claims with the same average payoff can have different values because their payments occur in different states of the world. A claim paying when resources are scarce can be especially valuable. In a replication argument, require identical payments in every relevant state at the same dates, after costs and contract conditions. A replicating portfolio combines traded instruments to deliver the same state-by-state payoffs as a target claim. If the portfolio and claim can both be bought or sold on the stated terms, persistent price differences allow a trade producing a certain gain. The law of one price compares payment patterns, not average returns or labels. Solve for the holdings With two possible future states, two traded assets with sufficiently different payoff patterns can often replicate a two-state claim. Assign weights x and y to the traded instruments. Write one equation per state equating the portfolio’s payoff to the claim’s payoff. Then price the portfolio by applying those weights to today’s traded prices. A negative weight represents short selling or borrowing. If the instrument cannot be shorted, the computed portfolio may be algebraically correct yet unavailable to the investor. When assets’ payoff patterns move in exactly the same proportion, the equations may not have a unique solution spanning every claim. This is a question about what can be traded, not about solving harder arithmetic. Construct the complete trade If the market price of a claim exceeds the cost of replication, sell the claim and buy its replica. If cheaper, reverse both positions. Show cash at inception and net payoffs at every later state. A gain today with zero later obligations, or zero cost today and nonnegative future payoffs with positive payoff in some state, meets common frictionless arbitrage definitions. title: Populations and samples
detail: F04 · Lesson 1 · Probability, Statistics and Inference
terms: Define the population that a claim concerns. A sample of current companies can omit failed firms and exaggerate historical performance. Define the quantity before collecting data A fund manager asks about the average return earned by investors in start-up funds. That sentence leaves open whether each investor, euro invested or fund gets one vote. It also leaves out the entry date and what happens when a fund closes. The estimand is the precise population quantity the study tries to learn. A sampling frame is the practical list from which observations can be selected. A register of currently open funds may be complete for that date yet unsuitable for estimating historical launch-cohort outcomes. Define eligibility as of the relevant start date and specify a terminal value for merged, liquidated or otherwise missing funds where evidence supports it. Sampling design changes interpretation A simple random sample gives every eligible unit the same chance of selection under the specified design. A stratified design samples separately within groups. If groups are represented in the sample at different rates from the population, use population shares to combine group means when estimating a population mean. A large convenience sample can give a very precise estimate of the wrong population. Respondents who voluntarily report performance may differ systematically from nonrespondents. Random-sampling standard errors capture variation from the sampling process under assumptions. They do not fix an unrepresentative frame or outcome-dependent nonresponse. Survival, missing endings and bounds A failed business can disappear from a commercial database before the analyst downloads the list. Excluding it is defensible for a claim explicitly about surviving businesses but can distort a claim about all original businesses. Obtain closure records or verified terminal proceeds before defining what loss corresponds to closure. When an outcome genuinely remains unknown, show a sensitivity range. If every missing unit has a plausible bounded outcome, calculate the target at the lower and upper bounds. This shows how strong a conclusion can be without inventing exact missing observations. title: Distributions
detail: F04 · Lesson 2 · Probability, Statistics and Inference
terms: A distribution describes both possible outcomes and their probabilities. Mean, median and quantiles answer different questions about its centre and tails. Describe the random quantity A record of late-payment days can be viewed as a list of observed values or as a model of future outcomes. An empirical distribution gives each observed item a weight, often 1/n. A theoretical probability distribution assigns weights according to a specified model. State which one you are using before interpreting frequency as a long-run probability. For a discrete variable the probabilities at all possible values sum to one. A cumulative distribution gives the probability of an outcome at or below a threshold. It answers whether a loss limit is exceeded and supports quantiles. For an ordered value x, P(X > x) = 1 − P(X ≤ x). Including equality matters when outcomes cluster at the limit. Center, dispersion and tail shape The mean reflects every observation’s size and can be pulled by a long tail. The median identifies a central position and resists one extreme replacement better. Two portfolios can share a median and have completely different average losses if one occasionally suffers exceptionally severe damage. The interquartile range is the difference between the 75th and 25th percentiles and emphasizes the central half of the distribution. A quantile locates an outcome threshold and says little about severity beyond it. Specify the sample quantile convention when the dataset is small because interpolation rules can differ across software. Compare loss distributions sensibly If losses are reported as positive numbers, a higher upper loss quantile means a more severe threshold. If returns are signed gains and losses, the bad tail is typically the lower return tail. Write down which convention the exercise uses before reading a chart. Otherwise conclusions can reverse simply because a minus sign was hidden. One useful comparison asks for expected loss conditional on crossing a specified threshold. This averages only the relevant tail outcomes, using probabilities rescaled within the tail. At a quantile with many tied outcomes, say whether the condition is strictly above or at or above the cutoff. These definitions can yield quite different numbers. title: Conditional probability
detail: F04 · Lesson 3 · Probability, Statistics and Inference
terms: Revise a probability when new evidence arrives. A useful warning indicator can still produce many false alarms if default is initially rare. Partition the evidence A bank sees a late payment and wants to know the chance of eventual default. One way to avoid reversing conditional probabilities is to build a table with actual default status as rows and warning status as columns. Each cell is a joint count or joint probability of both events occurring. For any events A and B with P(B) positive, P(A given B) = P(A and B)/P(B). Multiply a prior probability of A by P(B given A) to obtain the joint probability. Then divide by the overall probability of the evidence. That denominator must include all ways the evidence can arise, including warnings from customers who repay. Sensitivity, specificity and predictive value Sensitivity is the share of actual defaults flagged. Specificity is the share of nondefaults correctly left unflagged. The false-positive rate is one minus specificity. Positive predictive value measures the share of flagged cases that actually default. This fraction depends on prevalence, the underlying rate of default. Moving the same warning rule to a population with a different base rate can change its predictive value even if sensitivity and specificity stay stable. Predictive value can also change because customer behaviour shifts and the rule itself performs differently. Distinguish these mechanisms when interpreting a change in an alert dashboard. From updated probability to action A forecasted probability helps make a decision only together with the consequences of the alternatives. A manual review that costs €50 may be worthwhile if it can prevent a large expected loss. The same review may be wasteful for tiny accounts. State what the review would actually change, its effectiveness and whom its cost applies to. When several warnings are combined, their likelihoods can only be multiplied directly under suitable conditional independence assumptions. Two alerts derived from the same missed payment may add little information beyond the first. A joint count or a model of the second warning given both the first warning and default status is stronger evidence. Use natural frequencies Support tickets at an online lender

title: Expectation and variance
detail: F04 · Lesson 4 · Probability, Statistics and Inference
terms: Expected value averages possible outcomes using probabilities. Variance measures squared departures from that average and penalizes large moves more heavily. Build the distribution of money outcomes An insurer can list which payouts might occur and attach probabilities. Expected value is the weighted total, a long-run average under repeated comparable risks. A payout equal to the expectation need never occur. A policy paying either zero or €1,000 can have a mean of €100 even though nobody actually receives €100. Expectations add across exposures even when the exposures are dependent. If customer A’s expected loss is €8 and customer B’s €12, the total expected loss is €20. Dependence changes how losses cluster, and therefore changes variability and severe-tail outcomes, even when those individual expectations are fixed. Calculate variance two ways Variance is the expected squared difference between the outcome and its mean. A convenient equivalent calculation subtracts the square of the mean from the expected square of the outcome. Keeping both as separate lines helps avoid confusing the mean square with the squared mean. The standard deviation is the square root of the variance. If every outcome increases by a fixed €5, both the mean and every outcome shift equally. Deviations from the mean remain the same, so variance does not change. Multiplying every outcome by three multiplies each deviation by three and its square by nine. Standard deviation triples while variance increases ninefold. Risk measures depend on the use Squared deviations treat unusually large gains and losses symmetrically. A firm with a hard minimum cash requirement may care specifically about the probability of falling below it and the size of shortfalls. Two projects with equal mean and variance can still have different downside profiles. Inspect the actual states when a covenant or funding deadline matters. A theoretical probability variance uses the supplied probabilities. For an observed random sample used to estimate population variance, a common unbiased estimator of population variance under independent identically distributed sampling divides the sum of squared sample deviations by n−1. Be clear whether probabilities are fully specified or estimated from a sample. Compute and test an expectation A producer’s variable royalty

title: Covariance and correlation
detail: F04 · Lesson 5 · Probability, Statistics and Inference
terms: Two exposures can offset when they move differently. Covariance carries units, while correlation standardizes the strength of their linear co-movement. Co-movement relative to each average Suppose the same weather shock helps a cold-drink seller and hurts a hot-drink seller. To measure their joint movements, subtract each seller’s own expected profit in each state, multiply the two deviations and average these products using the state probabilities. This produces their covariance. When both deviations tend to share a sign, positive products dominate. Covariance depends on units, so measuring one account in cents instead of euros changes the numerical value. Correlation divides covariance by the two standard deviations, cancelling unit scaling when both are positive. It describes linear co-movement and does not establish causality. Derive a portfolio’s variance A weighted portfolio return is w times return A plus (1−w) times return B. Its deviation from the portfolio mean is the weighted sum of the two deviations. Squaring that sum produces the two weighted squared terms plus twice their product. Taking expectations gives the portfolio variance formula. In symbols, variance = w²σA² + (1−w)²σB² + 2w(1−w)ρσAσB. Here σ denotes standard deviation and ρ correlation. This shows why portfolio variance cannot be calculated as a simple weighted average of the two individual variances. The joint behaviour term can add risk or offset it. Limits of the diversification argument For a fixed pair of long positions and given individual volatilities, a lower correlation reduces the portfolio variance. Perfect negative correlation can remove all variability with a suitable choice of weights, but equal weights work exactly only when the weighted magnitudes of the two movements match. With unequal risks the hedge ratio must change. A sample correlation from ordinary times can change in a crisis. Zero correlation says linear co-movement is absent in the data or model. Nonlinear dependence can remain. A bank depending on the same source of emergency funding for both positions can face a joint risk that past price correlation alone misses. title: Sampling distributions
detail: F04 · Lesson 6 · Probability, Statistics and Inference
terms: Estimates change across samples. The standard error measures variation of an estimator under its sampling assumptions. Sampling a mean repeatedly Suppose a warehouse manager randomly chooses 25 invoices each week to estimate mean payment delay. Individual delays vary for many reasons. The sample mean also varies between random samples because each contains a different mix of delays. The distribution of those estimated means is the sampling distribution of the estimator. A sampling distribution is a conceptual tool even when only one sample is observed. Its standard deviation is the standard error. A standard error expresses precision of the estimated mean, not the spread of delays an individual future invoice might experience. Predicting one invoice generally requires allowing for individual variability in addition to uncertainty about the mean. Why the square root appears For independent observations with common variance σ², the variance of their sum is nσ². Dividing their sum by n to form an average divides variance by n², leaving σ²/n. Taking the square root gives σ/√n. In practice s, the sample standard deviation, often replaces the unknown population σ. Quadrupling independent sample size therefore halves the estimated standard error if the underlying spread is unchanged. A few high-variance observations can keep estimates imprecise despite a large headcount. Increasing n does not cure systematic measurement errors, missing units or an estimator that targets a different quantity from the requested one. When independence fails Successive months from the same shop may have correlated sales because one contract affects several months. The variance of a sum then includes pairwise covariance terms in addition to individual variances. Positive covariance can make observations provide less independent information than the simple count suggests. The central limit theorem can justify a roughly normal distribution for averages under suitable conditions such as independent observations with finite variance and adequate sample size. Strong dependence, heavy tails or very small samples can undermine that approximation. There is no universal sample threshold that makes all designs reliable. title: Confidence intervals
detail: F04 · Lesson 7 · Probability, Statistics and Inference
terms: Connect an estimate with a range produced by a repeated-sampling procedure. An imprecise estimate can include economically important gains and losses. From estimation error to a range A point estimate can be close to the true mean or far away in any one sample. A confidence procedure chooses a margin using a model of the estimator’s variation. For an approximate two-sided 95% normal interval, use estimate ± 1.96 times its standard error. The multiplier controls how much of the reference distribution is included. When observations are independent and normally distributed but their variance is estimated from the same small sample, a Student t multiplier with n−1 degrees of freedom is appropriate for the population mean. Its wider tails allow extra uncertainty. Use any critical value supplied in a question and state the population or design assumptions. Interpret confidence after observing data The confidence level describes the repeated-sampling performance of the procedure. Imagine repeating the entire design many times and constructing a new interval each time. Under the model, roughly the stated proportion cover the fixed true parameter. The endpoints in this particular observed sample have already been calculated. An interval containing zero for an incremental profit effect is compatible with no effect and potentially meaningful gains or losses. This does not demonstrate that the effect is exactly zero. Conversely, a tightly estimated small positive effect may rule out zero yet have little economic significance after implementation costs. Construct the right interval for a difference If the same companies are observed before and after a policy, form a difference for each company. A confidence interval for the mean of those paired changes uses the standard deviation of the differences. Treating before and after as unrelated groups throws away the pairing and can misstate uncertainty. For independent groups, the estimated standard error of their difference can be formed by adding their separate estimated variances of means and taking a square root. That calculation assumes independent groups. Within-company pairs require the covariance between pre- and post-values. Always specify which observations are independent sampling units. title: Tests and multiple comparisons
detail: F04 · Lesson 8 · Probability, Statistics and Inference
terms: Compare an observed result with a null model. Testing many rules increases the chance that an apparently striking result occurs by luck. Construct a null comparison A trading team estimates whether a signal improves average returns after costs. Before looking at results, state the null value and the alternative. The null might specify zero mean improvement. A two-sided alternative allows both gains and losses. The test statistic measures the observed deviation from the null in standard-error units. Under suitable conditions z = (estimate − null)/standard error can use a standard normal reference. A two-sided p-value is the probability under the null model of a statistic at least as extreme in either direction. Choosing one-sided testing only after learning the sign wrongly changes the question and invalidates the nominal error rate. False alarms versus missed effects A Type I error rejects a true null. The significance level sets its probability under the specified testing procedure and assumptions. A Type II error fails to reject a false null at a particular alternative. Power is one minus that error probability. Low precision or a small true effect can leave a study with low power. Reducing the rejection threshold can reduce false positives while making a real effect harder to detect at fixed sample size. A p-value is not the probability the hypothesis is false, nor the probability the strategy will make money next year. Profitability also depends on effect size, fees, capacity, implementation and stability beyond the sample. Searching many ideas Testing twenty rules and announcing only the best makes selection part of the experiment. For m independent tests of true nulls at level α, the chance of at least one false rejection is 1−(1−α)ᵐ. This number can be much larger than α. Dependence changes the exact family probability. A simple conservative procedure sets each test’s cutoff to α/m, the Bonferroni rule. It controls the probability of one or more false rejections at most α even without independence when the individual p-values are valid. title: Regression
detail: F04 · Lesson 9 · Probability, Statistics and Inference
terms: Fit a line by minimizing squared errors. Interpret slope, intercept and residual in the units of the underlying data. Construct a line from observations A line predicting revenue from transactions has form ŷ = a + bx. Here x is the recorded input, ŷ the fitted outcome, a the intercept and b the change in fitted outcome per unit increase in x. A residual for observation i is yᵢ − ŷᵢ. It describes the observed departure from the fitted line. Ordinary least squares chooses a and b to minimize the sum of squared residuals. With an intercept and nonconstant x, the fitted line passes through the point given by the sample means. The slope equals the sum of cross-products of centered x and y divided by the sum of squared centered x. Thus unusually distant x values can strongly affect the slope. What a slope tells an analyst A slope of €3 per transaction says the fitted revenue difference for two observed transaction counts differing by one is €3, under the estimated linear relationship. It does not establish that forcing another transaction would generate exactly that amount. Transaction size, customer type or season can move both recorded variables. The intercept is the fitted outcome at x = 0. It can be economically meaningful for a fee structure with a fixed charge, or pure extrapolation if no observation has x near zero. A fitted relationship estimated on small shops may not continue linearly for a nationwide chain. Express both numerical change and the range of data supporting it. Look beyond a good fit The coefficient of determination R² measures the proportion of sample variation around the outcome mean explained by the fitted model with an intercept. Compute it as 1 − residual sum of squares / total sum of squares. It is a descriptive measure of in-sample fit, not a causal test or guarantee of future forecasting accuracy. Inspect residuals by fitted value, time and group. A curved pattern challenges the linear shape. A fan-shaped pattern signals changing variability. A single extreme observation can drive a high correlation. Examine whether its records are erroneous or structurally different before deciding whether exclusion is defensible. title: Confounding and dependence
detail: F04 · Lesson 10 · Probability, Statistics and Inference
terms: A common driver can produce an association without a direct causal effect. Serial dependence can make naive standard errors too small. A comparison needs a counterfactual A bank compares the profits of firms receiving loans with those denied loans. The financed firms may have been stronger even before the loan. A causal effect asks how the same firms would have performed under different financing. Only one of those outcomes is observed, so identifying a credible comparison group requires an argument. Confounding occurs when a factor influences both treatment or exposure and the outcome. Baseline credit quality can affect both loan approval and future profits. Adjusting for measured pre-loan quality can improve comparability, but unmeasured customer demand or owner experience may remain. More data of the same selected type do not automatically remove that problem. Comparing changes across groups A differences-in-differences calculation subtracts the change in an untreated group from the change in a treated group. Its causal interpretation requires that, absent the treatment, their outcome trends would have been comparable. It also needs attention to simultaneous changes, shifting group composition and spillovers between groups. Plot multiple pre-treatment periods to see whether trends were different before the intervention. Similar pretrends strengthen plausibility but cannot prove the unobserved future counterfactual. If an unrelated factory closure affects only the comparison region at the same time, subtracting its decline could exaggerate the apparent treatment effect. Dependence changes standard errors Observations from the same company or month can share shocks. Even if a point estimate is calculated correctly, an independence-based standard error may be too small with positive within-group correlation. Block or cluster-aware procedures preserve such dependence under appropriate assumptions and need enough independent clusters to support inference. Distinguish bias from precision. Correcting standard errors for clustering changes estimated uncertainty and does not by itself remove omitted-variable bias. Adding a good control can help comparability and still leave correlated errors. A strong empirical design addresses both the credibility of the comparison and the way uncertainty is calculated. title: Model structure
detail: F05 · Lesson 1 · Financial Computing, Data and Reproducibility
terms: Separate source data, assumptions, calculations and outputs. A change to a single assumption should flow through the model consistently. Start from the decision and its units A lender asks how far an exporter’s sales can fall before cash runs short. Building a revenue chart immediately may look productive, but the question concerns available cash after dated collections and payments. Begin by naming the decision, required output, currency, frequency and reporting horizon. A clean model makes these choices visible. Distinguish an observed input, a chosen assumption, an intermediate calculation and a decision output. Last month’s invoiced units come from a system of record. Next month’s collection percentage is an assumption. Expected receipts are calculated. Whether a cash buffer is breached is the decision output. Each category needs a different source of verification. One direction of calculation Arrange the normal flow from records and assumptions through calculations to outputs. When a result is copied back into an assumption cell, subsequent calculations may quietly use a stale result. Circular logic occurs when an output feeds an input that determines the same output. Some financial equations legitimately need a simultaneous solution, but that dependence should be explicit. Write balances as opening amount plus inflows less outflows equals closing amount. Keep a stock such as month-end cash separate from a flow such as monthly sales. Adding twelve closing balances does not measure annual cash received. A total that is dimensionally implausible can reveal an architectural mistake before any formula is inspected. Scenarios are coherent sets of assumptions A downside case might combine slower customer payments with higher material costs. Store those changes together under a named assumption set while preserving the original observed history. Running the same calculation logic against each scenario makes output differences attributable to the changed assumptions. A sensitivity changes one or more defined inputs systematically to study how the output responds. A model should represent what happens when a threshold is crossed, such as a mandatory credit withdrawal. Testing only a small favorable change may hide a discontinuity. Identify which cash flows and contractual rules are outside your simplified model. Design a traceable cash model Cash required for a book fair

title: Spreadsheet references
detail: F05 · Lesson 2 · Financial Computing, Data and Reproducibility
terms: Use relative and absolute references to copy calculations across periods. Check a total in a second way to expose a shifted range. Understand how a copied reference moves A spreadsheet formula is written from a location. In C5, a reference to B5 points one column to the left in the same row. When copied down, that relative relationship stays the same. If a rate must always come from one fixed assumption, ordinary relative copying can silently direct later rows to an empty cell or another assumption. A dollar sign anchors the component it precedes. $B5 fixes column B but lets the row move. B$5 fixes row 5 but lets the column move. $B$5 fixes both. A mixed reference is especially useful when a row supplies rates and a column supplies exposures across a two-dimensional scenario table. Separate error detection from formatting A beautifully formatted matrix can contain a shifted range. Check corner cells by reasoning independently about the expected result, then examine the formulas at the first, middle and final positions. When rows are added within a fixed summation range, check whether the range expands. A blank separator row can break an assumed contiguous region. Reconcile totals another way. For exposures sharing one rate, sum the exposures and multiply once. If different rates apply, calculate each exposure times its own rate and sum those products, conceptually a weighted sum. A simple arithmetic average of rates multiplied by total exposure works only under suitable equal-weight or coincidental conditions. Types and signs are also inputs A displayed “5%” can be a numeric value of 0.05 formatted as a percentage or a text string imported from a report. Spreadsheets may coerce text in some functions and ignore it in others. Confirm numeric types and inspect the stored value before concluding a formula is wrong. Use one sign convention for receipts, expenses and balances, and label amounts in euros, thousands or millions. A reconciliation between a €2m statement and a 2,000 numeric input in thousands is legitimate only after conversion. Avoid rounding every intermediate value to the displayed decimals unless the contract requires it. Formatting a result and changing its stored precision are separate actions. title: Python fundamentals
detail: F05 · Lesson 3 · Financial Computing, Data and Reproducibility
terms: Write a short function with named inputs, a return value and tests. A zero price, a missing price and a zero return need different treatments. A function is a contract with its caller A function name such as simple_return suggests an operation, but callers also need to know the units, accepted input types, missing-data behaviour and output convention. A result of 0.05 can mean a decimal 5% return. Returning 5 instead silently scales the next portfolio calculation by a factor of 100. In Python, def introduces a named function, arguments supply values and return passes the result back to the caller. A variable defined inside it normally belongs to that call. A self-contained calculation that takes all inputs explicitly is easier to test than one that secretly reads whichever global currency or fee rate was last assigned. Guard clauses and explicit missing values For an introductory price-return function, assume valid beginning prices must be strictly positive and valid ending prices nonnegative. A verified end price of zero means total loss, while a missing end price means the result is unknown. Handling these cases separately avoids silently inventing a zero return on an unobserved position. In Python, None can represent an intentionally missing value under a documented contract. Some data libraries use distinct missing markers, such as NaN. NaN is unusual because comparisons with it can be surprising. Normalize missing representations when data enter your function, or use a library-aware missing check. Do not rely on a comparison with zero to detect missingness. Small calculations and executable checks A function can be tested with ordinary assertions, statements that fail if an expected condition is false. Use a normal gain, a loss, unchanged price, missing input and invalid starting price to test distinct behaviours. Checking solely that a function runs does not establish the numerical value is correct. Floating-point arithmetic represents many decimal fractions only approximately. An exact-equality check may fail for a mathematically correct 5% result. Use an agreed tolerance for calculated floating-point quantities, such as abs(actual−expected) < 0.000001. For currency posting systems, an explicit decimal type and contractual rounding policy may be more appropriate. Write a robust simple return A price feed with four instruments

title: Tabular operations
detail: F05 · Lesson 4 · Financial Computing, Data and Reproducibility
terms: Filter rows, group observations and calculate changes. Inspect the original rows contributing to a reported total. Decide what one row represents A payments table may contain one row per invoice, transfer, card authorization or settlement line. Calling every row a sale before establishing its grain can duplicate activity. A cancelled card authorization and its later replacement, for instance, do not necessarily represent two completed cash receipts. Record the key that identifies a transaction, the currency, the sign convention and which status indicates completion. Filtering a month by booking date can answer a different question from filtering by settlement date. State the operational event before counting records so a colleague can reproduce the same population. Aggregate correctly across currencies and weights A group-by operation partitions rows according to one or more keys, such as branch and currency, then calculates a summary within each group. Summing signed amounts gives net flow. Summing positive receipts separately from refunds gives gross inflow and outflow. A count of rows is different from a count of distinct customers or transaction IDs. A portfolio’s weighted rate is the sum of exposure times rate divided by total exposure. A simple mean of group averages generally misweights groups with different sizes. For currencies, translate at a specified rate and date before adding different units, or report distinct subtotals. Do not interpret a global total that adds euros and dollars directly. Changes need a coherent baseline A period-on-period percentage change is (new−old)/old under the usual base convention. If the old value is zero, this percentage is undefined even when the euro change is informative. With a negative starting value, a percentage change can be hard to interpret, so show the absolute movement and sign as well. Filtering before grouping can change denominators. Suppose only branches with sales in both months remain. This describes continuing branches and omits newly opened ones, whereas network growth includes them. title: SQL and joins
detail: F05 · Lesson 5 · Financial Computing, Data and Reproducibility
terms: Identify the keys that distinguish records. Joining two tables with repeated keys can silently multiply balances or transaction volumes. Keys describe an economic relationship Loans have facility IDs, borrowers have customer IDs and payments have transaction IDs. A facility may make many payments and one customer may own several facilities. Identify the tables’ grains before choosing a join. An account name typed differently in two source systems is a weak key even if the visible labels look similar. A primary key uniquely identifies a row in its table. A foreign key refers to a row in another table. For example many facilities can refer to one borrower. A borrower lookup intended to label facilities should contain at most one applicable borrower row per matching key at the date in question. What joins do to unmatched records An inner join returns matching pairs and drops rows lacking a match. A left join retains every row of the left-hand table and supplies missing right-hand fields when no match exists. Neither choice alone guarantees correct totals. An inner join can silently remove a facility whose borrower sector has not yet arrived. When a loan legitimately links to multiple collateral records, multiplying rows can be correct at collateral grain. Summing loan principal after that expansion still repeats amounts. Aggregate collateral to one per loan or report exposure from the facility table. SELECT DISTINCT can hide duplicates accidentally and can also delete different real rows sharing identical displayed amounts. Time is part of some keys A customer can move from one industry or risk band to another. A lookup with multiple historical rows per customer is valid, yet joining only on customer ID matches several eras simultaneously. Use the observation date with a nonoverlapping effective-date interval, commonly start ≤ date < end, to identify the correct record. Check for overlapping validity intervals and missing intervals for each entity. Assigning today’s sector or credit rating to an earlier decision can also leak later information into a historical analysis. The database relationship and the economic date definition must agree before aggregation. Protect a balance across a join Adding sectors to a loan book

title: Dates and time zones
detail: F05 · Lesson 6 · Financial Computing, Data and Reproducibility
terms: Distinguish order time, execution time, publication time and settlement. The date assigned to a record determines when a learner could have used it. Record at least two clocks A retailer reports December sales in a press release in February. December identifies the period to which the information relates. February identifies when an investor could first read the release. A trading model using those sales must look at availability, whereas an economic chart may legitimately group the value by its December reference period. An event can have order time, execution time, settlement date, official publication time, and actual system arrival time. A payment forecast may care about settlement while a historical strategy must respect both release and arrival if the data feed was delayed. Preserve the original timestamps and define the decision timestamp against which availability is tested. Offsets and exchange calendars A timestamp without an offset can be ambiguous, especially when clocks move back and the same local time appears twice. Store a time-zone-aware instant, typically also normalized to UTC, and the market time zone needed to assign trading sessions. A fixed offset does not necessarily hold over an entire year in markets observing daylight saving. A date in UTC can correspond to the next calendar day in Asia or the prior one in the Americas. A market holiday and an unexpected early close both change the next executable session. Use the stated exchange calendar or explicit exercise schedule. Calendar-day arithmetic alone cannot identify an executable auction time. Use point-in-time data Revised economic numbers can differ from first releases. A row may have one observation period and multiple published versions. At each historical decision, choose the most recent version actually available then, with a tie rule for records arriving exactly at the decision cutoff. This is often called an as-of selection. Look-ahead bias occurs when an analysis benefits from data impossible to know at the simulated time. The bias need not come from an obvious future return. An index constituent list determined later, a revised industry label or backfilled data vendor correction can supply future information just as easily. Reconstruct an information set A release between two closing auctions

title: Prices and returns
detail: F05 · Lesson 7 · Financial Computing, Data and Reproducibility
terms: Separate dividends, splits and currency conversion. Agree whether a series records price changes alone or total investor returns. Reconstruct an investor’s wealth The quoted closing price is a price per share, while the investor owns a number of shares and may receive cash distributions. Investor wealth can change because price moves, share count changes in a split, dividends arrive or the exchange rate changes. Begin with one shareholding and follow each component to the reporting date. A price return excludes cash dividends but should still account for splits when measuring an investor’s price performance. A total return includes distributions under the specified reinvestment assumption. If the data supplier’s adjusted series already embeds a dividend or split, applying the event again double counts it. Read the field definition and check a known event manually. Convert currencies as growth factors Suppose a home investor records the home-currency value of one foreign unit as e. Starting wealth in home currency equals starting foreign wealth times e₀. Ending wealth equals ending foreign wealth times e₁ when distributions are converted at the end in this simplified case. The home growth factor is local total-return factor times e₁/e₀. Adding local and currency percentage changes is only an approximation because their gains interact. If the exchange rate is quoted in the inverse direction, invert it before applying this rule. A dividend converted immediately at an earlier date uses its own exchange rate and cannot always be combined into a single end-date conversion. Chain a time series consistently Daily simple returns combine multiplicatively. For positive beginning and ending wealth, log return is the natural logarithm of the growth ratio. Log returns add over consecutive periods, while simple returns do not. Either representation must use a consistent total-versus-price basis, split treatment and currency throughout the chain. Large apparent losses on an ex-split date or gains around a data vendor transition deserve inspection against raw events. Distinguish a genuine price move from a change in instrument identifier, quote currency or decimal scale. Maintain both raw event data and calculated adjustments so the claimed return can be reproduced. Audit a total return A foreign share splits

title: Missing observations
detail: F05 · Lesson 8 · Financial Computing, Data and Reproducibility
terms: Record why data are absent. Filling a market holiday and filling a suspended stock can imply very different economic assumptions. Missing is a statement about observation A missing value can mean the field does not apply, the event did not occur, a machine failed, trading was suspended, or the vendor has not delivered the record yet. These reasons lead to different economic conclusions. A valid zero amount means an observed value of zero. Record the reason separately from the numeric value. When missingness is related to performance, analysing only complete rows can bias an estimate. For example riskier issuers may stop reporting before failure. In contrast, if a random transmission failure is unrelated to prices after conditioning on known factors, the effect of complete-case analysis may differ. Explain the mechanism before choosing an imputation rule. What filling really assumes Forward filling carries the latest observed value ahead. It can be appropriate for a slowly changing descriptive label when the last definition genuinely remains in force. Applied to a suspended share, it produces a stale valuation mark and an apparent zero daily move. No buyer or seller has demonstrated that the mark is executable. Linear interpolation fills an intermediate point using both earlier and later observations. It may be reasonable for a retrospective chart under an explicit assumption, but it introduces future information into a real-time trading simulation. A zero fill makes the stronger claim that the unobserved outcome is exactly zero. Each operation answers a different question. Preserve the denominator and show sensitivity An equal-weight portfolio holding a missing asset has an unknown total return unless the missing return can be recovered or bounded. Renormalizing the remaining assets describes an observed-assets-only portfolio. Keeping the original weights and using zero assumes no change in the missing holding. Neither method simply reproduces the full portfolio without an assumption. A sensitivity analysis makes the uncertainty visible. Assign a credible low and high outcome to the missing position and pass both through the original portfolio weights. Report how much of the portfolio weight is affected and whether the key decision changes across those bounds. Preserve raw records so a later correction can replace the assumption. title: Tests and reconciliation
detail: F05 · Lesson 9 · Financial Computing, Data and Reproducibility
terms: Test positive and negative cases, check balances and compare a sample calculation with a second method before trusting a long pipeline. Tests answer different questions A function-level test gives a small component known inputs and checks expected outputs, such as a return of zero for unchanged known prices. An integration test checks several components together, for example loading raw transfers, attaching currency conversions and grouping by account. Either type can pass while the other fails. Reconciliation compares an output with an independent record or accounting identity. A second formula copied from the same erroneous cell offers limited independent evidence. Use a bank statement, a separate calculation from raw inputs, or balances recorded by a different process. If two systems share the same erroneous source, note the remaining common risk. Invariants and negative cases An invariant is a condition that must hold for all permitted inputs, such as closing cash equalling opening cash plus net posted movements. Other useful checks are unique transaction IDs where required, probabilities summing to one, weights matching net invested capital, or counterpart entries summing to zero for an internal transfer. A negative test deliberately supplies invalid input such as a missing currency, duplicated ID, zero starting price or date outside the reporting period. Choose whether the process should raise a clear error, quarantine the input, or use a documented missing result. A test that merely confirms the job did not crash leaves the most important outcome unchecked. Safe retries and tolerances A payment feed can send yesterday’s transactions again after a timeout. If reprocessing adds every record again, balances change even though the economic events are identical. An idempotent process produces the same final state when the same input is applied again. Stable transaction IDs and an explicit correction policy make this behaviour testable. When reconciling values, distinguish a permitted rounding tolerance from an unexplained economic difference. Currency rounded to cents per transaction can differ from rounding a net aggregate. State which the contract or statement uses. Maintain an exception list with IDs and amounts so allowed tolerances do not conceal repeated systematic differences. Design a small but sharp test set A ledger replay after a timeout

title: Reproducible research
detail: F05 · Lesson 10 · Financial Computing, Data and Reproducibility
terms: Preserve original data, code versions and transformations. A fresh run should reproduce both the numbers and the figures cited in the analysis. Reconstruct the number, then the claim A chart in an investment report depends on choices about the universe, the time window, the data vintage, the handling of corporate actions, the calculation, and the plotting specification. Reproducibility means someone with appropriate access can run the recorded procedure on the same inputs and recover the same results within a stated tolerance. Replication using a genuinely new sample or a different source asks a further question about robustness. An exact reproduction can succeed even when the original model has a conceptual error. Reproduction establishes traceability. Independent checks on theory, source quality and generalization remain necessary. Capture a point-in-time recipe Retain a read-only original extract or an exact versioned source reference, a checksum for identifying the bytes, acquisition date, schema and units, code revision and the parameters used. A checksum shows whether two inputs are identical at the byte level. It does not prove a series is correct or legitimately obtained. Record software and package versions and any relevant time-zone or calendar configuration. For stochastic simulations record generator type, seed and how observations were ordered before drawing. A fixed seed controls pseudorandom variation under the same algorithm, but it does not freeze a vendor feed, library changes, concurrency effects or financial assumptions. Separate revisions from reproduction failures A supplier may revise economic history after new filings arrive. Keep the archived run and treat the refreshed data as a new vintage. Comparing results side by side can reveal the effect of revisions. Replacing old inputs without a record makes it impossible to distinguish a deliberate update from a hidden change in methodology. Define the verification target before running. Check the selected IDs and row count, set a tolerance for numerical results, and verify that each chart agrees with the table built from the same totals. title: National income
detail: C01 · Lesson 1 · Open-Economy Macroeconomics and Monetary Systems
terms: Output can be spent at home or abroad. Derive the connection between national spending, saving, investment and the external balance. Whose income are we measuring? Imagine a local factory owned by an overseas family. The factory's output belongs in domestic production because the factory operates here. The profit paid to the family belongs to foreign residents' income. A country's residents might also receive wages, interest or dividends from their work and investments overseas. Start with gross domestic product, the value added within the border. Add net primary income from abroad to obtain gross national income. Add net current transfers, such as incoming remittances less outgoing ones, to obtain national disposable income. Each step answers a different question about who can spend the resulting resources. Why investment links saving to trade Consumption uses resources now. Investment, including a new machine or goods added to inventory, sets resources aside for future production. National saving is disposable income left after private and government consumption. Investments in financial securities change ownership of claims and are recorded separately from producing new machines. The current account records net exports plus net primary income and net current transfers. Substituting the expenditure expression for output shows that national saving minus domestic investment equals the current account. This is an accounting equality. To explain a deficit, investigate which decisions about consumption, investment or income changed. Private and public balances A government's deficit contributes to national borrowing when everything else stays fixed. Households can respond by saving more, or private investment can change. The national balance alone cannot tell us which response occurred. Gross saving and gross investment include depreciation. Net measures subtract it from both sides. Match gross with gross and compare all entries over the same period. A flow for the year cannot be subtracted directly from the value of the existing capital stock. title: Balance of payments
detail: C01 · Lesson 2 · Open-Economy Macroeconomics and Monetary Systems
terms: Record current transactions and their financing counterparts. State the sign convention before reconciling financial flows and reserve changes. Follow both sides of an international sale A resident exporter can ship goods without immediately receiving cash. The shipment counts as an export when ownership changes. If the foreign buyer promises payment in ninety days, the exporter has acquired a financial asset, an enforceable claim on a nonresident. When the buyer eventually pays into an existing foreign deposit account, the exporter exchanges its trade-credit asset for a deposit asset. That later exchange generally creates no second export. Double-entry bookkeeping records the two sides at the relevant time and keeps the transaction distinct from its settlement. Identify assets, liabilities and the sign convention External assets are claims residents have on nonresidents. External liabilities are claims nonresidents have on residents. Under the convention used here, the financial account equals net acquisition of external assets minus net incurrence of external liabilities. A positive difference represents net lending through financial transactions. The current and capital accounts record different kinds of transfers. A worker's remittance ordinarily enters current transfers. A qualifying capital transfer enters the capital account. With no measurement discrepancy, current account plus capital account equals the financial account under this convention. The word “capital” in ordinary news may instead refer to financial flows. Understand why a residual appears Statisticians collect goods, services, financing and reserve data from different sources. Reporting dates, missing observations and price conversions can lead to a discrepancy. A residual helps reconcile published series while preserving the underlying accounting logic. A central bank's sale of international reserves reduces an external asset. Buying its own currency in the same operation is easy to mislabel as a fresh inflow of foreign financing. Draw the balance sheets from the resident country's perspective before choosing a sign. Build a transaction ledger New machinery with two sources of finance

title: Stocks and flows
detail: C01 · Lesson 3 · Open-Economy Macroeconomics and Monetary Systems
terms: A current-account balance is a flow over time. The international investment position is a stock that can also change through exchange rates and asset revaluations. Construct an external balance sheet Imagine photographing a country's financial claims at midnight on 31 December. On one side are residents' foreign shares, bonds, loans, property interests recorded as investment, deposits and reserves. On the other side are nonresidents' claims on residents. The difference is the net international investment position, abbreviated NIIP. A negative NIIP indicates net external liabilities at that date. It can coexist with a current-account surplus this year because the surplus covers only the flow over the year. A large positive stock can likewise fall despite new net lending if existing foreign investments lose market value. Three reasons a position moves Acquiring assets or incurring liabilities changes the stock through transactions. A change in an asset's price changes the value of an existing holding. A change in the exchange rate changes its value expressed in the reporting currency. Other volume changes include particular reclassifications or write-offs. Start the reconciliation with opening NIIP. Add the net financial transactions measured using assets minus liabilities, the net valuation effect and any other change. Only under additional assumptions, such as a zero capital account and no discrepancy, can you substitute the current account for the financial transactions line. Read currency exposure on both sides A stronger domestic currency reduces the domestic-currency value of a fixed foreign-currency asset. It also reduces the burden of a liability denominated in that currency. The net effect depends on the currency composition of both portfolios, even when gross assets and liabilities are similar. Identify the order of price changes and currency conversion. If both move materially, multiply their factors. A rise of 10% in a foreign stock alongside a 10% fall in its domestic conversion rate gives 1.10 × 0.90 = 0.99, a one-percent domestic loss. title: Borrowing across dates
detail: C01 · Lesson 4 · Open-Economy Macroeconomics and Monetary Systems
terms: Foreign borrowing can move consumption forward or finance productive investment. Sustainability depends on future income relative to obligations. Write a budget for two dates A country can consume more resources today than it produces if it sells assets or borrows from abroad. A promise to repay is a future claim on resources. Draw a timeline with one column for each date and put principal and interest together in the repayment column. In a two-period economy with no opening debt and no investment, consumption today plus tomorrow's consumption discounted to today equals today's output plus discounted future output if there is no final wealth. A one-unit increase in consumption today reduces feasible future consumption by one plus the borrowing rate. Match the use of funds with the repayment source Borrowing for a temporary income shortfall can smooth living standards even if no machine is built. Borrowing for new machinery can increase the future output available for repayment. Assess the value of the project from the extra cash it creates relative to its cost and the return required on alternative uses. A persistent shortfall is different. If export revenues repeatedly fall below promised payments, rolling over old principal can postpone a cash shortage without improving underlying capacity. Liquidity asks whether a payment can be met when due. Solvency asks whether feasible future resources can cover the obligations over time. Respect dates, currencies and risk Cash earned after a deadline cannot pay a loan at maturity without interim finance. A foreign-currency loan requires that currency, or local cash that can be converted on acceptable terms. A positive expected surplus across scenarios can coexist with default in a bad scenario. The simple intertemporal model assumes access to borrowing and lending at the specified rate. If borrowing is restricted, the model may describe a preferred consumption path that the country cannot finance. A debt-service schedule exposes such constraints more clearly than a lifetime average. title: Money and inflation
detail: C01 · Lesson 5 · Open-Economy Macroeconomics and Monetary Systems
terms: Distinguish a one-time price-level change from persistent inflation. Explore how policy rates, expectations and supply shocks affect purchasing power. Build a price index from a basket A shop receipt contains prices and quantities. To isolate the change in prices, hold the quantities of a reference basket fixed and reprice it. Divide the cost in the comparison period by its cost in the base period, then multiply by 100. An index of 112 means the reference basket now costs 12% more than in its base period. Successive inflation rates compound. If prices rise 10% and then fall 10%, the index moves from 100 to 110 to 99. A reduction in the inflation rate still allows the price level to rise. A sequence of falling price levels is called deflation. Translate income and borrowing costs into purchasing power A wage increase matters to living standards relative to the consumer's prices. To calculate real wage growth, divide the nominal wage growth factor by the inflation factor and subtract one. A fixed nominal repayment also loses purchasing power when the price level unexpectedly rises. At the date a loan is made, lenders can anticipate expected inflation and adjust the nominal rate. The approximate expected real rate is nominal interest minus expected inflation. The exact one-period calculation divides the nominal gross return by the expected price-growth factor under the simple certain-inflation assumption. Trace demand and supply separately A restricted fuel supply can raise firms' costs while reducing their output. A demand expansion can increase both prices and output in the short run. The fact that inflation rose gives incomplete evidence about which shock occurred or which policy response suits it. Raising the policy rate can slow borrowing and near-term demand and can influence expectations. It cannot immediately produce missing fuel. Transmission depends on debt contracts, exchange rates and expectations, so interpret a jump in inflation alongside wage data, output and the particular basket components that changed. title: Exchange-rate regimes
detail: C01 · Lesson 6 · Open-Economy Macroeconomics and Monetary Systems
terms: Under a peg, the central bank may buy or sell reserves to maintain the rate. Under a float, the exchange rate helps absorb shocks. Why a peg consumes or accumulates reserves Think of the central bank as a dealer promising to buy or sell foreign currency at a stated price. If importers demand more foreign currency than exporters and investors supply, defending the price requires the dealer to supply the shortfall out of usable reserves or other foreign funding. Under buying pressure on the domestic currency the flows reverse. The central bank may purchase incoming foreign currency and issue domestic money. A peg can therefore create both reserve shortages and expansion of the domestic money supply, depending on the direction of market pressure. Distinguish intervention from sterilization When the central bank buys dollars with newly created local currency, domestic bank reserves can increase. Sterilization is a second transaction intended to offset the domestic liquidity effect, for example by selling domestic securities to absorb bank reserves. It can change domestic liquidity while leaving the original foreign exchange purchase in place. The central bank cannot indefinitely sell usable foreign assets it does not have. Borrowing reserves or changing interest rates may buy time, but each has an associated cost. Published gross reserves may include funds already pledged or operationally unavailable. What a float adjusts and what it leaves exposed In a float the exchange rate may change until willing purchases and sales balance. A depreciation makes a fixed foreign price more expensive in local currency. It also raises local-currency revenues per unit of foreign sales if foreign prices and volumes are unchanged. The adjustment can be uneven across sectors. An exporter with domestic costs and foreign receipts may benefit, while a domestic utility owing foreign debt can face higher debt service. The consequences depend on pricing contracts, how quickly volumes respond and how much foreign-currency debt is hedged. Calculate the cost of maintaining the rate A central bank's operating buffer
