title: The policy trilemma
detail: C01 · Lesson 7 · Open-Economy Macroeconomics and Monetary Systems
terms: A hard peg, free capital movement and independent monetary policy cannot all be maintained in the standard model. Identify which choice is constrained. Replicate the investor's currency choice Consider two one-year deposits, one local and one in the anchor currency. If the peg is believed to hold and principal can be moved freely, a local investor can convert, earn the foreign interest and return at the same exchange rate. Two comparable deposits then face direct competition. Suppose local interest is lowered while anchor interest remains higher. Investors have an incentive to move funds abroad. Meeting the demand for anchor currency at the peg depletes reserves. Holding the rate difference, the peg and free movement indefinitely conflicts with this simple mechanism. Specify the assumptions behind the trilemma The comparison assumes similar credit risk, liquidity and tax treatment, negligible transaction costs and an exchange rate expected to hold over the investment horizon. A risk that the peg will break creates an expected currency gain or loss. Default risk on deposits can also matter independently. An observed difference in interest rates alone therefore cannot prove capital controls or disprove the trilemma. Identify the denomination of each promise and who guarantees it. A premium for local bank risk is economically different from a free choice by the central bank over its risk-free short rate. Locate the available policy adjustment A country retaining a peg and open capital markets usually allows domestic monetary conditions to follow the anchor. With capital controls, some interest differences can persist because access to the foreign opportunity is restricted or costly. With a float, exchange-rate movements and expectations make the foreign payoff uncertain in domestic terms. Actual regimes often lie between these extremes. A managed float can smooth some movements, and controls can be partial. On an exam specify which constraint is relaxed and explain the economic cost, such as lost autonomy, reserve exposure or restricted access to external finance. title: Trade and terms of trade
detail: C01 · Lesson 8 · Open-Economy Macroeconomics and Monetary Systems
terms: A change in export prices alters the income obtainable from the same production. Follow the effect through import demand, public revenues and private borrowing. Separate export prices from trade volumes Suppose the country sends one tonne of cocoa abroad in exchange for imported machinery. If the cocoa price rises relative to the machine price, each tonne commands more machines. Terms of trade measure this price relationship without requiring a change in tonnes exported. Use a price index for the exports and another for the imports, with compatible base periods. Divide the export index by the import index. To report a base-100 terms-of-trade index, multiply the resulting ratio by 100. Prices and quantities then answer distinct questions. Link the price gain to purchasing power A better relative export price can raise the purchasing power of national production even when real GDP volume changes little. Gross benefits depend on export quantities as well as the price movement. If a storm halves output while raising the export price, the country can still have lower export receipts. Who receives the additional income matters. Producers can be foreign-owned, royalties can flow to government, and imported inputs can become more expensive. Trace the part of the gain actually available to residents before discussing household consumption or public borrowing capacity. Distinguish the current account response A lasting price gain might raise desired consumption and investment, including imports. A temporary gain might be saved abroad to smooth spending after prices fall. Different expectations about the persistence of the change can therefore produce different current-account paths even with identical observed prices today. A commodity producer's response also depends on extraction constraints, fiscal rules and currency denomination. An improved price ratio alone does not establish a trade surplus. To calculate the trade balance, multiply actual prices by actual quantities on each side. Price a trade bundle A crop shortage during an export boom

title: Sudden stops
detail: C01 · Lesson 9 · Open-Economy Macroeconomics and Monetary Systems
terms: External funding can dry up before spending adjusts. Foreign-currency borrowing may worsen the domestic burden of debt after depreciation. Distinguish net borrowing from gross refinancing A country can have a modest current-account deficit yet face substantial financing pressure. Old foreign loans and bonds may mature this month. Even if new imports are close to exports, refinancing old principal requires lenders to advance new money or accept new securities. A sudden stop is a sharp reduction in external financing. The loss can take the form of fewer new loans, lenders refusing to renew existing claims, or residents moving their own liquid funds abroad. A net annual figure can conceal a much larger short-term requirement. Construct a currency and maturity ladder Write foreign-currency obligations in order of due date. Separate contracted principal, interest, essential operating payments and contingent collateral calls. Beside each item record liquid reserves actually accessible by then, contracted foreign receipts and credit lines that remain available under the stress scenario. A currency mismatch appears when debt is fixed in foreign currency and income arrives in local currency. Domestic depreciation then increases the local cost of the same dollar amount. A timing mismatch remains possible even when the currency matches, because an export receipt arriving next month cannot meet today's maturity. Trace feedback between finance and output If banks lose foreign funding, they may reduce lending to businesses. Firms can then cut production or imports, which can worsen income and tax receipts. Selling assets rapidly to meet deadlines can lower their prices and shrink the collateral supporting other loans. There are several routes to closing an external gap, including spending adjustment, reserve use, voluntary refinancing and new official assistance. They have different effects on output and future obligations. A calculation of today's cash gap tells the size of the adjustment needed without identifying which route policy makers will choose. title: Comparing countries
detail: C01 · Lesson 10 · Open-Economy Macroeconomics and Monetary Systems
terms: Compare a commodity exporter and an importer using dated series. Separate descriptive indicators, accounting identities and causal explanations. Start with a measurable comparison “Which country is more exposed?” is too broad to test. Decide whether the outcome is the size of external borrowing relative to income, the amount of debt due within a year, the buying power of exports or the change in consumer prices. Two indicators can support different answers without contradicting each other. For each country list the series definition, reporting unit, time span, denominator and observation date. Ratios such as current account to GDP require both series in compatible currency units over the same period. Converting one nominal series at a year-end rate and the other at an annual average can manufacture a change. Distinguish levels, changes and revisions A deficit of four percent of GDP is a level for the period. A move from minus four to minus two improves the balance by two percentage points. The magnitude of the deficit halves, a separate relative-percent description. Explicitly state the sign used so an improvement cannot be mistaken for a larger deficit. Historical observations can be revised and some exchange rates or trade prices can be measured with error. Keep the dataset vintage if possible. If a period is missing, say which conclusions can still be drawn rather than silently substituting a value from another year. Evaluate an explanation against alternatives Suppose an oil exporter improves after oil prices rise. An importer could serve as a comparison, but the two economies may also differ in policy, exchange-rate regimes and other exports. A before-and-after difference measures the pattern and becomes evidence about causality only under additional assumptions. Ask what would have happened to the exporter without the price shock. A credible comparison needs similar pre-shock trends or a reason for its counterfactual, and a test for other simultaneous shocks. title: Quotations and cross rates
detail: C02 · Lesson 1 · Foreign Exchange and Multinational Financial Management
terms: Decide which currency is in the numerator. Reversing the quote requires taking its reciprocal, including appropriate treatment of the bid and offer sides. Read a quote as a conversion instruction A dealer quotes 1.24–1.26 dollars per euro. The unit being priced is one euro. Selling euros to that dealer earns its bid of 1.24. Buying euros costs its offer of 1.26. Write the currency names beside the numbers before doing arithmetic. The bid–offer spread compensates the dealer for inventory risk, execution costs and other factors. Headlines often show the midpoint. A customer dealing at the posted prices loses part of a round trip to the spread even if the quotes never change. Invert an executable market Inverting a quote turns dollars per euro into euros per dollar. A customer selling dollars is buying euros at the old offer. The new bid is therefore one divided by the old offer. The new offer is one divided by the old bid. The same principle works without memorizing the switch. Imagine holding one dollar and buying as many euros as the dealer will deliver. Then ask how many euros you must surrender to acquire one dollar. The buying price for the newly quoted unit should exceed its selling price. Build a cross rate through an intermediary Some currency pairs can be traded by going through a third currency. To sell sterling for yen through dollars, sell the sterling at the dollar bid and then sell the acquired dollars at the yen bid. To buy sterling through the same intermediaries, use the offers on the reverse path. Multiplying like quote directions cancels the intermediary unit. Mixed directions require a division or inversion first. A discrepancy relative to a direct dealer quote only creates an executable arbitrage if all legs can actually be placed at favourable bid or offer prices after costs. Price an executable cross A buyer needs Swiss francs

title: Purchasing power parity
detail: C02 · Lesson 2 · Foreign Exchange and Multinational Financial Management
terms: Compare the price of the same basket in two currencies. Transport costs, non-traded goods and changing baskets weaken short-run predictions. From one tradable good to a basket If identical tradable goods can move freely, a large common-currency price gap can attract buyers to the cheap location and sellers to the expensive one. Shipping costs and import restrictions can prevent that adjustment. A restaurant meal also includes local rent and labour that cannot simply be shipped. Absolute purchasing power parity extends the comparison to a basket. Express both prices per copy of the same basket. The implied exchange rate is home-currency basket cost divided by foreign-currency basket cost. It is a benchmark sensitive to quality, weights and what is tradable. Derive the relative-price prediction Let the exchange rate be home currency per foreign unit. When home prices rise faster than foreign prices, more home units would be needed for the foreign currency if relative purchasing power stayed constant. Multiply the initial rate by the home price-growth factor and divide by the foreign one. This relative version asks whether the price relationship stays stable from an initial level. It does not require baskets to have exactly equal prices at the starting exchange rate. Over long intervals multiplication of successive growth factors matters, especially when inflation is high. Measure the real exchange rate One convention defines the real exchange rate as the nominal rate multiplied by the foreign basket price and divided by the domestic basket price. A value above one under this convention means the foreign basket costs more after conversion. State your definition because inverted ratios reverse the sign of change. Consumer-price indices measure changes over time and may use different baskets. Their arbitrarily chosen base values cannot generally be treated as comparable price levels for absolute PPP. They are useful for relative changes when their definitions are understood. Use prices for the appropriate question Two baskets under different inflation rates

title: Covered interest parity
detail: C02 · Lesson 3 · Foreign Exchange and Multinational Financial Management
terms: Compare investing at home with converting, investing abroad and locking in the future conversion. Equal riskless payoffs imply a forward rate under the model assumptions. Replicate a locked future conversion A forward fixes today the exchange rate for a future currency delivery. A money-market strategy can reproduce that delivery by borrowing in one currency and investing in the other. If both strategies deliver exactly the same certain cash in every state, their costs must coincide under frictionless trading. Take one foreign unit due next year. Buying only 1 divided by the foreign gross interest factor today will grow into that unit. Translate that cost at spot and borrow the home amount today. The home repayment due next year is the synthetic forward price for one foreign unit. Derive the parity ratio from cash flows Define S as today's home currency per foreign unit, F as its one-year forward and iH and iF as the respective one-year rates. The synthetic home repayment is S × (1 + iH)/(1 + iF). A higher home rate raises F with this quotation convention. The argument compares two locked payoffs. It makes no prediction of the eventual spot rate. Distinguish the forward rate fixed in a contract from a forecast used to plan uncertain receipts. At maturity an existing contract can gain or lose value relative to spot. Test a possible arbitrage If an actual dealer will buy foreign currency forward above the synthetic acquisition cost, an investor could borrow home money, buy and invest foreign currency, then deliver it forward. If the dealer will sell foreign currency sufficiently cheaply, the reverse trade may work. Real dealers quote spreads and borrowers may pay more than savers earn. Compare executable borrowing, lending, spot and forward terms on the correct sides. Differences in collateral, maturity or creditworthiness can explain a gap without any attainable risk-free profit. title: Uncovered parity and risk
detail: C02 · Lesson 4 · Foreign Exchange and Multinational Financial Management
terms: Removing the forward contract leaves exchange risk. Expected future spot rates and forward rates can differ when investors demand compensation for holding that risk. Build a distribution of home-currency returns Owning a foreign deposit without a forward leaves a known amount of foreign currency at maturity and an unknown home-currency value. For a spot quote in home units per foreign unit, its realized gross home return is foreign gross interest multiplied by future spot divided by initial spot. Construct possible future rates rather than assuming the average is guaranteed. Conditional on fixed foreign interest, expected home proceeds use the probability-weighted future rate. The distribution, including its downside when the investor needs cash, still matters even if the expected proceeds equal those of a safe deposit. Separate covered from uncovered reasoning Covered parity compares contracts whose future conversion is fixed. Uncovered interest parity compares expected returns under assumptions that leave no additional expected compensation for currency risk on otherwise comparable deposits. The second is an economic hypothesis, not the replication proof used for the first. Forward and expected future spot may then differ. Investors might require a premium for a currency that tends to fall precisely when their other income falls. A high interest differential can compensate for potential depreciation, a risk premium, credit risk or a combination. Evaluate a carry strategy A carry strategy funds in a lower-yielding currency and invests in a higher-yielding one without locking the exchange rate. Small regular gains can coexist with an occasional currency fall that erases them. The sign of the realized result is determined after translation and funding costs. Calculate a break-even future rate at which the investment just repays the funding leg. Compare that threshold with plausible outcomes. If an investor has an offsetting foreign liability, the relevant risk of the same deposit can differ from the risk for a purely domestic saver. title: Balance-sheet exposures
detail: C02 · Lesson 5 · Foreign Exchange and Multinational Financial Management
terms: Transaction exposure concerns an identified payment. Translation affects group reporting. Economic exposure concerns future competitiveness, prices and market share. Distinguish a payment contract from a reporting currency A French parent can keep euro accounts while a foreign subsidiary pays wages in pesos and makes sales in pesos. The subsidiary's functional currency reflects its main economic environment. The group chooses a presentation currency for consolidated statements. They can differ even though the subsidiary's factories and customers do not change. A foreign-currency customer invoice has a defined amount and date. It can change value in the business's functional currency between sale and collection. A foreign subsidiary's net assets can change value when translated for group reporting even if there is no planned sale or dividend. Trace exposure through a cash-flow map Start with contracts and identify who owes which currency on what date. Net same-currency payments against receipts only if timing and legal access permit. Next identify variable sales, purchasing costs and competitor reactions that can change the future stream of operating cash. A company quoting local prices can still have economic exposure. A competitor might lower its local price after a currency depreciation reduces its own costs. The effect then runs through order volume and margins. It cannot be measured from the face value of a single invoice. Choose a measure appropriate to the decision To forecast liquidity on an invoice, translate dated cash flows at alternative settlement rates or executable hedge rates. To investigate reporting volatility, specify the accounting assumptions and which balance-sheet amount is being translated. To assess competitiveness, build an operating scenario for prices, units and costs. A translation change may become cash relevant if a loan covenant uses reported net worth or if the subsidiary is about to distribute assets. The accounting label alone is insufficient. Explain the mechanism connecting a reporting change to a financing or operating decision. Separate a group's three exposures A group with three currency effects

title: Currency hedging
detail: C02 · Lesson 6 · Foreign Exchange and Multinational Financial Management
terms: Match a business exposure with a forward, option or natural offset. Imperfect matching of timing and quantity leaves residual risk. Identify the business risk before picking a contract An importer facing a fixed dollar payment fears a more expensive dollar. Its hedge should deliver dollars at a known or capped home-currency cost. An exporter awaiting dollars fears a cheaper dollar. It needs a floor on the home currency it can receive. Foreign receipts and payments at the same date naturally offset one another. Net them by currency and date before buying financial protection. If a future receipt is uncertain, distinguish the amount already committed from the possible amount and allow for delays or cancellations. Compare a forward with a currency option A forward commits both parties to exchange a fixed amount at a fixed future rate. A purchased option gives the buyer a choice. A dollar call lets its owner buy dollars at a stated rate. A dollar put lets its owner sell them. The premium is the up-front price of that choice. At maturity a dollar holder with a put chooses the higher of spot and the strike price. Add any unmatched exposure at spot, then subtract the premium on a consistent date. A forward on a matched receipt locks one value but gives up favourable movements on that part. Compare business outcomes after hedging A hedge can have a loss considered in isolation and still protect the company if the underlying business position gains. Measure the combined outcome, including the premium, funding costs, future collateral requirements and mismatch in timing or size. Even two currencies that usually move together may separate under stress. Hedging a currency through a related currency is an approximate hedge whose residual is called basis risk. title: Multinational investment
detail: C02 · Lesson 7 · Foreign Exchange and Multinational Financial Management
terms: Discount a project’s local cash flows at a local rate or convert consistently to the parent currency. Mixing conventions can create a fictitious gain. Value a foreign project in its own currency Begin with dated cash flows available to the party being valued. For a foreign subsidiary these might be local cash generated by operations. A parent might instead require dividends actually remittable after taxes and restrictions. Identify which series is being valued before choosing a currency. If certain foreign-currency cash flows are discounted at the corresponding foreign risk-free rate, the result is a foreign amount today. Converting that present amount at today's spot rate gives home value today. This final conversion differs from converting every future payment at today's spot. Reproduce the result in the parent's currency A certain foreign amount at each date can be sold forward for a certain home amount on that date. Discount each home amount with the matching home risk-free discount factor. Covered interest parity makes the two routes agree when the borrowing, lending and forward contracts share the stated terms. In an uncertain business, expected local cash and future conversion rates can move together. Expected home proceeds depend on this joint pattern. Simply multiplying independent forecasts is justified only if their interaction is negligible or appropriately modelled. The discount rate must also match the risk of the actual home cash flow. Treat inflation and financing consistently Nominal local cash forecasts should incorporate local price growth and a nominal local discount rate. Real cash forecasts use a real rate on a consistent price basis. A foreign market's higher nominal interest can reflect inflation differences and need not imply a worse underlying project. If debt, tax shields or guarantees are valued separately, keep them out of the base operating cash flows. A company deciding whether to accept the project compares the value of future benefits with the initial investment on the same currency and claimant basis. title: Funding and the cross-currency basis
detail: C02 · Lesson 8 · Foreign Exchange and Multinational Financial Management
terms: Compare local loans, foreign borrowing and swapped funding. Credit, collateral and funding constraints can create gaps from frictionless parity. Compare loans after matching their currency The cost advertised on a foreign loan is the cost in that currency. A parent needing euros must convert the initial advance into euros and obtain enough foreign currency for every future payment. A year-end forward locks a single payment. A cross-currency swap can exchange multiple interest payments and principal over time. A swap can transform a stream of payments without eliminating the borrower’s credit spread. Determine what the firm still pays to its original lender and what it receives and pays under the swap. On each date cancel only equal and opposite cash flows in the same currency. Understand the basis as a contract term In a frictionless benchmark covered interest parity relates spot, forwards and comparable interest rates. In markets, funding pressures, collateral rules, balance-sheet costs and different credit terms can put the effective swapped rate away from a simple rate comparison. A currency-basis quote specifies an adjustment to a particular swap leg. The sign is meaningful only alongside its convention. A quoted negative spread on the foreign leg may affect a euro borrower differently depending on which leg it pays. A cash-flow comparison avoids implying that every negative quote automatically saves the firm money. Use net proceeds and an equivalent annual cost For a one-year bullet loan with no intermediate payment, all-in cost equals final home payment divided by initial usable home proceeds minus one. An up-front fee reduces the amount available today. When there are multiple payments, compare present values at a common curve or solve for an equivalent borrowing rate on the entire schedule. Company treasury should also compare whether lines remain available, counterparties can post collateral and market liquidity supports an early exit. Build the investment rule from a financing alternative If a risk-matched investment earns 10%, one unit today can become 1.10 next year. Reversing that trade means one unit due next year is worth 1/1.10 today. Net present value adds all dated cash flows after putting them into today's units. For independent projects with adequate resources, each positive-NPV project adds estimated value. For mutually exclusive alternatives the company can take only one, so compare total NPVs on the same assumptions. A separate budget constraint can require choosing a feasible combination of projects. Interpret the internal rate carefully The internal rate of return sets a project's NPV to zero. For a conventional outflow followed solely by positive inflows, a higher discount rate lowers NPV. In this setting an IRR above the required return supports acceptance when the project is considered on its own. Mutually exclusive projects can differ in scale or timing. A small project can generate a high percentage on little capital. A large project can add more currency value at a lower percentage. When signs change repeatedly the NPV equation may even have multiple roots, making a single IRR rule unreliable. Find a crossover through incremental cash Subtract one project's cash-flow schedule from the other's to measure precisely what the larger commitment buys. Discount the difference at the required return. A positive incremental NPV means selecting the second project adds value compared with selecting the first. The crossover rate makes those incremental flows worth zero. It describes a ranking boundary, not necessarily either project's own IRR. A meaningful comparison also requires consistent project lives or an explicit assumption about replacement if equipment will be renewed. Choose between mutually exclusive designs Two bottling lines

title: Cost of equity and debt
detail: C03 · Lesson 3 · Corporate Finance and Capital Structure
terms: Investors require compensation for time and risk. Estimate the cost of new debt and distinguish it from an old loan’s stated coupon. Separate coupon, promised yield and expected return A coupon is the contract payment calculated on debt principal. A market yield uses the price investors pay today for the promised payments. A borrower with an old 4% coupon can therefore face a 6% market cost when it needs new finance. If repayment is uncertain, promised yield can exceed the expected return lenders receive after defaults and recoveries. A quoted marginal borrowing rate is a practical input under stated conditions. In a high-default setting be clear whether your model discounts expected cash flows or contractual promises. Estimate how shareholders price market exposure The capital asset pricing model links required equity return to the risk-free rate plus beta times the expected market risk premium. Beta measures how the security's returns move with the broad market. A beta of two describes systematic sensitivity, not a promise to earn twice the market return each year. The market premium is already the market return above the risk-free rate. If a question gives the expected market return itself, subtract the risk-free rate before multiplying by beta. Use a risk-free input consistent with the currency and maturity convention of the analysis. Choose comparison companies thoughtfully Historical equity beta reflects both business risk and financing risk. A highly indebted peer can have a larger equity beta even if its operations closely match the project. Sector peers, leverage differences and the noise in historical estimates deserve attention when selecting an input. Use marginal debt terms for similar borrowers and maturity. A subsidized old bank facility or a short floating loan might poorly represent a long-term corporate investment. title: Weighted capital costs
detail: C03 · Lesson 4 · Corporate Finance and Capital Structure
terms: Weight debt and equity costs by market values and match the discount rate to the cash flow. A company-wide rate can misprice an unusually risky project. Identify the cash flow being discounted Free cash flow to the firm represents operating cash after reinvestment but before interest or principal paid to creditors. Both shareholders and lenders have claims on it. A weighted required return reflects the cost of financing that same operating activity across those claimants. Equity cash flow comes after net borrowing and debt service, so the shareholders' return is the relevant starting rate. Charging interest in a firm cash-flow forecast and then discounting at a rate that already includes the debt contribution mixes financing methods. Why the weights use value today Market-value weights represent what capital suppliers currently have invested at today's prices. Book values measure historical accounting amounts and can be far from current market values. A long-run target financing mix may be more appropriate than a temporary balance-sheet position if the model assumes it will be maintained. The familiar after-tax formula is equity weight times cost of equity plus debt weight times pretax borrowing cost times one minus the marginal tax rate. It assumes interest deductions will be usable within the valuation framework. Tax losses or debt limits may change that assumption. Recognize project and policy boundaries WACC from an established retail business can misprice a risky mining project. A project should reflect its own operating exposure, currency and financing policy. Comparable pure-play firms can help estimate a more suitable rate, with adjustment for financing differences. title: Financing irrelevance
detail: C03 · Lesson 5 · Corporate Finance and Capital Structure
terms: In the Modigliani–Miller benchmark, investors can reproduce leverage on their own. Financing can redistribute risk even when it leaves total firm value unchanged. Start with the assets before dividing the claims Imagine identical operating companies generating the same cash in every possible state. One issues only shares. The other promises part of the cash to debt investors first and leaves the remainder for shareholders. The Modigliani–Miller benchmark asks whether this rearrangement alone can change the total market value of the operating assets. Assume no taxes, bankruptcy or transaction costs, identical information, access to comparable borrowing, and operating decisions that do not change with financing. Buying all the debt and equity in the levered firm then reproduces the unlevered firm's whole operating cash flow. Equal payoffs imply equal total value. Show homemade leverage explicitly An individual can mimic a fraction of levered equity by buying the same fraction of unlevered assets and borrowing the corresponding fraction of corporate debt. Subtract the individual's promised repayment in every state. With the model's common borrowing terms this reproduces the company's equity payoff. If the two packages have different market costs despite identical payoffs, the cheaper one can be bought against the more expensive one under the model's trading assumptions. This replication argument explains irrelevance. It does not claim that financing never matters in an actual company. Explain why equity becomes riskier Debt has a prior claim. When the same change in operating value passes to a smaller starting equity base, its percentage gain or loss grows. In the simple tax-free benchmark, required equity return equals the unlevered required return plus debt-to-equity times the difference between operating and debt required returns. Using more lower-cost debt while holding the equity cost fixed misses the increase in residual risk. The opportunity cost of the operating assets remains the weighted average under the benchmark. Distress costs, interest deductions, borrowing constraints or changed project selection can break the equivalence. Replicate a fractional equity position An investor copies a levered shareholding

title: Taxes and debt capacity
detail: C03 · Lesson 6 · Corporate Finance and Capital Structure
terms: Interest deductions can add value when usable. Compare the benefit with expected distress costs and the loss of financial flexibility. Calculate a tax shield on usable deductions An interest tax shield is the reduction in taxes attributable to deductible interest. Start by comparing tax paid with and without the interest deduction in the same period. If the company has enough taxable profits and the full interest is deductible, tax saved equals interest times the marginal tax rate. A business making losses may only use some deductions later, subject to the case rules. A tax saving used two years from now is worth less today than an otherwise equally safe saving received now. Label whether your figures are annual cash savings or present values. Distinguish fixed debt from a target leverage policy For a predictable debt schedule, calculate interest period by period from the opening debt. Calculate the usable tax benefit at each date and discount it for the modeled risk. The discount rate on the shield depends on the uncertainty of debt policy and the firm's ability to claim the deduction. The expression tax rate times debt is a special result often obtained for permanent fixed debt with fully usable deductions and a particular risk assumption. It does not apply automatically to a two-year loan that amortizes or to deductions that may expire unused. Evaluate costs of financial distress Distress can reduce business value before formal insolvency. Customers may fear interrupted support, suppliers can shorten credit terms, and management may reject valuable projects to conserve cash. Expected distress cost weights possible economic losses by their probabilities and dates. Compare the benefit and expected cost of an additional borrowing decision. Do not count a transfer of money from shareholders to existing lenders as lost total value unless the analysis is specifically from shareholders' perspective. Distinguish direct administrative costs and disruption of operations from a redistribution of claims. Evaluate additional debt A two-year loan repays in stages

title: Agency and information
detail: C03 · Lesson 7 · Corporate Finance and Capital Structure
terms: Managers, lenders and shareholders face different incentives. Information gaps can explain financing preferences and why an equity issue can move the share price. Use a payoff table to reveal conflicting incentives A company's debt promises a fixed amount while shareholders receive the residual after creditors have been paid. In a bad state limited liability can reduce shareholder payoff to zero. This asymmetry can tempt owners of a distressed firm to take extra risk with creditors' money. Compare total firm payoffs as well as outcomes for debt and equity. A decision that increases expected equity while reducing total expected firm cash is an agency conflict. Without that two-claimant comparison a risky project can look like an attractive investment even while it destroys economic value. Recognize debt overhang as a different mechanism With existing risky debt, a valuable new safe investment can increase creditor recovery. If shareholders must contribute all the new money but receive little of the gain, they can refuse a positive-NPV project. This is called debt overhang or underinvestment. Creditors and owners can sometimes negotiate a partial debt write-down, give new money a priority claim or agree on covenants and control rights. The proposed remedy should change the particular incentive and remain credible in bad states. Information also affects financing choices Managers may know more about company performance than outside investors. If investors suspect a share offering occurs when shares are overpriced, they may demand a discount. Internal funds avoid selling a security whose quality is hard for outsiders to judge. Relatively safe debt is often less sensitive to this information than equity. This logic helps explain a possible financing order, but companies also issue equity for acquisitions, regulation, risk reduction and growth options. Evidence of an issue alone cannot establish managerial intent. Consider other observable predictions, including how cash holdings or information quality affect financing. Map the conflict before proposing a remedy An owner declines a safe improvement

title: Payout policy
detail: C03 · Lesson 8 · Corporate Finance and Capital Structure
terms: Compare dividends, repurchases and retained cash. Ask how taxes, investment opportunities, signals and management incentives alter a frictionless payout result. Follow the cash through a distribution Before a dividend a share includes a claim on the cash about to leave. After distribution the company owns less cash and the shareholder holds a separate cash payment. In a frictionless benchmark, all else equal, the ex-dividend share price falls by the dividend per share. A share repurchase leaves fewer shares outstanding. At the fair pre-buyback price, the total value and share count fall proportionally, so the remaining price per share is unchanged under the same assumptions. Investors who sell receive cash in exchange for surrendering a claim. Compare payout with keeping cash A shareholder wanting cash can sell a few shares in a frictionless market, and one wanting to reinvest dividends can buy shares. This supports an irrelevance benchmark when investment policy stays fixed, markets work without costs and payout forms are taxed alike. If retaining cash finances a positive-NPV project which would otherwise be lost, the investment decision changes the comparison. Conversely, managers could spend excess cash on low-value projects. Assess the realistic alternative use of cash, likely external financing costs and liquidity needs. Understand transfer and signalling effects Buying shares above intrinsic value can transfer wealth from remaining holders to sellers, even if the company reports higher earnings per share. Buying below intrinsic value can favour continuing holders. Such statements require an intrinsic-value assumption that may be hard to observe. A regular dividend can create expectations about future payments. A repurchase program can offer more flexibility, though its signal depends on actual execution and context. terms: Value the project without leverage, then add financing effects separately. This is useful when the amount of debt changes markedly over time. Separate business value from financing arrangements Adjusted present value asks two questions in order. What would the project be worth if financed entirely with equity? How do the actual financing arrangements alter that value? Keeping these layers separate helps when debt balances, tax benefits or issue fees change significantly through time. The unlevered operating forecast includes taxes as if there were no interest deductions. Discount these operating cash flows at the required return on the underlying business assets. Subtract the initial operating investment to obtain unlevered NPV before adding financing side effects. Classify financing cash flows correctly Borrowing principal at fair market terms creates a matching repayment obligation. Loan proceeds alone are not incremental value for all investors. An issue fee uses real cash, a concessionary loan may confer a subsidy and interest deductions may reduce taxes. Each can create a separate adjustment. A subsidy can be valued by comparing the cash actually received with the market present value of the promised payments on equivalent risk and terms. A financing guarantee may have its own value or cost. Keep separate a true subsidy and the mere availability of ordinary borrowed money. Select a rate and date for each adjustment A predetermined tax benefit that is as safe as the debt can be discounted at the stated debt rate in a simplified case. A shield conditional on operating profit or refinancing can carry a different risk. A fee paid immediately is already in present-value terms. title: Flexibility and real options
detail: C03 · Lesson 10 · Corporate Finance and Capital Structure
terms: The right to delay, expand or abandon changes an investment’s payoff. Identify when a fixed cash forecast understates the value of waiting. Identify a decision that can actually be deferred A real option is a right to change a business decision after new information becomes available. An empty site can have value if its owner can open a store after demand becomes clearer. If a competitor can take the site or the owner is already bound to build, the supposed right may be much less useful. Distinguish uncertainty about cash from flexibility to act on it. A risky project with an irreversible spending commitment does not acquire a valuable option merely because outcomes are uncertain. Specify who controls the decision, when it can be exercised and what new information will be known. Solve choices at the decision node At the last decision date, compare the payoff from acting with the payoff from walking away. Choose the better permitted action separately in each state. Work backwards to the earlier decision using the case's valuation assumption. Averaging project values first and applying a single choice afterwards removes the flexibility. For an abandonment option, compare the sale or salvage value with the value of continuing operations at that date. For expansion, compare incremental operating value with the expansion cost. Existing business already owned should enter both choice alternatives consistently. Treat risk and opportunity cost explicitly Actual outcome probabilities can be used with an appropriate risk adjustment when supplied. For training cases a risk-neutral decision maker, risk-neutral probabilities or a zero-risk-adjustment assumption may be specified. Avoid discounting a payoff with strong market risk at a risk-free rate merely because it is an option. Waiting may forfeit early income, lead to a higher future construction cost or invite competition. Compare the full values of investing now, preserving the right and doing nothing. The value of flexibility is measured against an explicitly defined strategy without that flexibility. Work a small decision tree A developer reserves a site

title: Operating cash flows
detail: C04 · Lesson 2 · Company and Equity Valuation
terms: Convert after-tax operating profit into cash available to all capital providers through reinvestment and working-capital adjustments. Convert operating profit into distributable operating cash A sale made on credit can create reported revenue before the customer pays. Equipment bought today can use cash long before its depreciation is recorded. Free cash flow to the firm reconciles these timing differences to measure cash available to all capital providers after operating reinvestment. Begin with operating profit before financing charges. Calculate operating taxes on a consistent unlevered basis using the case assumptions. Add back depreciation and other relevant noncash charges already deducted. Subtract actual capital expenditure and the increase in noncash operating working capital. Rebuild operating working capital Operating working capital can include trade receivables and inventory less trade payables and other comparable operating liabilities. Ordinarily exclude debt, interest-bearing financing, and surplus cash from this operating balance. A supplier granting the business a longer credit period can temporarily free cash even if sales and profit are unchanged. Use the change between opening and closing balances. A positive operating working-capital change absorbs funds, since more resources are tied up. A decrease releases funds. Working-capital improvements may reverse if customers leave or suppliers demand quicker payment, so avoid projecting one-off releases forever. Identify reinvestment without double counting If you start with after-tax operating profit after depreciation, add depreciation back then subtract gross asset spending. Equivalently subtract net capital expenditure, defined as gross capital expenditure minus depreciation, without also adding depreciation. Keep acquisitions and disposals on the same operating perimeter as the earnings forecast. A company can show positive operating cash while consuming value if it postpones necessary maintenance. terms: Higher sustainable growth generally requires more reinvestment or better returns on new capital. Check that forecast margins and capital needs agree. Connect additional profit with additional capital Investing 30 of this year's after-tax operating profit into equipment and working capital creates extra earnings only if the added capital is productive. The return on incremental invested capital compares next period's increase in operating profit with this period's additional investment under the simple steady model. If after-tax operating profit is E and a fraction b is reinvested at an incremental return R, next period's extra profit is E × b × R. Dividing by E gives the growth rate g = b × R. This relation links a forecast of earnings growth to an explicit financing need. Separate prospective returns from historical averages A company might have earned 25% on early patents but achieve only 8% on new expansion. The old average return does not establish the return available at the margin. Competition, required distribution spending and asset intensity can all reduce the return on later projects. Growth can also come temporarily from higher margins or better use of assets already in place. A mature forecast cannot rely forever on rising utilization or margin. Separate the transitional improvement from the new capital needed once the business reaches a stable operating level. Check whether growth creates value If the incremental return exceeds the required return for the incremental investment's risk, reinvestment can generate economic surplus. When the returns are equal, a faster-growing business can redistribute cash across time without increasing the present value created by each extra investment. Use the same asset and tax basis on both sides of the comparison. Compare after-tax unlevered operating return on new assets with a suitable operating cost of capital. terms: Use a rate consistent with currency, inflation, financial leverage and operating risk. Distinguish diversifiable company risk from priced market risk. Choose the discount rate by the cash promise A known euro payment and a risky share of a company's cash cannot be assigned the same discount rate solely because they occur on the same date. Begin by identifying payment currency, inflation basis, business risk, financing exposure and who receives the cash. The risk-free starting rate can differ across currencies because nominal inflation and monetary conditions differ. A project located in one country can generate cash in another currency. Location alone does not determine which nominal rate matches the cash forecast. Translate real to nominal consistently A real cash flow is expressed in the purchasing power of a specified date. A nominal cash flow includes future changes in the price level. With constant inflation π, the consistent nominal gross return is the real gross return multiplied by 1 + π. The extra product term makes exact results differ from simply adding rates. Choose real-real or nominal-nominal for the whole calculation. Specific selling prices or import costs may rise differently from broad inflation, so the operating forecast can still require relative-price adjustments even if it is stated in constant purchasing-power units. Distinguish market risk from bad expected outcomes A forecast of expected cash should already reflect such possibilities as product failure or customers paying less than promised. A required risk premium compensates for exposure to risk investors price, such as outcomes correlated with market conditions. A diversified investor can bear some firm-specific variation without requiring the same premium as broad market exposure. State whether a scenario adjustment changes the average cash forecast or its systematic exposure. Reducing expected cash for an identified loss and mechanically adding a second full penalty for that same expected loss risks overstating the discount. Other remaining systematic uncertainty may still warrant a premium. Audit cash flow and discount-rate consistency A nominal forecast built from real factory income

title: Terminal value
detail: C04 · Lesson 5 · Company and Equity Valuation
terms: Estimate the cash after the explicit forecast. A perpetual-growth formula requires a discount rate above the growth rate and economically sustainable reinvestment. Place terminal value on the forecast timeline A company can keep earning long after the analyst's detailed five-year forecast ends. Terminal value is the value at the end of the explicit forecast of all later cash flows covered by the continuing-business assumptions. It is a value measured on a future date, not a cash receipt available today. For stable cash flows growing at g and discounted at r, each discounted payment is a constant fraction of its predecessor. Summing the geometric series gives next period's free cash divided by r minus g. Convergence requires r greater than g in the standard positive-cash perpetuity. Build a sustainable first continuing-period cash flow The numerator must be the first cash after the final explicit period. Apply growth only once. If the final forecast cash includes a temporary tax benefit, unusual margin or low capital spending, normalizing sustainable operating earnings and reinvestment can matter more than mechanically growing the last cash number. A positive perpetual growth forecast needs capital to support it. With stable incremental return on capital, the required reinvestment fraction is growth divided by that return. Apply the resulting free-cash conversion to sustainable after-tax operating profit and check that maturity assumptions fit the industry. Handle sensitivity and finite businesses As the discount-rate minus growth spread shrinks, value becomes highly sensitive. A table changing r and g can show this, but the cash numerator should also respond if greater growth requires more reinvestment. A firm cannot outgrow the market that sustains it indefinitely without a convincing change in assumptions. A concession that expires without renewal and equipment exhausted at contract end need a finite cash-flow forecast and any net recovery or cleanup cost. A perpetuity for an asset with no continuing rights overrides the economics of the contract. Reconcile the continuing value A mature business settles into steady growth

title: Trading comparables

terms: Put companies on a common accounting and time basis. Similar multiples can conceal different growth prospects or risk. Match the multiple to the financial claim A price-to-earnings multiple compares common equity value with earnings available to ordinary shareholders. An operating-value-to-operating-profit multiple compares all funders' claim on operations with earnings before interest. Combining equity price with operating profit can make companies with different debt loads look deceptively cheap or expensive. Write units beside each input. A multiple of eight means that eight units of value are paid for each unit of the specified earnings, sales or cash metric. A sales multiple can be calculated for a loss-making company, but its meaning depends heavily on attainable margins and capital needs. Normalize the comparison before ranking peers Ensure that all companies use the same earnings period. Trailing earnings refer to a completed period while forward earnings depend on forecasts. Select peers for economic comparability, explain genuine differences, and consider both the median and the spread rather than selecting the most convenient company. title: Banks and financial firms
detail: C04 · Lesson 8 · Company and Equity Valuation
terms: Debt is part of a bank’s operations, making industrial cash-flow methods awkward. Relate equity earnings and book value to sustainable return on equity. Value the bank from the shareholder's perspective A retailer borrows to finance stock and stores. A bank collects deposits to fund the loans and securities on which it earns interest, so interest paid and received are central to its operations. Removing deposit funding and interest as though they were incidental industrial financing can produce an uninformative operating-cash measure. Bank analysts often start from common equity, earnings available to shareholders and capital needed to support the balance sheet. The bank may report a profit but need to retain part of it to replace losses or support asset growth. Dividend capacity can therefore differ from the dividend actually paid. Derive a stable price-to-book relationship Suppose beginning book equity is B, sustainable return on equity is ROE, equity grows at g and required equity return is k. Next year's earnings are ROE × B. Retaining g × B supports the specified book growth, leaving a dividend of (ROE − g) × B under the simple clean-surplus assumptions. A growing dividend perpetuity has equity value equal to next dividend divided by k − g, provided k exceeds g. Dividing by B gives justified price-to-book of (ROE − g)/(k − g). An ROE above k can support a premium to book when the assumed returns persist. Interpret book equity with care Loan-loss provisions, asset measurement, goodwill and unrecognized credit deterioration can distort reported book value or near-term ROE. A low price-to-book might represent expected losses rather than a cheap franchise. Tangible common equity or normalized earnings sometimes provide a useful additional view if used consistently. If credit conditions are temporarily excellent, current ROE can exceed its sustainable level. A valuation should allow for normal provisioning, costs, capital needs and the effect of competition. title: Residual income
detail: C04 · Lesson 9 · Company and Equity Valuation
terms: Start with book equity and add the value of future profits above the equity charge, under consistent accounting and payout assumptions. Charge equity capital for its opportunity cost Accounting net income deducts interest on debt but does not normally charge a cost for the shareholders' opening capital. Residual income calculates earnings remaining after that charge. For a period, take net income attributable to common shareholders and subtract the opening common book equity multiplied by its required return. A business can report positive profit but negative residual income. Investors may be better off elsewhere if the return on the capital committed is below the risk-appropriate benchmark. The charge is an economic comparison rather than a payment the company actually sends shareholders. Connect residual income with dividends Clean surplus links closing book equity with opening equity, earnings and distributions, adjusting for owner contributions where relevant. In a simplified company with no new shares, closing book equals opening book plus earnings minus dividends. Rearranging expresses dividends in terms of earnings and changes in book. Substitute this expression into a dividend valuation and discount across periods. The book-value changes telescope, leaving current book equity plus the present value of future residual income under consistent accounting and terminal assumptions. It is a different way to describe the same economic claim. Forecast the charge on a moving base Use opening book equity for each year's charge. Retained earnings increase the book capital on which shareholders require a return in subsequent years. Starting every year from the original base can inflate future residual income. If earnings bypass the assumed income measure, reconcile the clean-surplus relationship before applying the model. The terminal assumption matters. If competition erodes return on equity to the required return, subsequent residual income becomes zero even though profit continues. Persistent excess returns instead require a continuing residual-income value. Explain why a forecast supports either outcome. Construct a residual-income timeline A two-year earnings franchise

title: Portfolio variance
detail: C05 · Lesson 2 · Investments, Portfolio Theory and Asset Pricing
terms: Combine individual variances with covariances. An asset can reduce portfolio risk even when its standalone volatility is high. Derive the covariance term For two assets held throughout one period, portfolio return is w times the first return plus (1 − w) times the second. Subtract expected return and square. Expanding that square produces two squared deviations and two copies of their cross-product. Taking expectations gives the familiar two-asset variance expression. The cross-product is positive when the two returns move to the same side of their means. Covariance reports its average in squared-return units. Correlation divides that covariance by both volatilities to express co-movement on a scale from −1 to +1. Keep decimal and percentage units consistent. When risk can disappear in a classroom model With exactly opposite standardized movements, one asset’s surprise can cancel the other’s. Matching weights requires matching the sizes of the weighted volatilities. Equal weights cancel only when the underlying volatilities are equal. Such an exact hedge depends on stable correlation and trading weights. With positive correlation less than one, diversification can still lower risk relative to the average weighted volatility. The incremental effect of adding an asset depends on its covariance with the existing portfolio. An especially volatile addition can reduce total risk if the exposure it offsets is large enough. What a covariance estimate represents Historical covariance estimates describe co-movement in the observations sampled. Monthly returns, local currencies and stale bond prices can change the apparent result. A covariance measured in different currencies from the intended investment does not describe its final spending risk. Asset weights drift when market values move. Rebalancing restores intended weights but creates trades and costs. Simulate high-correlation stress years as well as normal years when severe common shocks are the concern. title: The efficient frontier
detail: C05 · Lesson 3 · Investments, Portfolio Theory and Asset Pricing
terms: Find the best expected return feasible at each risk level. Estimated means and covariances can move the frontier substantially. Feasibility before efficiency A portfolio belongs to a feasible set if it meets the budget, borrowing, short-selling, liquidity and position rules. A mathematically elegant allocation involving short sales can be outside an actual mandate. First describe the set to which the efficient frontier applies. Efficiency in mean–variance analysis eliminates choices where expected return could rise without extra volatility, or volatility could fall without reducing expected return. The minimum-variance portfolio is the leftmost feasible point. Portfolios below the upper branch may offer less expected return for the same risk. Solve for a minimum with two assets Write variance as a quadratic in the weight w invested in A. Minimizing it gives w = (variance of B − covariance)/(variance of A + variance of B − 2 × covariance), if the denominator is positive. The unrestricted solution may fall outside zero to one. When short sales are prohibited, compare the permissible boundary if the optimal unconstrained weight is outside it. If a target expected return is imposed, the two-asset budget and return equations may fix the weights, leaving no freedom for further risk reduction. Uncertainty in the frontier Expected returns are estimates of future averages, often imprecise relative to monthly volatility. Small changes can swing an optimizer toward extreme weights that exploit apparent differences. Asset caps, alternative estimates and comparisons across samples help reveal where conclusions depend on noisy inputs. Variance penalizes unexpectedly good and bad returns symmetrically. A pension plan concerned about failing to pay benefits may also need a shortfall or liability-relative analysis. The mean–variance frontier summarizes a chosen objective, investment universe and set of constraints. Construct a defensible frontier The same frontier and two goals

title: The risk-free asset

terms: Combining a risky portfolio with borrowing or lending changes total risk. Real borrowing constraints complicate the textbook separation result. Separation of the risky choice from scale Suppose all investors can lend or borrow at one known rate and agree on expected returns and covariance. A blend of cash and a risky portfolio lies on a straight line in expected-return versus volatility space. Its slope is the risky portfolio’s excess expected return per unit of volatility, its Sharpe ratio. The line with the highest feasible slope touches the risky frontier at a tangency portfolio. Within this textbook setting, investors can share that risky mix but hold different amounts of it. A cautious investor lends the balance. An aggressive investor can borrow to fund additional risky holdings. The safe asset is horizon specific A nominal repayment in one currency can be known at its maturity. If the investor must sell a long bond tomorrow, its price tomorrow is unknown. Even a perfectly matched nominal payment can be risky in real purchasing power or in the investor’s home currency. If the institution lends at one rate and borrows at a higher one, the attainable line changes slope for leveraged positions. Borrowing limits, margin calls and collateral requirements can make some points unreachable. A single tangency solution need not govern every investor facing different borrowing terms. Leverage scales losses as well as expected gains For risky weight y, the cash position has weight 1 − y. When y exceeds one, that cash weight is negative. Equity risk is magnified because the borrowed amount is due even if the fund performs badly. The liquidity needed to avoid forced selling may differ from a model’s predicted annual volatility. A return on invested capital and return on the investor’s own equity use different denominators. title: Capital asset pricing
detail: C05 · Lesson 5 · Investments, Portfolio Theory and Asset Pricing
terms: CAPM relates expected excess return to exposure to the market. Estimate beta as covariance with the market divided by market variance. Read beta as a regression slope Plot a security’s excess returns against market excess returns over matching dates. In a linear regression the slope beta measures how much security return moves on average for a one-unit market move. A beta of 1.4 describes a conditional sensitivity, not a prediction that every 1% market increase produces precisely 1.4%. The intercept measures average return left unexplained by the fitted sensitivity to the market. A residual varies month by month. A large surprise on a single announcement date is different evidence from a stable positive intercept over a long, pre-specified sample. From sensitivity to required reward CAPM adds an equilibrium claim to the statistical regression. If investors share the model’s opportunities and the market portfolio is the aggregate risky portfolio, expected excess returns lie on a line against beta. The risk-free asset has zero beta, while the market portfolio has beta one. The relevant risk is covariance with the portfolio investors already hold. Total volatility includes firm-specific risks a broad holder can diversify. A volatile company with little market co-movement can consequently have a lower CAPM expected return than a quieter company with greater co-movement. Choosing and interpreting the benchmark The theoretical market includes all risky wealth. A local equity index is a practical proxy with omissions. Thin trading, leverage changes, sector shifts and a short estimation history can also change estimated beta. A failed CAPM test against one proxy may reflect both model and benchmark. A negative-beta claim can protect purchasing power when the market performs poorly. The model can assign such a claim expected return below the safe rate. title: State prices
detail: C05 · Lesson 6 · Investments, Portfolio Theory and Asset Pricing
terms: A payoff delivered in bad times may be especially valuable. A discount factor weights a payment by both when and in which state it arrives. State prices from traded cash flows Imagine writing a contract that pays one euro only if a specified future state occurs. The price today of this elementary claim is a state price. Any contract paying different amounts across those same states is a bundle of these claims. Its price is the sum of state prices multiplied by the corresponding cash flows. If elementary claims do not trade directly, try to reproduce them with traded assets. With two states, a risk-free bond and a share with different payoffs across the states can span both outcomes. Two copies of securities with proportional payoffs add no new state coverage, so some claims may remain unpriced by replication. Probabilities, discounting and insurance Let the physical probability of a state be p and let m represent how much a euro in that state is worth today per unit of probability. The state price is p × m. A severe downturn may receive a high m because a euro is especially useful when other resources are scarce. Adding all state prices gives the current price of a guaranteed euro. Dividing each state price by this sum creates pricing probabilities that sum to one. Those weights price a claim when paired with risk-free discounting. They need not equal the frequencies a forecaster assigns to actual events. Positivity and a price consistency test If someone can acquire a claim at zero or negative cost that pays a nonnegative amount in every state and a positive amount in a genuinely possible state, unrestricted trading permits an arbitrage. Under the usual no-arbitrage assumptions relevant possible states can be assigned strictly positive weights. If a market price implies a negative state price in a complete two-state setup, identify a replicating position before claiming a usable trade. Bid–ask spreads, short-sale restrictions or an omitted state can invalidate the simplified economic conclusion. Infer the price of protection Insurance against a bad harvest

title: Arbitrage and factors
detail: C05 · Lesson 7 · Investments, Portfolio Theory and Asset Pricing
terms: A portfolio can carry several common exposures. Factor models describe variation in returns and can be tested as explanations for average returns. A factor model has two jobs A statistical factor model decomposes realized returns into exposures to shared movements and a residual specific to the security. A pricing model adds the claim that differences in average returns are explained by exposure to factors with risk premiums. A regression that explains daily movements well need not explain average returns. Factors can be market-traded portfolio returns or surprises in macroeconomic variables. Their units matter. A coefficient on a one-percentage-point inflation surprise is different from a loading on a one-percent traded portfolio return. A macroeconomic shock has no obvious purchase price until a replicating or tracking strategy is defined. The logic behind arbitrage pricing Build two well-diversified portfolios with the same common exposures. If one offers permanently higher expected return without extra residual risk, buying it and shorting the other yields a positive expected spread with little modeled risk. This motivates linear relationships between expected returns and factor sensitivities. A finite long–short trade can still carry residual risk, estimation error, financing costs and short-borrow risk. Positive expected spread is weaker than strict arbitrage, which requires a nonnegative payoff in every state and positive payoff in at least one possible state. Constructing neutral exposure If one fund has market loading 1.2 and another 0.8, equal money long and short leaves market loading 0.4. To isolate a manager’s nonmarket contribution, scale the hedge to match exposure. Adding a second factor usually requires another independently exposed instrument. Track how hedge weights change the budget and funding. A long–short book with zero net purchase price can still require collateral and capital. Its return convention must specify whether results are divided by equity, gross exposure or another defined capital base. Separate fitted return from pricing error Two hedges for two influences

title: Efficiency and anomalies
detail: C05 · Lesson 8 · Investments, Portfolio Theory and Asset Pricing
terms: A test of excess returns also tests a benchmark model. An apparent anomaly may reflect a missing risk factor, a bias or a cost of trading. Specify what efficiency would predict An informationally efficient price reflects a specified information set in a way that leaves no systematic abnormal earning opportunity after allowing for the costs and risks of the test. The word abnormal requires an expected-return benchmark. Historical price information, public disclosures and private knowledge represent different information sets. A price can move sharply after unexpected public news in an efficient market. The relevant questions concern what was known before the announcement, how quickly it entered the price and whether an implementable strategy could have earned a predictable risk-adjusted gain afterwards. Reconstruct the research clock Create an information date, signal date, execution date and evaluation date. Financial statements are often published weeks after their accounting period ends. Constituent lists rewritten using today’s survivors and revised macroeconomic data can leak later information into a historical simulation. Multiple testing compounds the problem. Trying thousands of signals and reporting the top one creates apparent success even in random data. Lock the rule, keep a genuinely untouched period and compare results with implementation costs, turnover and realistic liquidity in the securities traded. Separate risk compensation from mispricing A small-company strategy might beat a broad index because its returns fall especially far in recessions. Its positive average excess return then has a risk interpretation. Alternatively, prices might respond slowly to news. To distinguish them, describe an observation that would be more likely under one mechanism than another. A factor-adjusted regression can supply a risk benchmark, but the factor model itself is estimated and debatable. Even a statistically unusual alpha is conditional on the model and sample. terms: Examine overconfidence, loss aversion and limits to arbitrage. Ask what distinctive evidence would support a behavioural account of a price pattern. Give a behavioural story a measurable prediction The disposition effect is a tendency to realize gains more readily than losses relative to a reference price, often the purchase price. To test it, count opportunities to realize gains and losses as well as the sales made. A bull market produces many winning holdings even for someone choosing sales at random. Loss aversion describes an asymmetric response to comparable gains and losses around a reference point. It does not alone predict every selling decision because beliefs about future returns matter. State a specific comparison that would distinguish reluctance to realize a loss from sensible expectations of recovery. Consider competing explanations A household can sell winners to rebalance a concentrated portfolio. Tax rules can favor realizing losses near a reporting deadline. Very small or illiquid losing positions may be disproportionately expensive to sell. Portfolio cash needs may force sales unrelated to any reference point. Compare similar opportunities within an account or across comparable securities and dates. Observe subsequent performance without assuming investors knew it in advance. Ask whether the pattern survives plausible differences in costs, taxes, rebalancing and desired portfolio weights. Why informed traders may not immediately erase mispricing An arbitrageur can recognize a valuation discrepancy but be unable to short the expensive asset, borrow it cheaply or hold the trade until convergence. The assets may have related rather than identical payoffs. Interim losses can provoke client withdrawals before prices correct. A behavioral explanation of prices requires both a reason for biased demand and a reason informed capital cannot fully offset it. A pattern in individual trading is evidence about investors’ choices. title: Prices and yield to maturity
detail: C06 · Lesson 2 · Fixed Income and the Term Structure of Interest Rates
terms: Discount promised cash flows to find a bond’s price. Yield to maturity is the single rate reproducing that price under the quoted convention. A yield is an internal rate on promises Set the amount paid today equal to the discounted stream of future contractual amounts. The rate solving that equation is yield to maturity under the chosen compounding convention. For an ordinary positive stream, increasing the rate reduces every future present value, so there is at most one economically relevant solution. Coupon rate measures promised interest relative to face. Current yield divides annual coupon by today’s price, omitting any eventual price movement toward redemption. Yield to maturity includes that redemption but still uses the promised schedule even when the borrower may fail. Why realized returns can differ A person selling before maturity receives an uncertain sale price. A holder to maturity also faces coupon reinvestment and default risk. The yield reproduces the present value of the promises today. To obtain the same compound rate on end wealth, interim coupons must be reinvested appropriately and the promised payments must occur. A zero-coupon bond has no interim coupon to reinvest. Its nominal compound rate to maturity can be locked in if bought at a known full price, held to redemption, and paid as promised. Currency, tax and purchasing-power effects can still change a particular investor’s outcome. Compare compounding conventions A quarterly nominal quote of 8% means 2% per quarter under the specified convention. Its effective annual rate is 1.02 to the fourth power minus one. A yield quoted under semiannual compounding must be converted before direct comparison with an effective annual yield. Between coupon dates, the valuation requires time fractions consistent with the settlement convention. The clean price excludes earned coupon interest. title: Convexity
detail: C06 · Lesson 6 · Fixed Income and the Term Structure of Interest Rates
terms: Bond prices are curved functions of yields. A second-order term improves a duration estimate when the yield move is larger. Look beyond the tangent Price as a function of a conventional bond yield slopes downward and usually bends upward when cash flows are fixed and positive. Two equal yield changes in opposite directions therefore have unequal effects. A fall adds slightly more price than duration alone predicts and a rise subtracts slightly less. Mathematically, modified duration is minus the first price derivative divided by price. Convexity is the second derivative divided by price. In the second-order approximation the proportional change is −duration × Δy + ½ × convexity × (Δy)². Omitting the half doubles the curvature adjustment. Estimate from three revaluations Some instruments lack a convenient fixed cash-flow derivation. Reprice with rates down and up by the same small decimal amount h. Effective duration equals (Pdown − Pup)/(2P₀h). Effective convexity equals (Pdown + Pup − 2P₀)/(P₀h²). The curve-shift and valuation model used become part of the estimate. Very small shocks can show numerical rounding error. Very large shocks capture nonlocal behaviour. A callable security can exhibit negative effective convexity as refinancing caps price gains when rates fall. Changing assumed exercise behaviour can alter both sensitivities. Use convexity in an economic comparison At the same initial price and duration, higher positive convexity can produce better modeled price performance for a symmetric yield move either way. detail: C06 · Lesson 10 · Fixed Income and the Term Structure of Interest Rates
terms: Match sensitivity of assets and liabilities. A duration match may leave exposure to a twist in the curve or a changing credit spread.
