title: Contract design and monitoring
detail: S02 · Lesson 9 · Lending and Credit Analysis
terms: Select maturity, amortization, security, covenants and reporting frequency. Explain which incentive or information problem each provision is meant to address. Write a term for a specific economic risk A maturity date answers how long the bank is exposed. Amortization determines how fast principal declines. Security addresses losses if repayment fails. Covenants can restrict behaviour or give early warning. Requiring a report is worthwhile when someone can obtain it, verify it and act on it in time. A maintenance covenant tests an agreed threshold regularly. An incurrence covenant may test a threshold only when a specified action occurs, such as raising more debt. A borrower can pass an incurrence test at origination but weaken between transactions. Contract definitions and test dates decide which right a lender actually has. Compute and interpret headroom For a minimum coverage ratio, headroom may be expressed as actual coverage minus the minimum or as how far sustainable cash could fall before breach. For a maximum leverage covenant, lower debt or higher earnings generally create room. State the unit of headroom, since ratio points and euros mean different things. Management may change reporting choices, postpone expenses or add back costs in adjusted earnings. Define permissible adjustments, cross-check statements, and test whether the ratio still represents cash risk. An overly tight term can generate repeated waivers for ordinary seasonality. Monitor asset-based lending with discipline Receivable eligibility, advance rates, overall commitment size and sublimits jointly determine availability. Outstanding drawings reduce what can still be borrowed. Concentration caps can leave a large customer invoice partially excluded even when it is current. Know the order in which the contract applies eligibility and caps. A falling base can leave existing debt above the allowed borrowing amount. That overadvance calls for a response under the agreement, rather than assuming the borrower can use remaining headline commitment. Ongoing reporting should detect disputed invoices, aging or related-party sales. Translate risks into terms A cap hidden beneath the headline line

title: Credit scoring and judgment
detail: S02 · Lesson 10 · Lending and Credit Analysis
terms: Distinguish ranking borrowers from calibrating their actual default probabilities. Check overrides, missing observations, fairness and performance across time and borrower groups. Separate ranking from probability accuracy Two applicants can be ordered from higher to lower risk without knowing either true default probability. Discrimination measures how often a score assigns greater risk to customers who later default than to those who perform. A ranking metric can stay unchanged after multiplying all predicted probabilities by two. Calibration asks whether, among customers assigned a particular probability, the observed event frequency supports that estimate over the matching horizon. A model can discriminate well but dramatically underprice loans by understating every probability. Measure both properties on observations unavailable when the model was fitted. Approval policy changes what is observable Credit outcomes are usually observed on loans the institution funded. A policy rejecting applicants below a cutoff changes the observed sample. A score that performs well inside the approved range may behave differently outside it. Treat claims about declined customers as assumptions unless separate outcome evidence exists. Avoid leakage from collections or later account deterioration into features purportedly available when underwriting. Divide tests by origination time, customer identity where relevant, and business-cycle period. Missing values can signal genuine differences, inconsistent data capture or treatment that changes across branches. Set a cutoff with economic and fairness evidence The cost of declining a viable customer differs from the loss on approving a defaulting one. A cutoff can be based on expected contribution using spread, exposure, loss severity and the calibrated probability. A lender should separately evaluate outcomes across relevant groups and investigate whether variables proxy for inappropriate factors under applicable rules. Judgment may add information absent from standardized inputs. Record both upward and downward overrides, the reason, who approved them and subsequent performance. Comparing overridden cases directly with all others can be misleading because they may have entered review for a reason. Validate an underwriting score A cutoff that looked sensible in training

title: Portfolio and country risk
detail: S02 · Lesson 11 · Lending and Credit Analysis
terms: Defaults can cluster by industry, currency or region. Two loans with the same standalone loss estimate can contribute different amounts of portfolio risk. Calculate the portfolio distribution Expected losses add across loans because expectation is linear. Independence is unnecessary for that sum. Dependence becomes important when asking how often losses exceed a level, how much capital a severe event might consume, or how much diversification a new loan contributes. A portfolio of small loans can behave like one large risk if every customer depends on a single employer or export buyer. Nominal loan count and borrower legal names can mask this link. Map ultimate sources of cash, common collateral, guarantees and shared funding markets. Move from domestic cash to foreign debt service A borrower can be solvent in local currency but unable to obtain or transfer the currency its foreign lender requires. Separate commercial default, adverse exchange-rate movement, convertibility restrictions and transfer restrictions. Each may harm collections through a different route. A currency hedge can have an amount or maturity mismatch, collateral requirements, and an exposed counterparty. Export receipts in the debt currency provide a natural hedge only if they actually arrive in the correct entity by the payment date. A domestic sales invoice labelled in dollars is less useful if buyers cannot obtain them. Use scenario limits intelligently A country limit can restrict gross exposure, net exposure after permitted guarantees, or stressed loss. State the chosen unit and avoid counting a foreign guarantee twice. A facility may concentrate country exposure despite a globally diversified parent if local restrictions trap the operating cash. Construct a common scenario and propagate its consequences loan by loan. Recalculate debt burden, cash transfer dates, default and recovery. Then compare aggregate loss with the stated tolerance. An average loss estimate is a different quantity from the amount lost if the scenario actually occurs. Map the shared shock Two suppliers and one port closure

terms: Track arrears, covenant breaches and deteriorating collateral. Compare a waiver, restructuring and recovery under the case’s enforceable priority and timing assumptions. Recognize deterioration before a payment is missed A borrower can keep interest current by selling inventory below cost, stretching suppliers or drawing another facility. Look for changes in collections, disputed invoices, management turnover, repeated covenant waivers and falling margin even while payments continue. Compare the figures with the original credit assumptions. Distinguish a liquidity problem, where cash arrives too late, from a viability problem, where future operating cash cannot sustain obligations. A rolling weekly forecast exposes payment dates. A medium-term forecast tests whether the business can produce returns after maintaining its assets. Identify the bank’s real alternatives A waiver temporarily relaxes a contractual right. A standstill can coordinate creditors while a plan is assessed. Restructuring changes payment promises and may require new working capital. Liquidation sells assets and distributes net proceeds by priority. The feasibility of each path depends on specific agreements and applicable law in the case. Creditors may disagree because senior claims and junior claims gain differently from waiting. A plan that increases total enterprise value can still reduce the senior lender’s own expected recovery if it must fund new money or cede priority. Build separate cash flows for each stakeholder. Compare economic recovery by date Calculate expected present recovery on each feasible path, net of enforcement costs, new advances and delay. Apply probabilities to internally consistent outcomes and state the discount rate and risk treatment. Avoid subtracting expected loss again if cash flows already reflect default scenarios. A plan may depend on owners injecting equity, retaining a key customer, replacing management or releasing collateral. Convert assumptions into conditions and milestones. title: Define the scope
detail: S03 · Lesson 1 · Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Accounting
terms: Connect each diligence question to a valuation or contractual decision. A possible earnings issue and a verified cash obligation require different evidence. A diligence question needs a decision A financial review has a deadline and a buyer with limited investigative time. Start with the decision that could change. If earnings depend on a distributor renewing next year, the decision is whether the business justifies the proposed price under plausible renewal outcomes. A list of all invoices would be an expensive first request. Set the perimeter before testing. Identify the legal entities, operations, dates and currencies included in the sale. A parent’s report may include a profitable division that will stay with the seller. No amount of detailed margin analysis rescues an incorrectly defined asset. Different claims require different records An assertion that sales occurred can be tested with contracts, fulfilment evidence and collections. An assertion that a customer will remain requires renewal terms, history, concentration and evidence of demand. A ledger can show how much was recorded without establishing either performance or repeatability. Evidence has dimensions of independence, completeness and relevance. A signed contract may establish a cancellation right, but a later signed amendment may supersede it. A random invoice sample can estimate frequency. A deliberate sample of unusual transactions can reveal mechanisms but cannot establish their frequency without further work. Allocate effort by decision value Materiality measures how a finding might influence a decision. Repeated small charges can matter at a large valuation multiple. A low-probability event can matter if it stops the business operating. Set quantitative thresholds alongside qualitative triggers such as unreliable records or conditions essential to completing the purchase. Assign an owner, deadline and consequence to missing evidence. A buyer might condition completion on evidence of a licence, model an ordinary commercial uncertainty in cash flows, or seek protection for a past liability. A request matters when its answer could genuinely change the decision. Draft a focused request A maintenance company’s contract renewal

title: Reconcile the data
detail: S03 · Lesson 2 · Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Accounting
terms: Tie management accounts to the ledger and signed statements. Track periods, entities, adjustments and unexplained reconciling items. Numbers that balance can mean different things Management accounts can show a division’s trading performance while statutory consolidated statements describe all controlled entities under the relevant reporting framework. A single euro difference can arise from an omitted company, a month cut off at a different date, foreign-currency translation or inclusion of internal group sales. A reconciliation explains the difference between two totals with identifiable entries. First harmonize scope and definitions. Matching two reports created by the same system proves they agree with each other, not that either one captures every delivery or obligation. Independent evidence becomes useful once the population is understood. From the transaction to the signed accounts A ledger is the detailed record of entries. A trial balance lists accounts and their debit or credit balances. Management reporting groups those accounts into lines useful for decisions. Statutory statements may then add consolidation eliminations, external reporting adjustments and audit entries. Follow the direction of the bridge. Removing an internal sale reduces consolidated revenue, while adding a previously excluded external subsidiary increases it. At the end, calculate a residual. An unresolved difference belongs in a visible open-items line with an owner, not a rounded plug treated as resolved. Data quality changes what can be sampled Obtain a reconciliation for each material period, not just a convenient annual total. Two different errors may cancel over a year. A December accrual reversed in January can distort the trend used for a valuation even though the two-year sum matches perfectly. Before selecting transactions, verify record counts, unique identifiers, date boundaries and signs. Select some entries from the ledger into source documents to test recorded activity, and some from dispatch logs into the ledger to test completeness. Those directions answer different questions. title: Sustainable earnings
detail: S03 · Lesson 3 · Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Accounting
terms: Separate normal business costs from defensible one-off items. Repeated exceptional expenses can be part of the cost of running the business. Recurring is an economic judgment A seller’s adjusted profit often starts with earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization, abbreviated EBITDA. Removing financing and certain noncash charges can help compare operations, but EBITDA still depends on accounting choices and can exclude large real demands for investment. Normalizing earnings asks what these operations would earn under a defensible ongoing arrangement. A charge with an exceptional label may recur every year as a succession of restructuring programmes. Conversely, a single relocation can be genuinely unusual if the move is complete and future costs reflect the new premises. Set a sustainable replacement cost The buyer needs the people, buildings and systems required to operate independently. If an owner pays herself no salary, replace that missing expense with a realistic market cost. If the seller charges unusually high rent, examine the binding lease and when a market-rate alternative is achievable. A buyer’s ability to close another site is buyer-specific synergy. Putting that saving into normalized standalone earnings and then adding it again in the integration model inflates the case. Maintain independent columns for historical normalization, achievable standalone changes and changes available only after combination. Link past adjustments to forecast cash An accepted add-back is a change to an earnings indicator. It does not reverse a real payment made in the past or erase an outstanding claim. If a one-time lawsuit produced a valid cash payable, adjusting recurring earnings and recognizing the cash obligation can both be appropriate if they represent different effects. Build a track record over several years. Check invoices, board decisions, staffing needs and subsequent trading. Where the future cost depends on uncertain volume or an expiring subsidy, present a range and explain why a single favourable year is unrepresentative. title: Revenue quality
detail: S03 · Lesson 4 · Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Accounting
terms: Examine cut-off, returns, customer concentration and contractual terms. A booked sale can exaggerate earnings if the underlying delivery occurred later. What the customer has actually agreed to buy Recording revenue involves identifying the promised performance, the consideration and when control passes to the customer under the relevant terms. An invoice may be issued before the company delivers. A cash deposit may commit a customer while still leaving the company obliged to supply the service. Start with the contract and subsequent changes. Delivery terms, rights of return, rebates, cancellations and obligations after shipment can all affect timing or amount. Inspecting bank receipts can establish that cash moved, but a refundable deposit does not by itself prove earned revenue. Timing versus underlying durability A cut-off error places a valid sale in the wrong reporting period. It can inflate a trailing earnings figure and make later growth look weak even if total lifetime sales are unchanged. Correct both the revenue and the associated cost of goods sold when the case warrants it. A different concern is sustainable quality. A sale correctly recorded to a customer that dominates revenue can be risky if renegotiation is near. A surge in quarter-end shipments with longer payment terms can also borrow demand from next quarter without creating lasting customer value. Construct evidence in both directions Sample material shipments before and after the reporting date. Match orders, contracts, delivery acceptance, invoices, inventory movement, returns and later cash. Tracing ledger sales to delivery tests occurrence and timing. Tracing delivery evidence back into the sales ledger also tests omitted transactions. Use credit notes and returns after closing to challenge estimates available at the reporting date. A later return might reflect a defect present before closing or a genuinely new event. Record the mechanism before projecting the observed return rate to products or channels with different histories. Quantify a quality adjustment An equipment dealer’s December rush

title: Cash conversion
detail: S03 · Lesson 5 · Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Accounting
terms: Compare earnings with collections, inventory purchases and recurring investment. A high margin can coexist with persistently weak cash generation. Why profit can arrive before cash Accrual accounting records economic activity when earned or incurred. Cash follows the payment terms. Growth can therefore increase profit and simultaneously absorb cash as a business stockpiles goods, pays suppliers and waits for customers. A business can succeed commercially while needing more funding to sustain that success. A simple operating working-capital measure adds receivables and inventory, then subtracts operating payables. An increase uses cash. If customers pay faster, an otherwise identical business can release cash without creating a new sale. If the business postpones supplier payments, the cash benefit can reverse sharply later. Where capital expenditure belongs EBITDA excludes depreciation. Depreciation spreads past investment across accounting periods, but worn machinery eventually needs cash replacement. Estimate maintenance requirements using operating evidence as well as recent spend. A seller can temporarily improve cash flow by postponing maintenance until after closing. A simplified cash bridge starts from EBITDA and subtracts cash taxes, capital spending and increases in working capital under the stated definition. Other cash items may be relevant in an actual business. Define the intended measure before comparing companies that treat leases, interest or acquisitions differently. Look through a flattering reporting date Compare monthly or quarterly conversion across a complete seasonal cycle. An inventory build before peak season can reverse. Overdue stock that fails to sell may require a write-down and fresh funding. Review aging, collection and sale evidence to distinguish a timing effect from economic loss. Assess whether cash improvement came from operations or financing. Selling receivables might move collections forward in exchange for fees or recourse, changing risk and timing. A rise in one period’s bank balance says little about the repeatable amount available to service debt. Build a cash-conversion bridge A distributor showing healthy profit

title: Normal working capital
detail: S03 · Lesson 6 · Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Accounting
terms: Estimate the level required to operate through a normal cycle. Check seasonality, growth and supplier-payment changes before choosing a target level. What the buyer expects to receive An operating-business price normally assumes the business has the stock, receivables and supplier support it needs to trade. A working-capital target, often called a peg, specifies a benchmark. The parties agree whether the purchase price moves euro for euro when defined closing balances differ from that target. Think of a shop delivered with empty shelves and all customers having already paid. Future buyers must finance restocking even if the historic profit figure was correct. The target protects the economic package on which the operating valuation was agreed. An excessively high target can also transfer value unfairly to the buyer. Select an operating period that makes sense Average monthly balances reduce sensitivity to one unusual date, but can be misleading for a fast-growing or seasonal company. A wholesaler may always build inventory before winter. Delivering a summer average at a winter closing could leave a shortfall even if the annual average was measured accurately. Relate balances to activity. Receivable days can be approximated by average receivables divided by credit sales times the number of days, using comparable periods. Inventory and supplier days require appropriate cost or purchase bases. A stable percentage of sales is a shortcut that needs verification if product or payment mix changed. Consistent definitions protect both sides Exclude the same items from historical targets and actual closing balances. Items treated as debt-like elsewhere should be checked for duplicate inclusion. A one-time old tax balance may be economically different from normal supplier credit, but a surprise reclassification at closing can bias the adjustment. Review collection, stock and supplier behavior near the measurement date. Faster discount collections, delayed stock purchases or stretched supplier payments can make closing appear attractive for cash while impairing operations. The contract and the economic interpretation should both be visible in the analysis. Estimate and challenge a peg A growing winter wholesaler

title: Net debt and debt-like items
detail: S03 · Lesson 7 · Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Accounting
terms: Define debt, cash and obligations economically similar to borrowing. Track items across earnings, net debt and working capital to avoid double counting. Which claims come with the shares? Equity holders own the residual after other claims. When a price is quoted for operations, a buyer needs a bridge to shareholder proceeds reflecting what cash is delivered and what obligations are assumed. Start with funded debt and identify other claims whose economic effect resembles a financing obligation. Contract definitions matter. Cash pledged to another creditor, deposits held for customers and money trapped in another entity may not be fully available to the buyer. A shareholder loan may be repaid, transferred or capitalized before closing. Trace each item to who ultimately receives or pays cash. Why operating bills are treated differently Ordinary unpaid supplier invoices continually arise in operating and are generally reflected in a working-capital mechanism where agreed. An overdue legacy settlement, an exceptional shareholder liability or unpaid transaction fee may instead be defined as debt-like. Classification depends on the terms and the cash-flow economics of the specific balance. Changing a classification without updating both the actual balance and historical working-capital target can create an artificial price effect. Build a grid showing each material account’s location in earnings, debt, working capital and forecast cash. More than one location can be valid only when genuinely different effects are being measured. Estimate uncertain and related items An indemnity, pension obligation or tax dispute can have uncertain payout, duration and enforceability. One may be valued probabilistically, excluded by contract, or protected separately. Do not automatically convert an accounting provision into an identical cash deduction. Inspect timing, probability and the contract’s remedy. Distinguish the same cash flow appearing twice from two effects of the same event. A one-time legal expense can be added back to recurring earnings while an actual unpaid settlement reduces closing equity, if they concern future earning power and a distinctly payable amount. title: Price mechanisms
detail: S03 · Lesson 8 · Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Accounting
terms: A completion-accounts clause adjusts the price at closing. A locked-box mechanism fixes a reference balance sheet and controls specified value leakage. What can change between signing and closing? A business continues to collect cash, buy stock and repay borrowings between the offer and legal transfer. Parties can agree how that movement affects their settlement. Completion accounts measure specified balances at closing, typically followed by a final reconciliation after the buyer obtains reliable records. A locked box uses an earlier agreed balance sheet to fix an equity price, subject to the contractual leakage and other agreed terms. The seller may receive a separately negotiated time-related amount. Identify exactly what is fixed, what can still adjust and when each party bears commercial changes. Design a completion calculation At closing the seller may receive an estimated price. An agreed process prepares and reviews the final accounts under stated definitions, accounting policies and dispute hierarchy. The final adjustment is the difference between final and provisional equity prices. It is not the entire final debt balance again. Use the agreed reference for each term. A €1m rise in debt lowers equity, a €1m rise in eligible cash raises it, and a €1m working-capital surplus can increase the price under a common formula. The direction comes from the contract, not from who prepared the accounts. Identify leakage in a locked box Leakage usually concerns specified value transferred to the seller or connected parties after the reference date, such as an unpermitted dividend. Ordinary payroll or buying inventory is generally economically different. A payment to a connected supplier could be legitimate if permitted and at agreed commercial terms. Evidence includes bank transfers, related-party ledgers, shareholder decisions and the approved list of permitted payments. A decline in sales after the locked-box date is an operating event and does not automatically become seller leakage. Check covenants and remedies before making a claim. title: Acquisition accounting
detail: S03 · Lesson 9 · Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Accounting
terms: Recognize eligible assets and liabilities at the measurement basis the applicable standard requires. In a simple 100% purchase, goodwill is the residual after identifiable net assets. Identify the acquirer and the measurement date Buying enough voting shares can give one enterprise control over another. For a business combination within the applicable acquisition-method rules, the acquirer recognizes the identifiable assets and liabilities it acquires at the acquisition date using the prescribed measurement bases, commonly acquisition-date fair value subject to exceptions. Determine what has actually been purchased. An asset purchase can have different accounting from acquisition of a business. Establish the control date and identify any pre-existing relationship, previous shareholding or remaining outside shareholders. These facts change the calculation beyond the simple full cash acquisition used first. What counts separately from goodwill? Identifiable assets include qualifying intangibles such as contractual customer relationships or patents even if the seller did not previously show them. Recognition and measurement requirements are specific. The analyst cannot simply recognize every positive synergy as an asset to eliminate goodwill or understate identifiable liabilities to improve a ratio. Goodwill is the residual after recognized identifiable net assets in a simple wholly owned cash acquisition. More complex cases can include the measured non-controlling interest and fair value of a previously held interest. A bargain purchase may require reassessment before recognizing a gain under the applicable rules. Accounting allocations affect later earnings Assigning more value to a finite-life asset can raise subsequent amortization expense. That accounting charge affects reported earnings even where the allocation itself creates no extra cash on the acquisition date. Valuation, contractual purchase price and later financial reporting each answer distinct questions. Tax bases can differ from accounting acquisition-date values and create deferred tax effects. Do not apply a universal adjustment without case assumptions. Similarly, expected future integration spending ordinarily requires a separate assessment of whether a present acquired obligation exists. A management plan alone does not establish one. title: Findings and uncertainty
detail: S03 · Lesson 10 · Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Accounting
terms: Distinguish evidence, company explanations, unresolved requests and estimated exposure. A weakly supported adjustment can matter more than a small precisely measured one. Facts and estimates have different evidential weight A good findings report lets a reader reproduce the evidence before accepting the recommendation. A signed settlement specifies an obligation. A manager’s statement that settlement is likely is a hypothesis. A range produced by multiplying contract volumes by a disputed rebate rate is an estimate, with assumptions that should remain visible. Distinguish absence of evidence from evidence of absence. If a requested side letter has not arrived, the analyst cannot value it at zero simply because the data room lacks it. Nor should an unverified rumour be deducted as a fixed debt. Describe what changes in each credible state. Quantify sensitivity with a decision in mind The useful number may be a threshold, not an expected value. If a bid creates €1m of headroom before an unresolved claim, find the claim size or probability that consumes that headroom. With a single cash claim paid today, expected exposure is probability multiplied by amount, only when the probability has evidential support. A valuation multiple amplifies a recurring earnings issue, whereas a fixed one-time payment often affects equity euro for euro. Treating them identically can hide the most important issue. Check dependence if several findings stem from one customer contract or one disputed accounting choice. Select a response and an evidence owner Choose a mechanism matching the problem. Missing proof of ownership may need resolution before closing. A clearly defined contingent tax cost might be allocated by a collectible indemnity. Falling sustainable earnings usually require a revised forecast or price. The decision must show which risk the buyer still bears. Document who should obtain the outstanding evidence and by when. A statement that a claim is “covered” should identify the cap, deductible, time limit and ability to collect. If the buyer keeps the downside above a cap, show it explicitly in the sensitivity. title: Liquidity and solvency
detail: S04 · Lesson 1 · Corporate Distress and Restructuring
terms: Map near-term payments separately from the value of the entire business. A solvent borrower can face a timing crisis and an insolvent one can have cash today. Two balance sheets for two questions A company can own a profitable building and still miss tomorrow’s payroll. The building matters to overall economic value but cannot necessarily be sold, pledged and converted into spendable cash overnight. Liquidity concerns money available on the date it is needed. Economic solvency concerns whether resources cover obligations in value. Cash is an asset in both tests, but the two analyses use different dates and comparisons. For liquidity, use unrestricted cash, expected cleared receipts and facilities actually drawable by the payment date. For solvency, estimate assets on an internally consistent sale or going-concern basis against the relevant claims. Why published figures can mislead The accounting balance sheet measures different assets under different rules and typically describes an earlier date. Book equity can be positive even if customers have stopped paying and specialist equipment would sell for very little. Economic value can also exceed book value where a profitable customer network is absent from the accounts. Debts need equal scrutiny. A loan with years to maturity may be immediately payable if an enforceable acceleration provision is triggered. A supposedly committed facility might be unavailable following a covenant breach. Read the facts supplied. Legal insolvency tests and directors’ duties depend on jurisdiction and cannot be inferred solely from these teaching measures. Match the remedy to the diagnosis A temporary timing gap can sometimes be solved with a bridge that is repaid from a confirmed collection. Borrowing to cover a permanent shortfall in business value can delay a wider restructuring and reduce future recovery if it funds ongoing losses. Evaluate what cash flow will repay the extra borrowing. A company with cash today but inadequate long-run value needs a credible operating or capital change before cash runs out. Conversely, forced liquidation of a valuable but illiquid company can destroy going-concern value. Prepare both tests before choosing a rescue, sale or standstill. Prepare a two-part diagnosis The freight operator’s Friday payroll

title: Causes of distress
detail: S04 · Lesson 2 · Corporate Distress and Restructuring
terms: Separate temporary working-capital stress, structural operating losses and excessive leverage. A different cause requires a different remedy. Trace the first break in the cash chain Cash distress can arise from weak operations, a longer operating cycle or an unsuitable funding structure. Start with the product. Does each additional unit generate cash above its variable cost? Do total margins cover fixed overhead and necessary investment at a realistic sales volume? Then trace how long the business must finance stock and customer credit. A profitable exporter can run short when buyers pay weeks late. Finally compare operating cash with contractual interest and principal. A healthy business may be unable to meet a maturity that was financed on the assumption of perpetual refinancing. Separate a seasonal squeeze from structural loss Seasonal inventory and slow collection can cause a reversible gap. Establish the evidence for reversal through customer orders, historical collection and actual post-period sales. A return to normal cannot be assumed when inventory is obsolete or customers have lost access to credit. Contribution margin is selling price less variable cost per unit. Break-even sales volume equals fixed operating costs divided by unit contribution under constant price and cost assumptions. This operational threshold does not include debt repayment unless included expressly. A business can clear operating break-even yet fail to service debt. Which intervention changes the cause? A maturity extension buys time but does little for products that lose money on every sale. Repricing, changing product mix or exiting a loss-making contract can improve unit economics. Refinancing can smooth payments if the remaining business generates sustainable cash, but may transfer risk to new lenders. Different causes can coexist. A recovery forecast might assume higher prices, quicker collections and cheaper funding simultaneously. Test which assumption matters most and whether they can hold together. A substantial price increase could slow sales or customer payments, offsetting the expected cash improvement. Diagnose in sequence A manufacturer with two problems

title: Thirteen-week cash model
detail: S04 · Lesson 3 · Corporate Distress and Restructuring
terms: Estimate collections and payments by week, roll cash forward and compare forecast with actual cash. Identify the first breach of a minimum balance. A direct forecast follows the bank account In distress a monthly profit forecast can conceal a Friday cash failure. A direct thirteen-week model organizes customer receipts, payroll, suppliers, rent, taxes and financing by the weeks in which money will clear. It starts with unrestricted bank cash in the entity that actually pays. Use due dates as a starting point, not as guaranteed behavior. For major customers, include actual payment patterns, disputes and collection promises. For critical suppliers distinguish the date the company wants to pay from the date supply will stop without payment. A late cheque can disrupt next week’s production. Distinguish funds available from cash drawn Keep the opening cash, ordinary net flows, facility borrowing or repayment and closing cash on separate lines. Undrawn credit is a resource if the conditions are met. It is not already bank cash. A minimum operating buffer can create a shortfall even when the closing bank balance is positive. Roll each closing balance into the next opening. A downside scenario that delays a collection should remove it from the original week and place it in its new week if still collectible. Deleting it permanently would model a credit loss instead of a delay. Learn from forecast errors Compare the previous week’s forecast with bank-cleared actual flows. A variance can be timing, amount or classification. A postponed rent payment temporarily flatters closing cash. Carrying that favourable variance into the next twelve weeks without inserting the overdue payment overstates liquidity. Prioritize actions before the first breach. A rescue facility that cannot close until week five cannot solve week three without an interim measure. Test the size and duration of extra funding, how it will be repaid, and whether its costs or security conditions change the subsequent forecast. title: Creditor map
detail: S04 · Lesson 4 · Corporate Distress and Restructuring
terms: Trace legal borrowers, collateral, guarantees, ranking and maturities. Group-level value does not automatically flow to every creditor of a subsidiary. Identify the legal borrower before adding values A creditor lends to a legal person. An operating subsidiary might own plant and customer receivables, while a holding company owns shares in that subsidiary. Consolidated financial statements combine the group’s accounts for reporting. They do not automatically combine the groups of creditors entitled to each asset pool. For each claim, identify borrower, guarantors, collateral, ranking, maturity and outstanding amount. A guarantee can create a second route to recovery subject to its terms. An intercompany loan can make a parent a creditor of a subsidiary as well as its shareholder. The applicable agreements and law govern reach and priority. Why structural position matters With no cross-guarantee and no parent-owned intercompany claim, a parent creditor can generally look to the parent’s own assets under the hypothetical terms. The subsidiary’s assets first support its own creditors. Only residual share value, if any, contributes to the parent’s pool. Security can attach to particular property, while unsecured creditors share other value according to the assumed priorities. A guarantee adds a claim, not a second entitlement to recover more than the amount owed. Apply contractual caps and count prior recoveries before calculating any remaining deficiency. Use a map, then a waterfall A diagram helps locate legal relationships, but the numerical work requires a separate waterfall for each pool. Start where assets actually sit. Deduct costs as specified, pay claims by the stated order, then move any residual or guarantee recovery to the correct claimant. Timing matters if several entities have different processes or cash restrictions. A parent might ultimately recover residual value from a subsidiary yet have no free cash this week. A recovery estimate and a dated cash forecast answer different questions, so a creditor should request both. Trace one monetary unit A hotel group with a parent facility

title: Liquidation value
detail: S04 · Lesson 5 · Corporate Distress and Restructuring
terms: Estimate proceeds, disposal costs and delay. Converting realizations into present value makes comparison with an immediate offer meaningful. What could the assets actually fetch? Liquidation replaces a continuing operation with proceeds from selling its resources and collecting claims. Start with saleable quantities and likely buyers. Specialized equipment may fetch less if removed from its site. Inventory sold in bulk might realise a lower price than if it were sold through an operating retail network. A receivable’s book face value is a promise, not cash in hand. Estimate recoverable amounts by customer quality, disputes and collection time. Likewise, proceeds from a building may require environmental work and broker fees. State which costs are already netted so they do not appear twice. Time and liquidity discounts are different A rushed sale can command a lower expected selling price because few bidders can inspect or finance the asset in time. Separately, a given expected receipt next year is worth less today than an otherwise comparable immediate payment. Estimate the sale-price effect first and then discount the resulting timed cash. A payment due to a professional adviser today and a percentage selling fee paid at closing belong on different dates. Discounting sale receipts but deducting all costs at their full amounts today can bias the comparison. Document whether returns are gross, net and risk-adjusted. From asset values to creditor recoveries The total liquidation value available to claimants is not a particular creditor’s recovery. Allocate net proceeds to the appropriate legal entity and collateral pool, then apply the agreed ranking and secured claim caps. A bank with security on the building may have no exclusive claim on inventory. Compare liquidation with a going-concern sale or immediate cash offer on the same basis. If the immediate offer includes taking responsibility for environmental cleanup, avoid charging that cleanup to the seller again. Sensitivity to realisation rates, timing and disposal expenses reveals the fragile parts of the estimate. Construct a realization schedule A two-stage warehouse liquidation

title: Going-concern value
detail: S04 · Lesson 6 · Corporate Distress and Restructuring
terms: Value a reorganized business after operating changes. Distinguish sustainable operating value from the separate distribution of that value among creditors. Value a business that survives A reorganized company can keep relationships, staff, technology and systems that sell for less if scattered. Going-concern value measures the economic benefit of keeping that organization together. Start with cash the operations could sustainably generate after taxes, necessary investment and working capital under a credible turnaround. A rescue has to pay for the path to those cash flows. If a new machine, severance payment or supplier catch-up is required today, include it unless the forecast already contains it. The cost of new money concerns economic resource use, how rescuers divide the resulting value is a separate financing question. Build the future from operating drivers Model what changes in units sold, realized prices, resource costs and capacity. A statement that margins will return to normal is inadequate if major customers left or skilled employees must be rehired. Compare the scale implied by the forecasts with supply constraints, working capital and the implementation timetable. A constant perpetuity pays the same cash every year beginning one period from the valuation date. Its present value is annual cash divided by the required return under the stated perpetual, stable assumptions. If cash is delayed an extra year, discount the perpetuity one further period. Businesses with finite contracts require finite forecasts. Compare continuation with disposition Compare net values belonging to the same stakeholder group at the same date. Liquidation can release cash immediately, while operating value can take time to deliver. Include disposal costs in liquidation and rescue funding in continuation. Do not deduct existing debt on one alternative and omit it from the other. Sensitivity matters because the decision can turn on a small long-run margin assumption. Compute the operating cash needed to break even relative to liquidation. Then ask if a credible plan can deliver and sustain it without hidden investment or additional risk. title: Priority and recovery
detail: S04 · Lesson 7 · Corporate Distress and Restructuring
terms: Apply the assumed payment order to distributable proceeds. A claim can recover only what remains after higher-priority claims have been satisfied. A euro is paid once A priority waterfall distributes a fixed pool among separate ranks. Start with proceeds available after the costs the problem says must be deducted. Pay the highest rank up to the amount of its allowed claim. Pass only the remaining pool to the next rank. Keep any unallocated residue for the last entitled party. Within one rank, claims may share proportionally under the assumed rules. If two equally ranked claims of €6m and €4m share €5m, they recover €3m and €2m. Their euro recoveries differ while their recovery percentages match. A contractual cap can change the amount entering the class. Collateral may create a separate pool A secured loan has a claim against specified collateral under the case terms. Net collateral proceeds might not cover the full loan. The unpaid shortfall, called a deficiency, may or may not share in the unsecured pool depending on the stipulated law and agreement. State the assumed treatment before calculating. A guarantee or cash held elsewhere can add a second recovery route, but cannot generally make a creditor recover more than its total allowed claim in the simple case. Apply previous payouts when computing the amount left outstanding and track which entity supplied each euro. What is being quoted as recovery? Recovery rate equals proceeds actually distributed to a class divided by its allowed face claim. A bond trading at 40 cents on the euro is a purchase price. If ultimate recovery is 60 cents, the buyer’s gross return on price is different from the 60% recovery rate on face. Time matters when comparing alternatives. A nominal 70% recovery after several years may be economically worse than 65% today. Keep a nominal waterfall and then discount dated payouts separately. Ranks and legal remedies are jurisdiction-specific. The teaching case supplies its rules. Run and check the waterfall A secured shortfall competes with trade claims

title: Debt overhang and new finance
detail: S04 · Lesson 8 · Corporate Distress and Restructuring
terms: A positive-value investment may benefit old creditors more than the investor funding it. Compare ways of sharing the incremental surplus. A good project can go unfunded Imagine old creditors are already entitled to virtually every euro the current business is likely to earn. Shareholders might be asked to supply fresh cash for a project whose proceeds initially fill the old creditors’ shortfall. A positive gain for the business as a whole may leave the party paying for it worse off. This is debt overhang, a conflict over who captures incremental value. Calculate payoffs with and without the project for old lenders, owners and the new financier. Subtract the new contribution from the appropriate party. Simply calculating the project’s total return misses the incentive problem. Separate project value from its financing terms A project costing €3m and producing €5m extra cash creates €2m surplus on a same-date or otherwise comparable basis. Paying the old creditors first can transfer part or all of the €5m to them. A change in priority, debt write-down or agreement to share incremental proceeds may enable financing. New senior financing can itself harm old secured creditors if it displaces existing collateral. A viable negotiated deal must leave consenting parties at least as well off as their credible alternative, unless the governing formal rules provide another mechanism. New-money priority is a case assumption, not a universal legal rule. Use the correct baseline Old lenders’ legal face amount is not necessarily their economic outside option. If a €100m claim would recover €55m without the project, a rescue returning €60m might improve their position despite a substantial accounting write-off. Price the realistic no-deal recovery before identifying negotiable surplus. Risk complicates fixed forecasts. If the project fails, who loses the additional contribution and which old assets are pledged? Compare cases as well as expected totals. A debt investor’s limited upside and substantial downside can produce different decisions from those of the shareholders. Identify a feasible rescue contract New equipment behind an old claim

title: Workouts and formal processes
detail: S04 · Lesson 9 · Corporate Distress and Restructuring
terms: Compare maturity extensions, interest concessions, new money and debt-for-equity swaps. Apply the legal rules specified for the case jurisdiction. A restructuring instrument changes a specific promise A maturity extension postpones principal. A rate reduction cuts future interest. A principal haircut lowers the amount owed. A debt-for-equity swap replaces a fixed claim with a residual ownership claim. Write down precisely which cash commitments change and which operating problem remains. Extending debt can solve a short-term maturity wall without making an unprofitable firm viable. Cutting interest can leave an impossible balloon repayment at the new maturity. A sponsor promising new funds must establish the amount, timing, conditions and rights acquired for that money. Why collective action matters Different creditors have different rankings, tax positions, maturity dates and alternatives. A lender may prefer others to grant concessions while insisting on full payment itself. This holdout problem can frustrate an agreement whose total value exceeds liquidation. Identify which signatures or class votes the hypothetical rules require. A formal process may help coordinate claims and impose outcomes under its applicable procedures, but timing, costs, eligibility and protections vary. Compare a negotiated workout and formal alternative under the stipulated case rules rather than assuming the law of one country applies everywhere. Judge both affordability and creditor economics For the company, calculate cash payments it can actually afford after essential operating investment. For the creditor, compare the present value and risk of the new terms with enforceable alternatives. A claim can keep its €10m face amount yet lose value if payment is pushed far into the future without compensation. For equity offered in exchange, value the residual after the revised debt and new-money claims. Applying the creditor’s new ownership percentage directly to operating enterprise value overstates the payout when debt remains. Add the value of any debt retained to the value of shares received. detail: S04 · Lesson 10 · Corporate Distress and Restructuring
terms: Compare each class’s alternative if negotiations fail. Test the valuation assumption that determines whether a junior class receives anything. Negotiating from the alternative Each claimant enters talks with a fallback such as proceeds under liquidation, enforcement or another buyer’s proposal, adjusted for timing, costs and risk. State the legal process and valuation assumptions providing that fallback. A €10m face claim is a legal amount, not necessarily €10m of bargaining power. A feasible rescue creates room for agreement when net value exceeds the participants’ combined alternatives and the agreement can distribute gains acceptably. Total value alone does not determine consent. A senior lender well protected in liquidation may require compensation to take additional business risk. Priority introduces thresholds A junior creditor starts recovering only after higher claims have been paid from its pool. Its payoff therefore changes nonlinearly with available value. In a poor outcome it can receive zero. In a strong outcome it can be paid in full while more upside goes to equity. Apply the waterfall separately for each possible outcome and then calculate expected receipts. Distributing average asset value first usually gives the wrong answer near a priority threshold. A creditor accepting new equity may also prefer risky upside that a senior lender would avoid. Use bargaining ranges transparently A restructuring plan can mix immediate cash, new debt, equity and contingent payments. Compare their values on the same date. When beliefs differ about future performance, a contingent payment can direct some realized upside to the party that expects it, although it introduces verification and enforcement issues. Prepare a sensitivity around the contested drivers. One stakeholder may forecast profit recovery while another expects liquidation losses after delay. Explain how each assumption affects the fallback or proposed value. This makes negotiations about evidence and risk allocation rather than the loudest percentage demand. title: Fund economics
detail: S05 · Lesson 1 · Private Equity, Venture Capital and Leveraged Finance
terms: Distinguish the operating company, the fund and the fund’s investors. Fees, carried interest and the timing of capital calls change investor returns. Follow money from investors to companies Fund investors promise a commitment. A capital call requests part of that commitment for an investment, fees or other permitted uses. Uncalled capital remains an obligation but has not yet been paid into the fund. A portfolio company’s sale price belongs first to the fund, which then allocates the cash under its agreement. General partners or managers operate the fund, while limited partners generally supply much of its capital. A management fee pays for running the fund. Carried interest gives the manager a contractual share of eligible profits. Ownership of a portfolio company and the manager’s right to carry are separate claims. Read the order of distribution A waterfall specifies who receives cash first. A simplified fund may return all contributed capital, then pay a preferred return or hurdle to investors, then share incremental profits. Some agreements include a catch-up paying the manager a larger share over an intermediate range. Never infer those details from a headline carry rate. Fund-wide waterfalls assess all investments together. A deal-by-deal waterfall can pay carry on an early winner before later losses appear, potentially requiring a later repayment under a clawback. Distinguish cash distributed now from the ultimate entitlement under the actual agreement. Why gross returns can look very different A gross deal multiple usually compares investment proceeds with capital placed in the company. A net investor multiple includes cash actually contributed for investment and expenses, and distributions after carry. Timing of capital calls and distributions also changes annualized returns even with the same eventual multiple. An ongoing fund may report remaining asset values. Cash returned divided by paid-in capital measures realized distributions. Adding remaining net asset value estimates total value relative to cash paid in. Report both where a large share of the result still depends on uncertain valuations. Trace a fund waterfall A small fund exits its last asset

detail: S05 · Lesson 2 · Private Equity, Venture Capital and Leveraged Finance
terms: Private markets have limited public information and uncertain exit routes. Connect the screening process to adverse selection and verification costs. Why screening a private company is costly Public prices and audited disclosures may be limited for a young business. Founders know more about their customers, product reliability and financing needs than outside investors. Adverse selection arises before investment when unattractive prospects may be especially willing to sell at a price based on the investor’s average expectations. After funding, incentives can change effort, risk taking or disclosure. This is moral hazard. Screening before a deal and monitoring after it address different problems. A rigorous investment proposal identifies what information genuinely changes the estimate and what behaviour a contract can influence afterward. Separate traction from an attractive investment Screen market demand, ability to deliver, unit economics and ownership of the product. A growing company can still destroy cash if the cost of acquiring and serving each customer exceeds the contribution it will produce over its lifetime. Historical results need a defensible link to future retained customers. Then assess price, terms, future funding and exit. A company with valuable technology can be overpriced if the present investment buys too little of the future proceeds or junior rights with weak protection. A staged cheque can buy time for learning, but can also leave a good project underfunded. Use evidence that can change the decision Start with an inexpensive, discriminating test such as matching a sample of customer contracts to invoices, cash and renewals. Sampling only the founder’s favourite accounts introduces selection bias. Sampling randomly estimates a population more credibly, while deliberately testing unusual cases exposes hidden failure modes. The expected value of an information exercise is the gain from making a better decision after the information arrives, less its cost. An impressive report is worthless to the decision if every possible outcome would lead to exactly the same action and terms. State the decision rule before commissioning it. Design a screening test A pilot can prevent a bad investment

title: Pre- and post-money values
detail: S05 · Lesson 3 · Private Equity, Venture Capital and Leveraged Finance
terms: Separate the value assigned before the new investment from the cash added at closing. Calculate ownership on the agreed share-count basis. What exactly does a valuation describe? A pre-money valuation is the agreed equity value immediately before the new company financing. In a straightforward primary round with identical rights, post-money value equals pre-money value plus new cash paid to the company. These are negotiation terms and implied prices, not a guarantee that the company could be sold for that amount tomorrow. Use the agreed share-count basis. Basic outstanding shares may omit options, warrants or convertible instruments that participate economically. A fully diluted capitalization table includes the securities the agreement says count as if converted or exercised. Changing this base can transfer ownership even when the stated pre-money value is unchanged. A primary purchase differs from a secondary transfer A primary issue creates new company shares and adds cash to the business. A secondary transaction transfers existing shares from an owner to a buyer. It changes who owns the shares but contributes no operating cash. A combined transaction can contain both, and each leg needs a separate calculation. For a simple priced issue, pre-money value divided by the agreed pre-round share count gives the issue price. New primary investment divided by price per share yields new shares. Then add any secondary shares purchased to the buyer’s existing holding and divide by total post-primary shares. Check rights and optional securities Two securities with apparently identical percentages can have different economic value because of preferences or conversion rights. The simple post-money formula establishes headline ownership, while a payout waterfall is needed to value different classes. A preferred price need not imply every existing ordinary share could sell at exactly that price. An option pool reserved before financing can dilute existing holders more than the new investor if the pricing convention includes the reserve in the pre-round denominator. State whether unused options are included and whether a top-up occurs before or after the investor acquires shares. Reconcile a priced round A mixed financing for a medical supplier

title: Preferred rights
detail: S05 · Lesson 4 · Private Equity, Venture Capital and Leveraged Finance
terms: Trace liquidation preferences and conversion rights across possible exits. Two investors with equal headline ownership can have different cash payoffs. A percentage alone cannot price a preference A liquidation preference gives a class a contractual priority when the stated sale or liquidation event occurs. Read the base amount, multiple, seniority and whether dividends count. Under a simple one-times preference a €5m investor may claim the first €5m available, capped by proceeds if less is available. Non-participating preferred typically chooses the better of its preference or conversion to an ordinary share fraction under the assumed terms. A participating class may first take its preference and then share some remaining proceeds. Caps and conversion options can change that calculation again. Use the agreement in the question. Find the conversion threshold With one non-participating preferred class invested amount I, an as-converted ownership fraction f and net exit proceeds V, its simple payout is the larger of min(I,V) and f × V. The two uncapped alternatives match when V = I/f. Above this level the percentage claim is more valuable. Apply the formula to proceeds available after senior debt and transaction costs. If the question gives enterprise value, first convert it to the distributable equity pool. A price stated for all company assets cannot be allocated directly among equity classes while debt remains unpaid. Why the shape of the return matters Preferences protect part of the downside while preserving the option to join the upside. Founders can retain a majority of shares but receive little at a modest sale. These different payoffs can produce disagreement over an early exit, a new risky project or a future financing round. Multiple classes complicate the election because one class’s conversion can change the share fraction and available pool for others. Work through feasible conversion choices and check individual incentives under the stated rules. A shortcut assuming every preferred class converts can fail in a low or medium exit. title: Staging and dilution
detail: S05 · Lesson 5 · Private Equity, Venture Capital and Leveraged Finance
terms: Later rounds can dilute earlier investors while funding activities that increase total company value. Model both effects in a capitalization table. Learning has an economic value Instead of paying the entire development budget now, investors can commit enough to reach a milestone and decide later whether to continue. Staging creates an option to stop funding a weak project after receiving information. The option has value only if the milestone conveys information and the investor can genuinely change course. Staging has costs. A company with too little runway may raise money under pressure, delay a valuable launch or lose bargaining power. Investors and founders can choose milestones that look impressive without measuring durable value. Link the release of money to a verifiable result close to the commercial or technical risk. Track shares and percentages separately A new issue dilutes existing holders’ percentages because total shares rise. An individual’s share count ordinarily stays the same unless that person sells, buys or exercises rights. A reduced fraction can be worth more in euros if the issue adds resources on attractive terms and creates value. A pro-rata participation right allows existing investors to buy a portion of a round to maintain their percentage under the agreement. Maintaining a percentage requires fresh cash and should be assessed as a new investment. The legal ability to participate is different from having the money or wanting the exposure. Understand financing sequence In a down round, the new price per share is below the previous round’s issue price. The changed price can reflect weaker prospects, changed market conditions or bargaining. Anti-dilution rights and convertible instruments can alter existing share counts, so a simple unchanged-count calculation requires those rights to be absent. Prepare a capitalization table for each round rather than multiplying percentages informally. Track founders, early investors, option pools and new financiers in shares and cash. Separately value each owner’s new stake and show the additional cash they supplied to obtain it. Model a staged issue A follow-on round after a successful trial

title: Buyout sources and uses
detail: S05 · Lesson 6 · Private Equity, Venture Capital and Leveraged Finance
terms: Reconcile purchase consideration, fees and refinancing with new debt and sponsor equity. Keep transaction costs and ongoing operating effects distinct. Where the closing cash goes A leveraged buyout combines sponsor equity with borrowing to acquire a business. The sources-and-uses table is a cash settlement for closing. It answers who provides each euro and who receives it. The operating company’s income statement answers a different question about future revenues and costs. If a price is quoted for enterprise value, first convert it to equity consideration using the old debt, available cash and other specified items. If the old debt must be refinanced, paying that lender is a use. Paying both full enterprise value to the seller and full old debt to the lender generally counts the same value twice. Be precise about target cash Target cash can increase the price sellers receive if it is delivered with the company. The same eligible cash may then help fund closing if the transaction permits a cash sweep. These are two sides of a consistent cash bridge. Cash that must remain to fund operations cannot also pay the seller. Fees, taxes and minimum cash requirements often create the balancing sponsor equity need. If the existing loan stays outstanding, show clearly whether it is assumed or refinanced. Counting it as a new funding inflow when no money moves obscures closing liquidity and can distort leverage. Evaluate leverage after the table balances A balancing table proves the cash adds up, not that the borrower can service the new loan. Compare gross and net debt to sustainable operating earnings, interest coverage and the cash left after necessary investment. Use closing balances after any cash sweep and fees. A sponsor may prefer debt because less sponsor equity is initially at risk, but the loan has priority over equity and can force a restructuring in a downside. Ask how marginal changes in fees, available debt or the minimum cash cushion change the required equity cheque. Assemble the transaction settlement An acquisition with a minimum cash floor

title: Debt schedules
detail: S05 · Lesson 7 · Private Equity, Venture Capital and Leveraged Finance
terms: Model interest, mandatory amortization, cash sweeps and covenants. Test whether cash remains adequate before counting a possible distribution. How a borrowing balance changes Loans can require mandatory principal payments, permit voluntary prepayment, or require a sweep of cash remaining after defined uses. Begin with opening principal and follow each drawing and repayment. Cash interest pays for use of funds. It generally does not reduce principal. Payment-in-kind interest, when expressly agreed, adds to principal instead. For an annual teaching model, the interest basis might be opening debt. Real loans may use daily or average balances or floating reference rates plus a spread. Use exactly the convention supplied. Financing scenarios can change both the cash charge and the resulting closing debt. Cash available for a sweep Start with cash the company can actually use after operating needs, taxes, investment and any required buffer. Deduct interest and required amortization in the contractual order. Define the sweep percentage and apply it only to positive eligible excess, subject to remaining principal and any permitted exemptions. A distribution to the sponsor follows loan covenants, contractual restrictions and cash needs. The fact that a model shows a year-end surplus does not mean it is freely distributable. A working-capital peak shortly after year-end can make that apparent surplus necessary for operations. Covenants test specific definitions A leverage covenant may compare defined net debt with agreed earnings. An interest-coverage rule may compare earnings or available cash with interest. The loan agreement can define different add-backs, testing dates and cure rights than an analyst’s default calculation. Display both the economic measure and contractual test if they differ. An incurrence covenant may restrict a new action, whereas a maintenance covenant can require ongoing compliance at specified tests. A forecasted failure can block borrowing, require a waiver or trigger other consequences under the case terms. Do not assume every breach produces immediate liquidation. title: Returns and attribution
detail: S05 · Lesson 8 · Private Equity, Venture Capital and Leveraged Finance
terms: Compare the money multiple with annualized return. Break value creation into operating change, debt reduction, timing and the entry-to-exit multiple change. Three measures answer different questions The money multiple measures how much an investor gets for each unit of capital paid in. It ignores time. An annualized return accounts for how quickly the money was received. With one outflow and one later inflow, the annualized rate is the multiple raised to one divided by holding years, minus one. With several flows, the internal rate of return is the discount rate that sets net present value to zero. An early dividend can raise the internal rate without changing total cash materially. Compare multiples, timing and actual cash value together, particularly when borrowing pays out a dividend before the exit. Trace the increase in company value In a simple buyout model, enterprise value equals operating earnings times an entry or exit multiple. A rise in operating value can come from stronger earnings or from a higher price the market pays per euro of earnings. Separating these mechanisms matters because managers may influence operations more directly than the exit market. The attribution convention must specify where to place the interaction between changing earnings and multiples. One exact bridge first values the earnings change at the entry multiple, then values the multiple change on exit earnings. Another convention can be valid if its contributions sum correctly and are stated. From enterprise value to sponsor cash Equity equals enterprise value less net debt and other senior claims under a simple capital structure. Debt repayment increases the sponsor’s share of a given enterprise value. It is funded by operating cash, asset sales or additional injections. Investigate the source before calling every euro operational success. Add interim distributions and subtract later capital contributions when measuring sponsor cash returns. Avoid adding debt paydown as an extra distribution if exit equity already reflects the lower remaining debt. Fees, outside investors and different share rights can make sponsor cash differ from total equity value. Reconcile return drivers A sponsor exits a components business

title: Exit choices and liquidity
detail: S05 · Lesson 9 · Private Equity, Venture Capital and Leveraged Finance
terms: A sale, public listing or continuation vehicle changes timing, fees and execution risk. Test the return with a delayed exit. An exit price is not always cash A trade buyer can offer cash, shares or a mix. A stock market listing may establish a quoted price while the fund remains unable to sell all its holdings before a lock-up ends or without affecting the price. Separate amount quoted, fraction sold, time of sale and costs paid. A continuation vehicle buys assets from an older fund and lets some investors take cash while others roll into a new fund managed by the same sponsor. That creates a valuation and incentive question because the manager participates on both sides. Independent price evidence and a genuine choice help evaluate terms. Compare cash on the same date A high future sale price can be inferior to a lower certain bid today. Discount the actual amounts available to the investor after fees, debt repayment and any retained exposure. If all of those are already netted, do not subtract them again. Use one discount rate only when the assumptions justify it. An earn-out ties part of consideration to later performance. Expected nominal payment equals the weighted payoffs under plausible outcomes. Discount it to today and assess whether the buyer controls the accounting measure or business decisions used to determine the payment. Collectibility may matter even if the target meets its goal. Liquidity, choice and incentives Selling part of a position can reduce concentration while retaining upside exposure. The unsold part remains at risk, so valuing it at the sale price for a small initial block can be optimistic. Model alternative prices and delays for its eventual sale. Fund maturity can also push a manager toward accepting an immediate exit. Check whether a proposed extension creates real extra value or mainly postpones recognition of losses. title: Evidence and selection
detail: S05 · Lesson 10 · Private Equity, Venture Capital and Leveraged Finance
terms: Compare private and public performance using matched cash-flow dates and benchmarks. Consider survivorship, valuation smoothing and the choice of vintage. Match the dates of private and public investment A private fund calls cash and returns it at irregular dates. A comparison with the full market index over the fund’s life can credit the index with capital before the investor actually supplied it. A dated public-market benchmark buys index units at each capital call and models withdrawals or equivalent value at distribution dates. One common public-market equivalent carries all cash flows to a common date at index returns. Multiply each contribution or distribution by terminal index divided by index on its flow date. Compare the sum of scaled distributions plus terminal net asset value with scaled contributions. A ratio above one means outperformance of this particular cash-flow-matched index comparison. Read realized and unrealized values separately Distributions are cash investors have received. Net asset value estimates remaining holdings after relevant obligations. A fund can appear successful largely because its remaining companies are marked at optimistic private prices. Compute a ratio both with reported remaining value and with plausible discounts where the uncertainty matters. Series of private valuations can move more slowly than traded prices because they are updated on different dates or rely on model estimates. Low measured short-run volatility need not indicate genuinely lower economic risk. Check the valuation dates, methods and proportion backed by recent independent transactions. Selection changes which funds you observe A vintage groups funds beginning in similar periods. Market entry price, financing conditions and exit markets can vary by vintage. Compare compatible strategy, leverage, geography, currency and fee basis. A benchmark with the wrong industry or risk exposure can leave apparent outperformance unrelated to manager skill. Survivorship bias occurs when only funds still operating or voluntarily reporting remain observable. Backfill can arise if a successful manager joins a database and provides earlier good outcomes selectively. Neither a large sample nor a precise average corrects a selection process tied to performance. Construct a transparent comparison A fund still owns an unsold company

title: Cash positions
detail: S06 · Lesson 1 · International Treasury and Trade Finance
terms: Reconcile bank and ledger balances by currency, entity and date. A consolidated balance may include money that cannot be transferred when needed. A balance has an owner, date and currency Treasury needs to know what the paying entity can use before a settlement deadline. A positive amount in a foreign subsidiary’s bank account contributes to consolidated cash but does not pay a head-office supplier until a permitted transfer or conversion reaches the right account. Record the legal owner alongside every balance. Distinguish the date a transaction was entered, booked by the bank and value-dated for available funds or interest. A bank may show a deposit that is still uncleared or a transfer already instructed that has yet to appear. Identify which convention the balance report and the payment deadline use. Reconcile ledger and bank in both directions Start from the bank statement. Deduct issued payments still outstanding and add deposits in transit to reconcile to adjusted book cash when appropriate. On the book side record missing bank charges or interest. Differences explained by a legitimate timing item need tracking until the bank eventually clears them. Reconciliation and availability are different. A deposit in transit can help reconcile an accounting balance while still being unavailable today. A payment already debited by the bank should not be deducted again as an outstanding instruction. Identify who controls each adjustment and its evidence. Translate for reporting without losing the operational view Convert currency balances to one reporting currency for a group overview using explicit exchange quotations. Keep original-currency amounts as well. A group with euro-equivalent net cash can have a dollar payment shortage if FX trading or settlement has passed its cutoff. Cash may be restricted by security pledges, regulatory requirements, customer ownership or agreement. Restrictions are specific facts, not universal rules for a country or currency.
