title: Cash forecasting
detail: S06 · Lesson 2 · International Treasury and Trade Finance
terms: Separate committed payments from uncertain receipts. Track the size and timing of forecast errors to choose an appropriate cash buffer. Forecast what settles, not what is billed An invoice due Monday and an expected bank receipt Monday are different pieces of information. Cash forecasting translates customer payment behavior, committed payroll, taxes and supplier terms into dated settlement estimates. Short horizons need detailed evidence for large items. Longer horizons can use operating drivers where individual payments remain unknown. Categorize flows by certainty and who can change them. Payroll may be fixed. A dividend can sometimes be deferred subject to agreement. A customer receipt may move even after a verbal promise. Build a central forecast and a small set of internally consistent alternatives. Compare amounts and timing of errors Actual minus forecast cash should be traced to components. A €100,000 payment moved from Tuesday to Thursday raises Tuesday cash without improving the week’s total. A permanent customer default reduces the week and future cash. If the forecast treats a timing difference as permanent, the apparent error contaminates later decisions. A repeated tendency to overforecast collections indicates bias. Use average signed error to see direction and average absolute error to see typical size, both calculated at a consistent horizon and sign convention. Positive and negative errors can cancel in a signed mean while leaving substantial uncertainty. Choose liquidity for the bad date A buffer protects the ability to make essential payments if forecast receipts disappoint. Size the buffer or standby credit against plausible shortfalls, taking account of unused line fees and the cost of idle cash. A buffer based only on average ending cash can miss a single large payment concentration. Do not assume that many receipts are independent. A transport disruption, banking holiday or common buyer can delay several at once. Test an explicit joint downside. The needed funding is the gap at the worst date in that scenario, not the sum of every imagined deficit if some reverse. Evaluate a forecast A payment concentration over two days

title: Short-term funding
detail: S06 · Lesson 3 · International Treasury and Trade Finance
terms: Compare overdrafts, revolvers, commercial paper and internal lending. A committed source can carry an explicit fee even when no funds are drawn. Financing the amount and the period actually needed A seasonal importer may need money for sixty days between paying a manufacturer and receiving customer cash. Choosing a funding source requires the amount drawn, time used, rollover risk, fees and currency. A one-year facility rate and a short-term issue discount are not comparable until expressed as cash costs over the same period. An overdraft allows an account to run below zero subject to the bank terms. A revolving line permits repeated drawing and repayment within a limit. Commercial paper is short-term debt sold to investors. Its apparent low rate may rely on issuing replacement paper when old notes mature. Availability has a price A committed line can charge an annual fee on unused capacity in addition to interest on drawn amounts. That fee buys standby access subject to contractual conditions. Uncommitted funding can be cheaper until markets tighten just as the company needs it. Distinguish commitment from unrestricted access under every circumstance. The effective annual cost of a financing can exceed its quoted rate because of up-front fees, discounts or compensating balances. For a simple short-dated borrowing, calculate cash paid for the amount of usable cash actually received. Specify the 360- or 365-day basis and whether an annualized simple comparison or compounding is required. Funding and currency must match Borrowing internally from another entity can save external interest when cash can legally move and both sides are funded in the correct currency. It can also create an internal currency or maturity mismatch. Check the lending entity’s own payment calendar before treating its current balance as permanently available. A foreign-currency loan with lower quoted interest may have a higher home-currency cost if its repayment currency appreciates. Compare fully hedged or clearly specified unhedged costs and the date on which any margin must be provided. Financing strength is the ability to meet payments in the required conditions. Compare funding alternatives A seasonal draw on a revolving line

title: Concentration and netting
detail: S06 · Lesson 4 · International Treasury and Trade Finance
terms: Group cash pooling and net settlement can reduce external funding. Legal-entity restrictions, local rules and settlement timing can limit those benefits. Payments and balances are different Netting offsets amounts counterparties owe one another and settles the remaining obligations. A pooling arrangement mobilizes or offsets cash balances across group entities. The first can reduce transfers and bank charges even when it creates no new cash. The second can reduce external interest by matching one entity’s surplus with another’s deficit. Bilateral netting offsets two counterparties’ eligible obligations. Multilateral netting combines a network of participating entities under agreed rules. Each entity’s net position is its total receivables from the network minus its payables to the network. Positive positions receive cash, negative positions supply it. What makes a settlement eligible? Amounts need compatible settlement dates, currencies or agreed conversion terms and enforceable rules for offset. A disputed invoice, restricted local payment or party outside the arrangement may need separate settlement. Do not offset across legal persons unilaterally merely because the ultimate group owns them. If balances in different currencies are converted into a common settlement currency, specify the FX rate, timing and who bears the interval risk. If two invoices mature days apart, waiting to net can create interim funding, late-payment or counterparty risk. Consider those effects alongside lower transaction fees. How cash pooling can change external cost Physical pooling moves funds, often creating intercompany claims between participants and the pool leader. Notional arrangements can calculate interest on net balances without identical physical transfers if the bank and local arrangements permit. The legal and operational arrangements determine what is accessible in a stress. Measure interest saved by replacing simultaneous expensive borrowing and low-yield deposits, then deduct bank, operational and tax costs supplied in the case. A local currency balance subject to restriction might still earn deposit interest without being usable against another entity’s loan in an emergency. Net a payment cycle Three affiliate invoices

title: Hedging policy
detail: S06 · Lesson 5 · International Treasury and Trade Finance
terms: Identify exposure, risk limit, decision owner and permitted instruments. Assess how much cash a hedge protects under a delay or cancellation. Choose the financial exposure before the instrument A euro exporter with a contractual dollar receivable is effectively long dollars because fewer euros per dollar reduce the cash available for its euro expenses. A dollar payable creates the opposite position. First put receipts and payments due in the same currency and period together to identify any natural offset. Separate committed contracts from forecasts of probable sales. A forward can fix a rate on a definite amount and date but remains binding if the forecast sale disappears. A purchased option can protect an adverse exchange rate while allowing the buyer to decline exercise, at the cost of its premium. Hedging protects a specified objective A firm might want a minimum profit margin on a contract, a cash floor for debt service or less variability in a planning budget. Define which objective matters before selecting a hedge percentage. Maximizing the derivative’s standalone profit is incompatible with evaluating protection over the combined exposure. A natural hedge may already exist if euro costs are insensitive to dollars but purchases and sales in dollars offset each other. Hedging gross dollar receipts without allowing for dollar supplier bills can reverse the sign of the economic exposure. Consider amount, date, currency and settlement conventions together. What can still go wrong? Basis risk means the hedge price or dates do not move exactly with the commercial exposure. Forecast volumes can change, the exchange-rate fixing date can shift, or the company can receive dollars later than the forward’s delivery date. The hedge can be economically sensible while causing interim liquidity needs. A policy assigns authorized instruments, limits, decision owners and a review procedure for changed exposures. Specify how much of committed and forecast flows may be covered and what happens if an order is cancelled. Avoid increasing an unmatched derivative position merely to prevent a previously reported loss. Set an auditable hedge A customer changes its order size

title: Trade payment terms
detail: S06 · Lesson 6 · International Treasury and Trade Finance
terms: Compare advance payment, open account, documentary collection and a letter of credit. Each arrangement assigns financing needs and non-payment risk differently. Goods, documents and money travel separately A sale contract decides when the seller ships, when the buyer pays and which evidence triggers release of documents. Under advance payment the buyer supplies cash before delivery and bears risk that the seller fails to perform. Under open account the seller ships first and finances the buyer until payment. A documentary collection lets banks transmit documents under instructions. Documents against payment requires payment for their release under those terms. Documents against acceptance may release them after a buyer accepts a future payment obligation. In an ordinary collection the collecting bank does not itself promise to cover the buyer’s default. What a bank undertaking changes A documentary letter of credit can substitute an issuing bank’s undertaking against a complying presentation for reliance solely on the importer’s willingness to pay. Its effectiveness depends on the issuing bank, applicable country risk, document compliance, maturity and terms. An advising bank is not automatically adding its own payment promise. These arrangements allocate different risks instead of making them disappear. The obligations concerning goods quality, shipment or insurance under the sale contract remain relevant. Shipment terms allocating transport responsibilities do not by themselves guarantee the customer’s payment or make trade credit risk vanish. Compare terms by expected net proceeds A seller can calculate the funding cost of bridging production and customer payment, bank and insurance fees, possible default loss and the value of any price difference. Keep the exposure base consistent. Funding an entire invoice for ninety days is a stipulated teaching approximation. Actual financing could follow an earlier cost outflow. Expected loss is exposure multiplied by probability of default and the share lost conditional on default, under the simplified assumptions. Risk concentration, timing of recovery and the ability to survive a large loss also matter. A low expected loss is not equivalent to capacity to bear the full downside. Choose a payment structure An exporter negotiates its first delivery

title: Documentary credit
detail: S06 · Lesson 7 · International Treasury and Trade Finance
terms: A bank’s obligation depends on the relevant undertaking and complying documents. Distinguish a document discrepancy from a physical defect in the goods. Four contracts can surround one shipment A documentary credit sits alongside the sale contract, transport arrangements and arrangements between banks and their customers. The seller must understand the specific bank undertaking. An issuing bank promises to honour complying documents under the credit’s terms. A confirming bank adds its own undertaking when it explicitly confirms. An advising bank can authenticate and pass on the credit without itself becoming a guarantor. Identify the applicant, beneficiary, issuing bank, confirming bank if any, the amount, required documents, presentation place, expiry and payment timing. A credit payable at a future date does not create cash at sight. Compliance concerns the documents The bank examines the stipulated presentation against the credit and applicable rules. An invoice, transport document, insurance evidence or inspection certificate may be required. A certificate requirement creates documentary evidence, not a bank inspection of the actual goods. The underlying buyer can retain ordinary contract remedies for defects. Strict calendar and wording conditions can make timely performance difficult. Compare shipment deadline with the latest date documents can be issued, the presentation period after shipment and the expiry. If dates contradict realistic operations, request an amendment before shipment rather than relying on a friendly buyer to waive problems later. What happens when documents differ? A discrepancy may result in refusal or a request for a waiver through the relevant process. Correction can work if the factual record supports it and the corrected document can still be presented in time. Documents must accurately describe events. Changing a true late shipment date on paper would misrepresent performance. A buyer’s willingness to accept the goods does not automatically amend the bank’s undertaking. Confirm whether a valid waiver or amendment has been obtained and from whom. In cash planning, model delayed payment, finance cost and fallback recovery rather than treating an uncertain waiver as cleared cash. title: Receivables and supply-chain finance
detail: S06 · Lesson 8 · International Treasury and Trade Finance
terms: Compare selling invoices, borrowing against them and financing a supplier. Identify who bears customer default and who provides cash. Three ways to raise cash against invoices A supplier can sell a receivable to a factor, borrow against invoices, or participate in a buyer-arranged programme once the buyer approves an invoice. Each structure advances cash earlier but creates different claims. Draw who pays cash today, who pays at maturity, and who bears insolvency, late payment or disputes. In recourse factoring, the seller may have to repay the financier if the buyer fails under stated circumstances. In non-recourse factoring the financier can assume specified credit risks, while the seller can still bear invalid invoices, returns, fraud or contractual disputes. The label alone does not settle every risk or accounting treatment. How early cash is calculated A factor may advance a proportion of face, hold a reserve against adjustments, charge a service fee and charge interest on the advance for the actual period. At collection it can release the reserve after fees. A reserve is not automatically a permanent loss. Determine when it becomes cash. A secured borrowing typically leaves the supplier with the receivable and a separate obligation to the bank. A borrowing base applies agreed eligibility and advance fractions to accepted invoices. Concentrated, disputed or old invoices can be excluded, reducing available liquidity even when reported sales are growing. Look through a buyer-led arrangement In supply-chain finance a financier may buy a supplier’s approved invoice and receive repayment from the buyer at an agreed date. The supplier gains earlier money at a discount, often linked to the buyer’s credit standing. The buyer may seek longer terms but must monitor funding concentration and supplier dependence. Consider what happens if the financier withdraws. Suppliers suddenly paid later may demand shorter terms, creating a cash need for the buyer. Accounting or disclosure classification depends on the terms and applicable standards. Assess the economic cash timings before assigning a label in the accounts. title: Liquidity under stress
detail: S06 · Lesson 9 · International Treasury and Trade Finance
terms: A derivatives hedge can create margin calls before a shipment produces cash. Combine collateral, credit lines and operating payments on one timeline. An economic offset need not fund a margin call A commodity exporter can sell futures to stabilize the selling price for inventory. If commodity prices rise, the inventory becomes more valuable and the short futures lose value. The gains and losses can offset economically over the sale horizon, but futures variation margin can require cash well before goods are sold. A margin call is a demand to provide cash or eligible collateral under a derivatives agreement. It can happen even if the hedger is solvent and the underlying commercial transaction remains valuable. A mark-to-market gain on inventory cannot settle the call until it can be financed or sold. Build a combined timeline List unrestricted cash, immediately drawable committed credit, ordinary operating payments, collateral already posted and new margin due on their actual dates. A restricted collateral balance should not also be counted as free cash. A facility can be counted only if available by the margin deadline and acceptable under its conditions. Then model when margin is returned or when the eventual sale result offsets the derivative position. Avoid counting both daily futures settlements and the full final derivative gain or loss again. Keep a cumulative cash ledger and separate the timing question from the ultimate hedged selling price. Stress more than one exposure The same disruption can delay shipment, increase freight costs, change commodity basis and raise margin requirements. Testing one event while assuming all other sources remain available may understate the peak need. Include scenarios where lenders reduce borrowing-base eligibility or a customer postpones payment. Options can limit certain adverse derivative cash paths for a buyer after paying a premium, but cost, liquidity and contract terms differ. Changing the hedge ratio can also change commercial risk. Compare alternatives against both the price-protection objective and the ability to fund interim cash obligations. Measure peak liquidity A grain business before shipment

title: Governance and performance
detail: S06 · Lesson 10 · International Treasury and Trade Finance
terms: Assign dealing, confirmation and payment authority. Evaluate a hedge against its stated objective and the underlying exposure as a whole. Keep dealing authority separate from payment authority Treasury staff can commit large amounts through a small number of trades. Separation of duties divides trade initiation, independent confirmation, settlement approval and reconciliation. If one individual can initiate a trade and redirect its settlement, a wrong amount or unauthorized counterparty change may pass without independent review. Small organizations may have fewer people, but the same exposure can be controlled through separate authorization, bank-side dual release, independent call-back to a known counterparty contact and timely reconciliation. Controls should correspond to actual payment and market risks, not simply the existence of a signed policy. Define performance before trading A treasury team may be asked to protect a budget exchange rate, maintain a liquidity floor, reduce earnings variability or minimize funding cost subject to risk limits. These objectives imply different benchmarks. The quality of a hedge cannot be judged solely by whether the derivative made money in isolation. For a budget comparison, measure underlying converted cash plus derivative settlement less fees against the target for the actual covered exposure. Separate volume or price changes in the commercial business from hedge execution or coverage decisions. An apparently poor result may be attributable to a smaller shipment beyond treasury’s control. Independent confirmation and exception review A back office compares the recorded trade with the counterparty’s independent confirmation, checking amount, direction, currency, dates and settlement instructions. A reconciler matches bank cash with the authorized trade and investigates differences. Independent price verification can reveal an incorrect mark even if the cash has not settled. A policy breach and a financial loss are separate outcomes. A profitable oversized speculative trade can breach authority. A properly authorized hedge can produce a derivative loss while achieving its combined cash target. Report objectives, positions, cash performance, limits, exceptions and responsibility separately. title: Cost behaviour
detail: S07 · Lesson 1 · Management Accounting, Planning and Control
terms: Separate fixed, variable and mixed costs within a stated operating range. A fixed cost can become variable when the business adds capacity. Why the activity measure matters A cost driver is something that causes resource use. The number of parcels can explain packaging consumption while the number of delivery stops explains a driver's hours. Orders, customers and units are different measures even when all three grew last month. Use the same period and activity definition for all observations. If a business outsources long-distance deliveries in one month, distance covered by its own vehicles changes. Comparing total deliveries with its own fuel bill across both months mixes different operations. Estimating a mixed cost Suppose total monthly cost equals a standing charge plus a constant price for every machine-hour. Subtracting costs in two months removes the common standing charge. Divide the difference in cost by the difference in hours to estimate the variable rate. This high–low estimate depends entirely on two observations. Take the highest and lowest activity levels rather than the most expensive and cheapest months. Compare the predicted bills with the remaining observations. A scatterplot can reveal a tariff change or an unusual repair. When another unit needs another shift The relevant range is the activity interval in which a given staffing plan, contract and production method apply. Within that range each extra unit can cost the same amount, while average cost per unit falls as more output shares the standing charge. Beyond the range, an extra supervisor or a second machine can make fixed cost rise in a step. The relevant decision then concerns a block of capacity. Ask how long the extra commitment lasts and how much output can actually use it. Building a defensible cost forecast A laboratory adds a weekend shift

title: Contribution and break-even
detail: S07 · Lesson 2 · Management Accounting, Planning and Control
terms: Contribution is revenue left after variable costs. Compare it with fixed costs and identify how sales mix affects a multiproduct break-even point. From revenue to operating profit Cost–volume–profit analysis writes operating profit as total contribution less fixed costs. Each extra unit adds selling price minus variable cost so long as price, unit variable cost and capacity remain unchanged. Positive contribution is compatible with an operating loss when volume is too low. Break-even solves for zero profit. A target profit changes the numerator to fixed costs plus that target. A contribution margin ratio expresses contribution per euro of sales, which lets a manager convert a profit objective into revenue when the product mix is stable. A mix has its own economics If a business sells basic and premium memberships with different contributions, an observed average embeds how many of each were sold. Replacing premium sales with basic ones reduces profit even if total subscribers and capacity costs are unchanged. Write one representative bundle using the expected mix and compute its contribution. To reach a target with indivisible products, round the bundle count upward. If the mix is flexible, there can be many combinations that reach the same profit. The cushion before losses begin Margin of safety measures the difference between planned sales and break-even sales. Express it in units, money or a fraction of planned sales, and specify which. A narrow cushion makes profits sensitive to even a small forecasting error. Operating leverage describes that sensitivity. At a profitable starting volume, total contribution divided by operating profit approximates the percentage change in profit per percentage change in sales volume under fixed prices, mix and costs. The ratio becomes unstable near zero profit. Tracing a profit target Two plans at a design school

title: Relevant cost and capacity
detail: S07 · Lesson 3 · Management Accounting, Planning and Control
terms: A special order can be attractive when there is spare capacity. If capacity is scarce, include the contribution lost on displaced business. Designing the right comparison A relevant cost is a future cash flow that differs between feasible alternatives. Past research spending is sunk, but an asset already paid for might still fetch a resale price or free a scarce machine-hour. Its original invoice alone cannot determine today's choice. Start by describing what happens if the order is rejected. Unsold materials might expire, be sold, or be used in ordinary production. Each alternative produces a different opportunity cost, even though the inventory appears at a single carrying amount. The bottleneck determines the ranking When one resource limits production, contribution per unit of that resource measures the gain from its next available hour or kilogram. A high contribution per finished item can hide an inefficient user of the bottleneck. Demand limits matter because high-margin work may run out. This ranking solves a simple divisible-product problem with one binding constraint and no setup effects. A second bottleneck, indivisible orders or minimum runs can change which feasible combination is best. Compare whole schedules when the simple rule no longer applies. What can actually be avoided Annual rent allocated to a product may continue after that product disappears. Conversely, a contract cancellation fee, extra quality test or associated repeat purchase may be genuinely incremental. Identify whether removal of an overhead line frees cash, capacity or neither. In a temporary order decision, a lower price can be attractive without being sustainable as a regular list price. Repeated discount orders can crowd out ordinary demand, change customer expectations or require a larger permanent plant. Calculating the reservation price A testing bench at full stretch

title: Allocation and activity costing
detail: S07 · Lesson 4 · Management Accounting, Planning and Control
terms: Allocating overhead by volume can misrepresent products that consume different support activities. Compare product rankings under two allocation bases. Unit, batch and customer-level support A cost hierarchy distinguishes work performed for each unit, each production batch, each product line or the whole facility. Factory cleaning may depend on production days while a regulatory design review can support an entire product regardless of its unit volume. Allocating all support by units implicitly assumes each unit consumes the same resources. High-volume simple products can then subsidize complex short runs. The total company cost is unchanged, but apparent product margins and price decisions can change. Building and interpreting activity rates In activity-based costing, group similar support costs and choose an observable driver for each group. A rate is budgeted pool cost divided by the amount of driver capacity used in the model. Multiply each product's driver usage by that rate. Using practical capacity rather than actual low demand exposes idle capacity. The unassigned cost then has an explanation. Spreading the same capacity bill over unusually few jobs can suggest raising prices just when demand is already weak. A cost assignment and a cash decision An ABC calculation helps identify which customers or products require complex work. It does not establish that allocated resources could be eliminated immediately. Staff may stay on the payroll while learning to support other products. Ask what decision is being made. For a long-run product redesign, reducing setups may avoid an extra team. For a one-off order with existing idle capacity, the incremental setup cash can be far less than its fully assigned cost. title: Operating budgets
detail: S07 · Lesson 5 · Management Accounting, Planning and Control
terms: Translate activity into units, prices, staff and cash. Distinguish a target used for accountability from a forecast used to anticipate outcomes. How the schedules fit together A master budget starts with expected customer demand, then derives production, resource needs and financing. Opening stock and desired ending stock connect adjacent periods. Purchases made just before year-end can fund next year's production, so the final period may require assumptions beyond the forecast horizon. The production equation is sales plus desired closing inventory minus opening inventory. The same structure applies one stage upstream to raw materials, using material consumption in place of sales. Keep units of finished goods separate from kilograms, litres or staff-hours. Cash is a calendar question Sales, production cost and cash collection follow different recognition dates. Credit terms can leave a growing company short of cash even as it reports profit. A cash budget starts with opening cash, adds actual collection schedules and financing, then deducts payments when due. Include opening receivables and payables, payroll and asset purchases. A budgeted depreciation charge reduces accounting profit but does not itself use cash this month. Trace the underlying machinery purchase to the period when suppliers receive payment. Why the target and forecast can differ A target sets a performance ambition while a forecast is management's best current estimate. If missing a target is punished by changing the information reported, managers may build in slack or withhold bad news. A practical budget can show both numbers side by side. Rolling forecasts add a new future period when the latest actuals arrive. They help operations reorder stock or renegotiate funding early. Keep the original approved budget so reviewers can understand what management believed when it authorized spending. From demand to a cash request A furniture maker's busy month

title: Flexible budgets
detail: S07 · Lesson 6 · Management Accounting, Planning and Control
terms: Recalculate the budget at actual activity before analysing performance. This separates an output change from changes in unit cost or selling price. Separating volume from operating performance A static budget answers what managers expected at the planned volume. A flexible budget keeps the original standard prices and resource requirements but substitutes the actual output. The comparison with the static budget quantifies how much spending or profit should change purely because output differs. Comparing actual spending with the flexible budget then asks whether operations performed as anticipated for the output actually delivered. A flexible budget cannot by itself assign fault. A genuine change in input prices and inefficient consumption can both produce the same spending excess. The correct activity to flex For direct materials, the relevant activity is often finished output adjusted for normal yield. For a call centre, different call types can consume different standard minutes. If the mix changes materially, flexing only to total call count gives a distorted performance measure. Fixed costs stay fixed across the relevant range, even though their cost per unit changes. When volume crosses a shift boundary, use the capacity step specified in the original cost plan. A spending variance should not punish an unavoidable capacity addition already built into the standard. When a favourable number hides a problem Spending below the flexed allowance can result from better purchasing, but it may also reflect skipped maintenance or lower product quality. Compare physical outputs, customer outcomes and subsequent rework before calling a favourable expense variance an economic gain. For profit, use a favourable sign when actual profit exceeds the comparison figure. For expenses measured as positive amounts, an excess is unfavourable. title: Variance analysis
detail: S07 · Lesson 7 · Management Accounting, Planning and Control
terms: Reconcile budget and actual performance through price, volume, mix and currency. Specify how interaction effects are allocated so the bridge adds up. From a variance to a causal question Price and quantity variances are a decomposition of an arithmetic difference. They do not establish why prices or quantities changed. The procurement team may have accepted costlier materials that cut waste, while cheap materials can require more labour or create later warranty claims. For input spending, a convenient convention measures the price difference on actual quantity consumed and the usage difference at the standard price. With purchases and usage in different periods, a purchase-price variance measured on purchased quantity must be reconciled through inventory. Material price and usage Standard quantity allowed means the material that actual output should have consumed at normal yield. This is different from the standard input for planned output. Comparing actual consumption to the latter would wrongly assign output growth to factory inefficiency. With expense increases treated as unfavourable, price variance is actual quantity times actual minus standard price. Usage variance is standard price times actual minus allowed quantity. Their sum takes standard allowed cost exactly to actual cost. Volume, mix and currency An exporter's revenue can change because of quantities, local-currency prices, product mix and exchange rates. Build a bridge by replacing one input at a time and stating the order. Interactions are assigned to whichever step changes later. A different order changes the named effects without changing the total difference. For accountability, constant-currency sales at a common rate can be useful alongside actual consolidated revenue. Cash gains on hedges should be shown in the appropriate location so they are not inadvertently counted twice. Reconciling a production variance A pigment supplier changes grade

title: Incentives and responsibility
detail: S07 · Lesson 8 · Management Accounting, Planning and Control
terms: A manager evaluated on an uncontrollable exchange-rate movement may make poor decisions. Consider controllability, short horizons and incentives to game measures. Who holds the decision rights? A cost-centre manager controls inputs, a profit-centre manager usually controls selected revenues and expenses, and an investment-centre manager also controls assets committed. Classifying a unit by its name alone can assign accountability for prices or assets decided centrally. A good measure should reflect decisions the manager can influence without hiding losses borne by the organization. Report both the full economic result and an evaluation adjusted for uncontrollable items. The adjustment needs a rule agreed before results arrive. When a measure becomes a target A principal delegates work to an agent whose effort is hard to observe. Basing pay on an observable result can encourage effort, but it can also shift attention toward the easiest measured task. A sales-volume bonus can encourage deep discounts, long payment terms or risky customer selection. A balanced set of measures should address specific trade-offs rather than simply collecting a longer list. Measure contribution after discounts, track cash collection and monitor subsequent returns. A delayed review or clawback can align rewards with outcomes that arrive later. Transfers between divisions An internal transfer price changes reported divisional margins while cancelling out for the group. A selling division with spare capacity gives up little by transferring internally. A fully occupied division may have to forgo profitable external orders. A negotiated range exists when the supplying unit's incremental cost plus its opportunity cost is no higher than the buying unit's outside alternative. If accounting rules prevent a beneficial deal, review the incentive contract as well as the transfer formula. Evaluating a performance measure Internal components or an external supply?

terms: Compare incremental cash, return on invested capital and economic profit. Positive accounting earnings can coexist with a return below the capital charge. Who provided the capital? Return on invested capital compares after-tax operating profit with the operating capital tied up in the business. It is useful when financing structures differ because the numerator is measured before interest. Compare it with a required return reflecting the risk and financing of those same operating assets. Economic profit is invested capital times the gap between the operating return and its required return. A positive result means that period's operating profit exceeded the capital charge. How ratio targets can reject good work A division returning 20% can decline an additional project earning 15% because it dilutes its average. terms: Build upside and downside cases around operational drivers. Locate the demand, cost or exchange-rate threshold that changes the decision. Operational drivers and their connections A scenario should describe a coherent economic story. Selling fewer units may trigger lower utilization and higher unit costs, but it can also release inventory and delay capacity spending. Forecasting every variable as an independent downward percentage can double-count hardships or miss cash relief. Specify what is held constant in a sensitivity and what moves jointly in a scenario. A short trial or staged lease may preserve the ability to stop after poor demand becomes visible. Compare the cash flows after an actual exercise decision with those of a business forced to continue under every scenario. Do probabilities answer the management question? A probability-weighted forecast averages outcomes and can be informative for repeated decisions. It can conceal a cash shortfall in one outcome that makes continuation impossible. A positive expected profit and an unacceptable chance of violating a funding covenant can therefore coexist. Identify evidence that would change the probabilities, such as binding customer orders. title: Define the exposure
detail: S08 · Lesson 1 · Financial Risk Management and Regulation
terms: Choose a base currency, loss convention, horizon and portfolio perimeter. A daily price loss and an annual credit loss measure different events. What exactly can be lost? An insurer may lose quoted market value, miss a promised repayment or face an immediate cash call. These outcomes can happen at different dates and affect different decisions. Start by stating the question the loss measure must answer for the person responsible. Trading valuation asks what existing positions would be worth at the end of a fixed horizon. Funding analysis asks which payments actually settle. An asset can gain value while creating a cash need if collateral must be posted on a related contract first. Choosing the measurement perimeter Include all positions whose gains and losses legally and economically belong to the chosen portfolio. An offshore subsidiary's cash may be unavailable to meet the parent company's same-day obligations. A guaranteed invoice and an unguaranteed invoice can have different collection risks. Distinguish gross exposure, net directional exposure and settlement exposure. Opposite currency amounts may offset movements in mark-to-market value while leaving the firm dependent on two distinct customers paying on time. Enforceable netting of claims requires checking the parties and contracts. Holding period and convention For a frozen portfolio, use starting positions and revalue them at the endpoint. An actual daily result may also include new trades, fees, interest and realized cash. State whether these components belong to the comparison so an apparent model failure has a defined meaning. Express loss consistently as starting wealth minus ending wealth including cash received under the specified convention. Converting each position to a common currency allows aggregation. title: Value at risk
detail: S08 · Lesson 2 · Financial Risk Management and Regulation
terms: Use a quantile to find a loss threshold at a stated confidence level. Record the estimation window, method and treatment of ties. The meaning of a quantile A daily loss distribution includes ordinary gains, small losses and rare large losses. At confidence c, define VaR as the smallest threshold whose cumulative probability is at least c. This definition remains meaningful when many outcomes repeat, as in a credit portfolio with a substantial chance of zero defaults. VaR does not report the largest possible loss or average loss beyond the threshold. Its value can move abruptly when a small change in scenario weights moves an outcome across the selected probability. Reporting the underlying distribution makes that jump understandable. Three ways to estimate the threshold Historical simulation applies past movements of risk factors to today's holdings, revalues each scenario, then ranks the losses. Parametric methods assume a probability distribution and estimate its parameters. Monte Carlo simulation draws hypothetical risk-factor changes from a model and reprices the holdings. Historical windows can omit a crisis. Normal-distribution approximations can underrepresent asymmetry in option portfolios. More simulated scenarios can reduce numerical sampling noise but cannot repair a wrong dependence model or omitted risk factor. The method is part of the result. Why diversification needs care For approximately normal linear losses, correlations allow partial offsets. But VaR need not reward diversification for every discontinuous loss distribution. A position that rarely defaults can have zero VaR at one threshold, while combining two independent positions can make at least one default sufficiently likely to cross that threshold. Use a confidence level and holding period consistent with the actual decision. Scaling a one-day VaR by the square root of days relies on restrictive assumptions about independent increments, stable volatility and position behaviour. title: Expected shortfall
detail: S08 · Lesson 3 · Financial Risk Management and Regulation
terms: Average outcomes in the worst specified fraction. Two portfolios can have equal value at risk and very different losses beyond that point. Averaging a fixed slice of the distribution Expected shortfall at confidence c is the average loss in the worst 1 − c portion by probability. For continuous distributions this can often be expressed as a conditional tail mean. For discrete distributions a tied observation may straddle the boundary and must be fractionally included. Order from worst down, fill the desired probability mass and divide the weighted loss by that mass. Extreme outcomes receive weights proportional to their probabilities within the tail. A severe but very rare loss can matter materially even when it lies beyond the VaR cutoff. What changes when portfolios combine Expected shortfall on combined positions is generally no larger than the sum of separate expected shortfalls for the same definition and joint distribution with finite losses. Intuitively, the combined portfolio's worst scenarios need not coincide with each standalone position's worst scenarios. The amount of diversification depends on joint outcomes. Estimating each book's losses independently and pairing the worst observations by rank silently imposes a very strong dependence assumption. Use synchronized historical shocks or a justified common scenario model. Uncertainty about the tail At 97.5% confidence, a dataset of 200 equally weighted observations contributes only five full observations to a historical tail estimate. Adding ten years of calm prices can change the weights without introducing examples of the crisis being studied. Check how much one observation influences the answer, how portfolios were revalued in that scenario and whether missing instruments were proxied. A scenario beyond observed history can complement the estimate without pretending its probability is known. Computing a discrete tail mean A cyber outage changes a reserve

A second-order approximation adds one half of gamma times the squared change. Gamma measures how quickly the first sensitivity itself changes as the underlying price moves. Matching total exposure at one parallel shock can leave substantial losses if long-term yields rise while short-term yields fall. title: Stress testing
detail: S08 · Lesson 7 · Financial Risk Management and Regulation
terms: Choose internally coherent shocks and revalue both assets and liabilities. Reverse stress tests ask what would have to happen to breach a specified limit. Historical, hypothetical and reverse tests A historical stress replays a past pattern of risk-factor changes on today's balance sheet. A hypothetical stress constructs a relevant new pattern, such as a drought, inflation shock and currency depreciation. Exposure composition and market depth can make a familiar episode behave differently today. A reverse stress defines failure first and works backward to combinations that produce it. This reveals assumptions that have to fail together, including the ability to refinance or sell assets. It identifies vulnerability without attaching an unsupported probability to the scenario. First and second rounds A first-round effect is the immediate change in value or cash under the shocks. A second-round effect follows from responses, such as other firms selling similar assets or customers withdrawing after losses become visible. Specify the sequence and do not count the same fire-sale loss twice. Test both sides of the balance sheet. A decline in long-term yields can raise the value of an insurer's bond assets but raise its longer-duration liabilities further. A favourable asset movement alone can therefore conceal a deterioration in capital. Can management actually respond? A static balance-sheet assumption holds positions fixed to reveal the initial exposure. A dynamic test includes decisions such as cancelling dividends or raising funds. The two sides of a capital ratio A prudential ratio has a numerator of eligible loss-absorbing resources and a denominator that reflects defined exposures. Regulatory deductions, instrument eligibility and consolidation can make the numerator differ materially from ordinary equity. The applicable jurisdiction and reporting date determine the real definitions. Risk-weighted assets reflect supervisory or approved-model treatment across exposures. A firm can increase its ratio by raising eligible capital, reducing risky assets or changing the composition of exposures. The same reported ratio can conceal very different absolute balance sheets and leverage. How losses feed back into both sides A credit loss reduces earnings and may reduce eligible capital. If credit quality worsens, the risk weights applied to remaining assets may rise at the same time. Computing a loss against the old denominator can overstate the post-stress ratio. Some transactions change the denominator without reducing the entire economic risk. Selling a recognized exposure with a guarantee, for example, may leave a residual obligation. Inspect risk-transfer terms and accounting treatment before interpreting movements in the headline figure. Risk-based and unweighted views A leverage measure compares a defined capital amount with a broadly unweighted exposure measure. It can complement risk-based ratios when model weights are low or uncertain. Large nominal holdings can generate funding and concentration concerns even with low measured risk weights. Buffers and supervisory expectations can affect distributions or intervention before legal insolvency. Do not infer an actual legal minimum from a classroom threshold. title: Trading venues
detail: S09 · Lesson 1 · Market Microstructure, Trading and Settlement
terms: Compare a dealer market, a continuous limit-order book and a call auction. The matching rule changes how orders interact. How parties find one another A dealer can provide immediate execution by buying or selling from its own book, taking inventory risk until it offsets the position. A broker generally seeks a counterparty on the client's behalf. The same institution can act in different capacities in different trades. The distinction concerns who actually takes the other side. In an order-driven market, prices and quantities come from participants' outstanding instructions. In a quote-driven market, dealers communicate terms at which they will transact. A request for quote can be useful for a large bond trade when little firm size is displayed publicly. Continuous and periodic matching A continuous limit-order book processes each incoming order against executable resting interest under its priority rules. Price–time priority first rewards the best price, then the oldest order at that price. A venue using pro-rata allocation instead shares eligible executions according to size. A call auction waits until the designated time and picks a common clearing price under published rules. For each candidate price, matchable volume is the smaller of all eligible buy quantity and all eligible sell quantity. Ties need the exchange's stated tie-break rules. Market design and price discovery Continuous trading gives a prompt way to act when news arrives. A scheduled auction pools buyers and sellers who might otherwise just miss one another. Pooling can be particularly helpful near an opening after substantial overnight news. Venue selection depends on the investor's quantity, urgency, likelihood of a fill and information exposure. A price indication for 100 shares does not establish the cost at which a large institutional order could actually trade. Clearing a simple call A small reopening auction

title: Quotes and depth
detail: S09 · Lesson 2 · Market Microstructure, Trading and Settlement
terms: The bid is the best stated buying price and the offer the best stated selling price. Displayed quantity limits how much trades at either price. Price, quantity and resilience A quote has at least three properties to record, including its price, the quantity available there and the time it was observed. The smallest permitted price change is the tick size. A one-tick spread can be large in percentage terms for a cheap share and tiny for a costly one. Depth measures available quantity at one or more price levels. Resilience describes how quickly quotes replenish after a trade. A market can show substantial size at this instant yet take a long time to recover after that size trades. Comparing spread measures The midpoint is halfway between the best bid and offer. The quoted spread is offer minus bid, often expressed relative to the midpoint. The effective spread measures how far the actual trade price lay from the pretrade midpoint, typically doubling the signed one-way difference for comparability. For a buyer, execution above the midpoint is a cost. For a seller, execution below the midpoint is a cost. Price improvement, hidden liquidity and orders large enough to consume several levels can make the effective spread differ from the displayed spread. When the screen misleads A displayed book is conditional on the orders remaining available. Other traders can take or cancel them first. A routed instruction may encounter a different depth profile by the time it reaches the venue, particularly during announcements. For an intended quantity, compute the volume-weighted average execution price by multiplying each fill by its price. Examine whether the next trade would face depleted liquidity and whether the fee schedule changes the ranking between venues. Reading a two-sided book The same top price with different depth

title: Order choice
detail: S09 · Lesson 3 · Market Microstructure, Trading and Settlement
terms: A market order prioritizes immediate execution. A limit order constrains price but can remain unfilled or execute when the market is moving against it. Limits, queues and execution risk A limit protects a worst acceptable execution price but gives no promise of quantity. On a price–time venue, a buy limit added at an existing bid queues behind earlier interest at that price. Transactions observed at that price may consume earlier orders without reaching the new buyer. An immediately executable buy limit is marketable up to its limit. Its remaining quantity may rest or cancel depending on time-in-force. An immediate-or-cancel instruction takes available eligible quantity now and cancels what remains. A fill-or-kill condition requires the specified whole quantity immediately. Why a passive order might be expensive A resting buy order can save the spread if filled while the underlying value is stable. It is also likely to execute when news makes sellers urgently willing to trade. Its conditional price performance after a fill can therefore look worse than average market performance. Consider both the path where the order executes and the path where prices rise away and it does not. If the investment decision remains in force, a later replacement purchase can be costly. Expected cost includes both outcomes on a comparable share count. Choosing an order around a deadline A fund needing cash by a specific time faces an opportunity cost from missing the sale. A patient fund with a strict valuation ceiling faces a different trade-off. Price protection, deadline and required quantity cannot all be guaranteed by a single order instruction. Venue priority, valid price increments, fees and the possibility of a market halt also matter. A stop order activated by a price condition may become a market or limit order depending on its terms. A trigger price alone does not guarantee the eventual fill price. Evaluating an order instruction A patient buyer compares two instructions

title: Inventory models
detail: S09 · Lesson 4 · Market Microstructure, Trading and Settlement
terms: Dealers facing accumulated positions may change quotes to attract offsetting trades. The risk and cost of warehousing inventory affect spreads. A dealer's reservation price An unhedged long position gains when price rises and loses when it falls. A risk-averse dealer already holding a large long book may value one additional share less than an otherwise identical dealer with no inventory. Its personal indifference price is called a reservation price. Quoting a lower bid can discourage more selling to it, and a lower offer can attract buyers. Both changes move the quote centre downward. That effect differs from widening the spread around the old midpoint to compensate for uncertainty or inventory holding costs. Time and volatility increase inventory exposure A simple mean–variance approximation subtracts a penalty proportional to inventory squared times price-change variance from expected wealth. The incremental risk of one extra share grows with the inventory already held, volatility and time expected before the position can be offset. A dealer able to hedge with a closely related future can reduce market-direction risk. Basis risk remains if the hedge and inventory move differently. Borrowing, funding limits and the cost of crossing another spread also affect how quickly an inventory correction is worthwhile. What evidence supports an inventory explanation? Compare changes in quote centre with the dealer's recorded positions, while controlling for market-wide price moves and publicly available information. A lower quote immediately after taking inventory may be inventory management or a rational response to information implicit in the sale. If the dealer gradually returns toward its old quote as the position unwinds and other venues do not follow, that is consistent with an inventory motive. It is still evidence about a mechanism, not a conclusive identification from one trade. Reading a quote adjustment Inventory skew with a changing market

title: Adverse-selection models
detail: S09 · Lesson 5 · Market Microstructure, Trading and Settlement
terms: Informed traders can trade against stale quotes. A dealer anticipates losses to informed flow and may require a spread from remaining customers. How a trade changes beliefs In a simple model a share has one of two future values. Some customers know which one. Others trade to meet unrelated cash or portfolio needs. Even when traders' identities are hidden, the direction of an order contains information because informed customers tend to buy before high payouts. Bayes' rule combines the prior chance of a value with the probability of observing a buy at that value. Divide their joint probability by the total chance of a buy. This gives a posterior probability different from the prior even before public news appears. Competitive quotes under asymmetric information A risk-neutral dealer facing competition expects zero average profit on the marginal trade if it quotes the expected value conditional on that trade direction. Its offer reflects what a buy reveals, and its bid reflects what a sale reveals. Liquidity traders may pay part of the spread that compensates for trades with better-informed counterparties. More informed order flow can widen the information component of the spread. Actual quotes also include fees, price ticks, inventory and market power. Limits of a trade-sign explanation A buy can signal favourable fundamental information or one large fund dividing a mechanical index purchase into pieces. Both create patterns in trade signs. Their later price effects can differ depending on how other participants interpret them. A quote update after a trade is evidence that beliefs, inventory or both changed. detail: S09 · Lesson 6 · Market Microstructure, Trading and Settlement
terms: Distinguish temporary liquidity pressure from a lasting change in the market’s information. A trade can move the price through either channel. A trade through time Record the midpoint before an order, its actual execution price and the midpoint after a specified delay. A buy that pays above the old midpoint may simply cross the spread. A later increase in the midpoint is separate from paying that spread. A lasting midpoint move can reflect information inferred from the trade. A temporary move can reflect inventory pressure or depleted depth that disappears as new orders arrive. An unrelated news event during the measurement window complicates either interpretation. Separating effective and realized spread Use a sign of +1 for a buyer-initiated trade and −1 for a seller-initiated trade. Doubled effective spread is twice the signed difference between execution price and pretrade midpoint. Realized spread uses the later midpoint instead, approximating what a liquidity supplier retained over that interval. Twice the signed midpoint change accounts for the difference. Effective spread equals realized spread plus that measured impact by arithmetic. The identity holds even if the economic explanation of the price movement remains uncertain. The benchmark horizon changes the answer A five-second comparison describes a different outcome from a thirty-minute or closing-price comparison. A slower reaction may reflect a series of correlated trades. Longer windows admit more market or issuer news that has little to do with the original order. Study many comparable orders and adjust for common market movements, trade direction, size and volatility. A randomized execution comparison, when feasible and consistent with the client's instructions, can help separate execution-policy effects from the decision to trade when a price move is expected. The paper portfolio benchmark Implementation shortfall asks how much wealth the investor gave up relative to executing the full investment decision at a designated starting price. For a buy, the ideal paper portfolio owns the full desired quantity from that moment, while the actual one may hold fewer shares at different prices. Specify the decision price, arrival price and horizon used to mark unfilled shares. A buyer harmed by a later rise may have positive shortfall even when completed fills match the arrival quote. title: Execution scheduling

terms: Faster execution reduces exposure to later price moves but can increase market impact. Model the trade-off and distinguish a decision benchmark from an execution benchmark. The timing–impact trade-off Trading an entire order now secures exposure immediately but may use expensive depth and reveal demand. Trading slowly leaves part of the intended position unexecuted and exposed to adverse price moves. A schedule can minimize expected cost plus an explicit penalty for uncertainty about the result. Expected impact may increase faster than quantity traded per interval. If impact cost is proportional to the square of each interval's volume, dividing a fixed order across identical intervals lowers the sum of those squared costs. Comparing scheduling rules An equal-time schedule trades equal lots in each time interval. A volume-weighted schedule aims to trade more when expected market volume is high. A participation rule trades a specified fraction of observed activity, so cumulative completion depends on actual market volume. Each requires a completion plan. A quiet session may leave a participation order far behind schedule. A market-wide volume benchmark can be inappropriate for a client with a narrow deadline, an information-sensitive order or a mandate to trade only below a limit. Decision price, arrival price and urgency A portfolio manager worried about an impending announcement may prefer faster execution even at higher expected impact. An expected information advantage that decays with time is another reason to accelerate. Without such information, faster execution still reduces variance by shrinking shares left untraded. A late arrival at the desk is distinct from a slow desk execution schedule. title: Clearing and settlement
detail: S09 · Lesson 9 · Market Microstructure, Trading and Settlement
terms: Match trade terms, collateral and final delivery. Delivery versus payment links securities delivery to payment, addressing a specific settlement risk. From execution to finality Execution agrees price, quantity and counterparties. Confirmation checks that both records describe the same transaction. Clearing establishes obligations and may net offsetting trades. Settlement transfers cash and ownership with the legal finality defined by the system. Each stage can fail for different reasons. A central counterparty interposes itself between clearing members under its rules and manages default exposures through resources such as collateral and default funds. It changes the pattern of exposures. It cannot remove the need for its members to provide resources or meet settlement deadlines. Principal risk and replacement cost If cash and securities settle independently, a party may hand over the full principal while receiving nothing if the other leg fails. Delivery versus payment, or DvP, conditions final securities transfer on final payment and addresses that particular risk. If a trade fails before either leg settles, a rise or fall in the replacement price can still hurt one side. Margins can mitigate this replacement exposure. Cash and securities must still be sourced on time, so liquidity risk survives even under a sound DvP design. Gross versus net obligations Gross settlement processes transactions individually, which can require considerable intraday funding. Netting can reduce the amount of cash or securities that participants have to deliver. Its benefits depend on enforceability, timing and whether the same counterparties or central system support the offsets. Shorter settlement windows can reduce the time that replacement exposure is open but leave less time for reconciliation, foreign exchange and securities lending. A nominally short cycle still creates pressure if payment systems operate in different time zones. Diagnosing a failed trade A payment linked to delivery

title: Conduct and evidence
detail: S09 · Lesson 10 · Market Microstructure, Trading and Settlement
terms: A fair-execution claim needs timestamps, order instructions and market conditions. Separate an unfavourable result from evidence of a flawed process. What a fair comparison can establish A client may care about total cost, likelihood of completing, speed, price protection or discreet handling. Document the client's priority before evaluating a route. A small market order and a confidential block order can have different feasible alternatives at the same timestamp. An unfavourable fill can be consistent with good execution in a moving market. Conversely a favourable outcome can conceal a routing conflict. Review decision quality against the information and alternatives the trader could genuinely access at the time. Reconstructing the alternatives Time synchronization matters because the best quote can change within the reporting delay. A firm quote at sufficient size on a venue open to the client is stronger evidence than an indicative price, a stale screen or an order behind a long queue. Compare all-in amounts. Rebates may benefit the broker or client depending on the contract. A venue with an apparent price advantage can be worse after fees, lower fill probability or additional impact on the rest of the order. title: Project structure
detail: S10 · Lesson 1 · Project, Development and Sustainable Finance
terms: Map the project company, sponsor, contractor, customer and lenders. Identify which cash flow or guarantee supports each party’s claim. Why put one project in its own company? A project company contracts to build and operate a specific asset. Its separate accounts let lenders trace collections, costs and claims without assuming that every unrelated sponsor business will support them. That ring-fencing can improve monitoring but does not eliminate construction or commercial risk. Corporate finance relies broadly on the borrower group's available resources. Limited-recourse project lending instead specifies when, how much and for how long sponsors can be called upon. An explicit completion guarantee can coexist with limited recourse after completion. Contracts transmit the risk Map the engineering and construction contractor, operator, customer, lenders, public authority and insurers. For every key risk, identify both the contract that transfers it and the party's financial ability to perform when it matters. A promise by a thinly capitalized contractor may have little recovery value. Examine interface risks. A constructor may certify mechanical completion while the customer requires a longer performance test before paying. The uncovered period belongs somewhere even when each individual contract appears comprehensive. Claims, priority and step-in rights Senior creditors generally negotiate priority over distributions to equity under the transaction documents. Sponsor funds, subordinated loans and contingency reserves can absorb losses before senior debt, depending on their terms. Do not infer economic priority from the name of an instrument alone. Step-in rights can allow a lender or nominated operator to remedy a project default before the authority terminates a key contract. Their usefulness depends on notice periods, approvals and whether a capable replacement operator exists. Drawing the financing map A small regional data centre

Construction work can be physically finished while the asset is waiting for a performance certificate, a grid connection or a regulator's approval. Revenue may depend on the latest of those events. Draw a timeline from construction start to first collectible operating invoice. Lenders may make a final draw or release sponsor support only after defined completion tests. If the contractor's obligations end earlier than the customer's acceptance conditions, an interface gap leaves responsibility with the project company unless another contract covers it. Draw timing and interest during construction Interest accrues on drawn debt. If capitalized, it increases the loan balance to be serviced later instead of being paid in cash today. Assuming all debt is drawn on day one overstates interest in a staged build. Assuming all draws occur at the end understates it. State draw dates, rate basis, whether interim interest itself bears interest and any unused-commitment fees. Confirm whether the facility limit includes interest and reserves. A delay can breach the debt cap before the project ever earns a euro. Contractual protection is bounded A fixed-price construction contract may transfer specified overrun risks, while variations, force majeure, land delays or changes in law remain outside its price. Delay damages can offset a portion of lost cash but often have a cap and may be disputed or collect late. Distinguish additional cash paid from receipts merely postponed. For lifetime value, a later cash receipt loses present value and may fall outside a fixed concession end date. For near-term funding, a postponed receipt can create a full temporary shortfall. Define the cash entering the waterfall Cash available for debt service, often abbreviated CFADS, is a contractual measure. It generally begins with operating collections after costs, taxes and specified maintenance or investment needs. A change in receivables can make operating profit diverge from cash even when the asset is running normally. Define whether the waterfall begins before or after a reserve movement and whether a receipt is allowed into the debt-service calculation. The same reserve cannot be included both in CFADS and again as separate support without double counting. Seniority and restricted amounts Senior interest and scheduled principal often have priority, followed by reserve replenishment, junior claims and distributions under the stated documents. A debt-service reserve account holds cash for a specified future payment. Its balance can support lenders while being restricted to a particular use. A cash sweep may dedicate a share of surplus to accelerated debt repayment. A distribution lock-up can retain earnings inside the project if a coverage test fails. Triggering a lock-up need not be a payment default. Look up each test separately. Timing changes who can be paid A project may have sufficient annual cash but fail a quarterly payment because seasonal revenue arrives after the due date. Build the waterfall at the contractual testing frequency. Explicitly carry opening cash and reserve balances to the next period. A reserve draw can bridge a temporary gap. terms: Debt service can follow project cash generation subject to a coverage target. A weak individual period can constrain borrowing even with a strong average. Debt sizing as a present-value problem A required debt-service coverage ratio is cash available divided by scheduled principal plus interest over a specified period. Dividing projected CFADS by the target gives the total service each period can support. This is a ceiling on a payment, not an initial principal amount. If the interest rate is fixed and there are no fees, reserve adjustments or final balloon, discount the sequence of allowable service at that rate. Its present value is the largest starting loan supported by exactly that repayment stream under those assumptions. Sculpting interest and principal Begin each period with the outstanding principal. Calculate interest on that balance for the period. Subtract interest from allowable service to find principal repaid, then carry the reduced balance forward. Negative scheduled principal flags capitalization or an infeasible schedule unless explicitly permitted. A lender may require a margin between final loan repayment and contract expiry, called a loan tail. This can create a lower sizing limit than average coverage suggests. A loan-life coverage ratio compares the present value of remaining eligible cash with the remaining debt balance. The weakest period may bind A level-payment loan is designed around constant service and can fail a low-output year even when a sculpted loan fits. A reserve or grace period may shift cash across dates, but their permitted use, funding cost and repayment must be modelled. Stress resource availability, tariffs, operating costs and interest jointly. title: Allocation and guarantees
detail: S10 · Lesson 6 · Project, Development and Sustainable Finance
terms: Allocate a risk to a party able to control or absorb it. A public guarantee changes who bears a loss and may create a contingent fiscal obligation. Allocating control and bearing capacity A risk can be managed by the party best placed to prevent it, observe it, insure it or finance the residual loss. Transferring a large risk to a contractor with little control may produce an expensive bid or a promise the contractor cannot honour. A risk matrix should identify trigger, allocation, mitigation, evidence, limits and residual exposure. Separate events by cause. Delays caused by the contractor, land acquisition or a general disaster can be subject to quite different rights even if all postpone opening. The value and cost of a guarantee A guarantee is a contingent claim. Its expected payout is the sum of each scenario's probability times its contractual payout. A capped minimum-revenue guarantee often pays only on the shortfall below a threshold. Apply the covered fraction and cap to each scenario before averaging. A guarantee's expected payout is distinct from its maximum legal amount, a fair market premium and the cash authorities must have during a severe downturn. Public revenues may fall precisely when several project guarantees become payable together. Incentives and verification Covering all demand losses can weaken incentives to advertise or improve service. Sharing a fraction, including a deductible or requiring independently verified performance preserves some incentive. Overly narrow triggers can instead leave the project unable to raise finance. Two separate counterfactuals Financial additionality asks what financing terms, risk-bearing capacity or private participation change because development finance is supplied. Development additionality asks what outcomes for people or the environment change. Securing a larger loan does not establish that additional households gain a service. A credible baseline specifies what would have happened without the support, including commercially viable alternatives. Investors may already have intended to fund the initiative, while the subsidy improves returns without expanding coverage. Evidence matters more than the transaction's label. First-loss capital and risk sharing A first-loss tranche absorbs project losses before a senior tranche, up to its stated size. This can change the private lender's expected losses even when total project risk is unchanged. The public investor's commitment and its expected loss are different quantities. Use minimal concessionality as a design question. Compare competitively obtained commercial terms, test a smaller guarantee or longer maturity, and explain why the proposed support changes a binding constraint. Assess whether it may crowd out another lender or nearby investment. Measuring additional outcomes Ratios of total private commitments to public funds are useful descriptions but are sensitive to what is counted. Attribute only mobilized financing plausibly linked to support and disclose whether amounts are committed, drawn or refinanced. Two institutions must not each claim the same entire financing contribution. Select outcomes with a baseline, timeframe, observed users and a mechanism connecting finance to results. A still broader public-sector view can include certain public corporations. A debt claim can be outside one perimeter and inside another without its underlying contract changing. Classification is about the institutional units and definition in the dataset. Ownership or a government guarantee alone does not automatically identify how a borrowing is recorded. Reconcile borrower, guarantor and current legal obligation before adding an exposure to a headline stock. Consolidation and valuation Combining units requires removing reciprocal holdings among them. If a public pension fund holds a central-government bond, one covered unit's liability is another's asset. It remains relevant to the individual units but cancels as an internal claim in a consolidated debt-to-outsiders measure. Face value, market value and amounts payable at maturity can differ after market yields move. Compare values on the same basis. Net debt further deducts specified financial assets. An illiquid equity holding is distinct from immediately available cash and may not qualify under a chosen definition. Guarantees and stock–flow adjustments A contingent guarantee depends on a future trigger. The guaranteed face amount, expected payout, maximum payout and actual borrowing incurred after a trigger are separate quantities. Report potentially material guarantees alongside recorded debt when they are outside its definition. A rise in debt beyond the deficit can reflect currency revaluation, financial asset purchases, recognition of old obligations or a newly consolidated enterprise. These stock–flow adjustments can be economically significant without representing current primary spending. Reconciling a public-sector figure A pension fund holds state bonds
