In the constant-parameter Vasicek model dr = κ(θ − r)dt + σdW, κ > 0 controls how quickly the drift pulls r toward θ. The local shock size σ is independent of r in this model. Taking conditional expectations leads to m′(h) = κ[θ − m(h)], with m(0) = r₀. Separation or an integrating factor gives m(h) = θ + (r₀ − θ)exp(−κh). A deviation’s expected half-life is ln(2)/κ in the model’s time unit. Separate the pricing curve from an expected rate A zero-coupon price is an expectation under the relevant pricing measure of exp(−∫rₛds). In general it differs from exp(−∫E[rₛ]ds) because the exponential is nonlinear. Discounting at the future mean short rate misses the dispersion of its accumulated path. Parameters estimated from historical movements describe a physical measure. Risk-neutral parameters value traded interest-rate claims and can embed term risk premiums. A model can fit today’s bond prices yet imply unrealistic empirical forecasts. Assess model trade-offs Gaussian short rates permit negative values and give tractable calculations. terms: Infer volatility from prices and inspect skew, maturity effects and fit errors. A model can fit a calibration sample and hedge poorly on later dates. Invert an option quote For a plain European option under a chosen pricing formula, implied volatility is the value σ that makes model price match a quote with other inputs fixed. If the price is outside relevant no-arbitrage bounds or other contract inputs are wrong, inversion may fail or produce misleading outputs. The sensitivity of price to volatility is vega. Near zero vega, a small price discrepancy can imply an unstable volatility estimate. Fit a surface, choose a loss Options across strikes and maturities reveal a surface rather than one number. Calibration selects parameters to minimize weighted discrepancies between model and observed quotes. A price-error fit emphasizes large monetary errors, while volatility-error or spread-scaled fitting weights different instruments differently. Raw midquotes may violate no-arbitrage relations due to stale or mismatched observations. Inspect bid–ask spreads, timestamps, put–call parity and strike shape before attributing every pattern to a volatility model. Interpolation between quotes should respect relevant economic restrictions. Separate fitting from prediction A calibrated surface describes prices observed now. Its movement after changes in the underlying affects hedge results. Models that fit today’s quotes equally well can predict different movements in the surface and different sensitivities. Use out-of-sample strikes, later dates and realistic rehedging to examine those implications. Record parameter bounds, objective weights and optimizer start points. title: Greeks and hedge error

terms: Compare analytic, bump-and-revalue and simulated sensitivities. Balance finite-bump bias against numerical noise and assess discrete rebalancing error. Estimate local slopes and curvature Delta is the derivative of value with respect to the underlying input. Gamma is the second derivative. For a smooth price function, centered delta uses [V(S+h) − V(S−h)]/(2h). Centered gamma uses [V(S+h) − 2V(S) + V(S−h)]/h². Taylor expansions explain the cancellation. The even powers cancel in the delta numerator and the constant and odd powers cancel for gamma. Under sufficient smoothness, both centered formulas usually have leading truncation error proportional to h². Balance numerical error sources Making h smaller reduces truncation error but can amplify roundoff or simulation noise. Some payoffs have kinks or discontinuities and a finite bump crosses a boundary. A sensitivity may then be unstable or have a different interpretation. What a delta hedge leaves behind For a small move ΔS, an option has approximate change ΔΔS + ½Γ(ΔS)², plus effects of time, volatility and other inputs. Offsetting its delta with stock removes the linear stock contribution locally. The squared term remains between hedge rebalances. If a desk is short convexity, either direction of a sufficiently large move can hurt a delta-neutral position, all else equal. terms: Separate information available at decision time from the outcome to predict. Track filing release dates, revisions and the delay before a trade can execute. A quarterly balance sheet belongs to a quarter end for accounting purposes but becomes a usable signal only when published and available to the strategy. terms: Penalizing coefficient size can reduce estimation noise. Select the penalty using training data and keep the final test separate. Why shrink coefficients When predictors such as two related valuation ratios move together, an ordinary regression can assign one a large positive slope and the other a large negative slope while fitting historical returns closely. Small changes in data then produce large changes in the separate coefficients and unstable trades. Ridge chooses coefficients to minimize prediction squared-error loss plus λ times their squared magnitude. Increasing λ discourages extreme coefficients. Under this standard convention the intercept is normally left unpenalized after centering. Scaling and the use of sum versus mean loss affect the numerical meaning of λ. Derive ridge in one dimension For centered x and y, minimize Σ(yᵢ − bxᵢ)² + λb². Differentiating gives −2Σxᵢyᵢ + 2bΣxᵢ² + 2λb = 0. Thus b = Σxᵢyᵢ/(Σxᵢ² + λ). For λ > 0 the estimate is a fraction of the unpenalized slope. Lasso replaces b² by |b|. The kink at zero can make a coefficient exactly zero when the fit improvement from including it is too small. Correlated features can receive unstable individual selections even when a penalized model’s overall predictions are stable. Tune on future-like data The penalty trades bias against estimation variance. A value minimizing training squared error alone favors little or no regularization, since an unconstrained training fit can only improve that in-sample objective. Use successive time-ordered validation windows to select the penalty for the actual forecasting objective. terms: Trees can capture interactions and thresholds. Compare their additional flexibility with overfitting risk and inspect where predictions are unstable. A tree partitions the observations A regression tree repeatedly divides observations by conditions such as “leverage exceeds three times operating profit.” At a terminal leaf the squared-error-optimal prediction is the average training outcome among observations in that leaf. Different branches can split on different features, creating interactions. For classification the leaf may predict a category or estimated event probability. A tiny leaf containing two defaults and zero nondefaults predicts 100% under the raw frequency rule, yet its uncertainty is large. Minimum leaf-size and validation rules protect against such extremes. Compute a split improvement For a candidate split, calculate squared errors using the unsplit mean and subtract the sum of squared errors using the two child means. A large reduction indicates the threshold divides outcomes in the training set. Growing many potential splits allows a tree to capitalize on chance patterns. A split threshold between observed values may be unstable. If future companies cluster near the chosen boundary, a tiny input change can jump the prediction from one leaf mean to another. Stress values around the boundary and check their economic plausibility. Control flexibility and inspect interactions Limit maximum depth or minimum leaf size, or prune weak branches using a complexity penalty chosen on earlier validation dates. Ensembles can reduce the variance of a single tree. Averaging predictions across trees trained on varied samples is one such approach. It changes interpretability and computational needs. A fitted threshold is predictive under the observed data and training procedure. title: Multiple testing and robustness
detail: Q05 · Lesson 9 · Systematic Investing, Machine Learning and Portfolio Construction
terms: Repeatedly trying signals can select luck. Report the search process, uncertain estimates, regime results and a genuinely untouched period. Selection changes the null question For one specified test, a 5% threshold roughly limits false discoveries of significance under its null and assumptions to 5% across repeated samples. A researcher who publishes the strongest result from many attempted signals asks a different question about the maximum statistic. For m independent null tests with individual false-positive probability α, probability of at least one false positive is 1 − (1 − α)ᵐ. Dependence changes the exact probability. Shared data, similar signals and repeated parameter choices can make independence implausible. Control or disclose the search The Bonferroni procedure controls the probability of any false rejection by testing each of m hypotheses at α/m. The union bound gives an overall false-rejection probability no greater than the sum of individual probabilities, without requiring independence. This comes at a power cost. A different aim is controlling the expected proportion of false discoveries among selected results. The suitable procedure depends on the decision and dependence assumptions. Neither adjustment fixes lookahead data, impossible trades or a badly specified return benchmark. Stress economically meaningful alternatives Track the full number of searches, including window lengths, rebalancing dates, universe choices and sign reversals. Re-run a frozen rule across markets, periods and input definitions for which the mechanism should apply. Report failing settings alongside successful ones. Keep a genuinely untouched time period for the final assessment. Once its results influence any choices, it is development data. Robustness checks can illuminate which conditions matter. title: Attribution and reproducibility
detail: Q05 · Lesson 10 · Systematic Investing, Machine Learning and Portfolio Construction
terms: Explain performance using factor exposures and actual trades. Rebuild results from dated inputs and state the conditions under which the strategy would be suspended. Explain active return with exposures and positions Attribution decomposes portfolio outcomes using a declared comparison. In a linear factor description, active return equals active factor exposure multiplied by realized factor returns, summed across factors, plus a residual. Active means the difference between the portfolio and the chosen benchmark. Factor definitions, currency, horizon and gross-versus-net convention must line up. A return residual can arise from omitted factors, estimation error, security selection, nonlinear payoffs or accounting differences. Calling it skill requires additional evidence about persistence, costs and alternatives. Reconcile holdings and trades first For a period without external capital flows, ending wealth equals beginning wealth plus investment profit and loss net of charges. Position-level price changes, income, currency translation and trade-related cash movements should reconcile to the published total. A dimensionally correct factor regression does not repair a missing dividend or duplicated trade. Distinguish economic active performance from execution effects. Comparing live fills with decision-time reference prices can reveal implementation shortfall. Comparing a gross paper series with a net real portfolio mixes execution, fees and other effects unless each component is documented. Reproduce and govern the decision Archive the exact input vintage, feature transformations, parameter and code versions, universe, calendar and execution assumptions. An audit should reconstruct both successful and rejected trade orders from data available at the time. A random seed alone does not reproduce a revised price feed. Define review triggers in advance, such as withheld critical inputs, breach of position limits, unexplained holdings discrepancies or persistent slippage above tolerance. Separate an operational pause from a hypothesis losing economic support. Each calls for a different investigation. Build an attribution bridge Three contributors to net active return
